title: Kalanj
eyebrow: Anna's people, and the parish nobody has opened
dek: The family this archive's own great-great-grandmother came from — what can be proved about her, what two archives disagreed about, and the parish register that would answer it. The Kalanj genealogy proper is kept in The Blažević Archive; this page is the join, and the evidence on this side of it.
lead: David asked on 29 September 2026 whether Kalanj was a family this site should track and give a page of its own. It was — and building the page found a misreading this archive had carried in fifteen files, and a phrase in the same line of the same entry that no file carried at all. What follows is the evidence on this side of the join, in the order it was read: the baptism, the two things that baptism says which this archive had got wrong or missed, the stone the registers contradict, and eleven photographed graves that suggest a sibling set and cannot yet prove one.
source_kalanj: Ledenice baptismal register, entry 2 of 1864, read from the plate held here at 6×. David's photographs of the Kalanj graves, 29 September 2026. The Blažević Archive's Kalanj page, read 29 September 2026.

sections.lab: Ledenice baptisms, entry 2 of 1864 · «Kljenovica N° 22»
sections.h2: It begins with one line in a Vinodol baptism
paras: «Anna, legitima — **Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ**» — at «**Kljenovica N° 22**». Godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. The register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica. (**doc** — the plate is held here and was read at 6×.)

She married **Josip Defranceschi**, the stonecutter's son who brought this archive's line down from Gračišće to the coast, and she is **generation four of [the direct line](/direct-line/)**. Five children are recorded to the couple. Anton Rudolf's baptism is entry 9 of the Ledenice / Klenovica baptismal register for 1890 (born 20 January, baptised 9 February); four further baptismal entries at Crikvenica name the mother **Ana Kalanj**, and those four entries are the reason the next section but two exists.

Two sentences of that one line turned out to be worth a section each. The first is a place name this archive had been reading wrongly since it first transcribed the entry. The second is four words nobody had transcribed at all.

sections.h2: How this household joins the Defranceschi line

sections.lab: Corrected 29 September 2026 · fifteen files, including the pedigree's own wall note
sections.h2: «Rijenovica» does not exist, and the mistake hid a fact
paras: Until today this archive read that place as «**Rijenovica** house 22» and said so in fifteen files. There is no Rijenovica. The word returns **zero hits** in this archive's Croatian gazetteer. The register says **KLJENOVICA** — the older spelling of **Klenovica** — and [the Blažević Archive](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/) has read it correctly all along.

What the misreading concealed is the part worth keeping. This site's [Crikvenica page](/crikvenica-house/) already said: «House 22 is somewhere in this line of roofs — **Anton Rudolf Defranceski was born in it on 20 January 1890**.» **Anna was born in the same house twenty-six years earlier.** The archive held «house 22» at both ends of the same family and never joined them, because at one end the village had the wrong name.
The correction is recorded on [corrections](/corrections/), and `check-propagation.py` now holds every file that asserted the old reading.

sections.lab: «Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» · four words later in the same line
sections.h2: And the same entry says where they came from, which no file of this archive carried
paras: **Country people of the parish of Brinje.** Not one file of this archive carried that phrase, and it is the most important thing in the entry: **the Kalanj were not coastal people.** Brinje is inland, up behind the Velebit gap; they had come down to Klenovica on the shore.

**And the Blažević Archive has since walked through that door.** It called Brinje «the single largest hole in this family» when not one page had been opened. **That is no longer true.** Its own session located the films on 15 September and has been reading the marriage book of 1888–1899 through today, 29 September — and has found **Kalanj men actually resident in the village**: Niko, of Brinje house 231, son of Juro; Mijo, of house 249, born about 1838; and Mate as a witness. Also a **Perković** as a bride, and seven Borić men across four Brinje hamlets. *None of them is yet tied to Anna's household, and this archive does not tie them.* [The family and the findings are kept there.](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/)

sections.lab: The register against the stone
sections.h2: The oldest open question in this archive is a Kalanj question
paras: The registers name **ANA KALANJ** in all four Crikvenica baptismal entries of her children. The family's own genealogy gives Josip a wife **ANA GRUBIŠIĆ**, 19 September 1863 – 28 May 1936, and that is the name cut on the Crikvenica gravestone.

**The registers govern here and the stone is unexplained.** And the stone no longer exists: the plot was sold to the neighbour of the family house and the monument taken apart, so [the photograph of it](/crikvenica-house/) is now the only record there will ever be.

This is why Anna's page carries **no death date**. The only date on offer belongs to a name this archive cannot yet reconcile with hers, and borrowing it would be the kind of quiet join that the Rijenovica correction above exists to punish. (**open**)

sections.lab: Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica · photographed 29 September 2026
sections.h2: Eleven stones, and a sibling set taking shape
paras: Eleven Kalanj monuments have been photographed in the three cemeteries and are held here as plates. Which of the three each stone stands in is not distinguished in the photographs and is not guessed.

subs.h3: Four of them cluster around Anna's own generation
paras: **LUKA KALANJ 1859–1944** and **KATA 1860–1942** on a ledger slab; and **ROZALIJA KALANJ 1865–1943**, whose first digit is damaged and was read at 5×. Anna was born in **1864**.

So there are Kalanj born in **1859, 1860, 1864 and 1865** in one small stretch of the Vinodol — and **Rozalija is the name of Anna's own mother**, Rosalia née Perković, which is exactly what a second daughter would be called. A sibling set is the obvious reading: Josip Kalanj and Rosalia's children, with one daughter named for her mother.

subs.h3: It is still a guess, and the test is cheap
paras: **No stone here names a father.** Four birth years in a six-year span, in three small cemeteries of one parish, with a shared given name, is proximity — and this archive has spent the day learning what proximity is worth without a document.

The test is specific and it is the most tractable question on this page: **the Ledenice baptisms of 1855–1870**, where Anna's own entry (number 2 of 1864) already sits, and where her brothers and sisters would sit within a few pages of her. (**open**)

Albert 1895–1945 with five of his household; Petar 1913–1971 and Vera 1917–2011 with the infant Milan 1943–1944; Mate 1928–1992; Franjo 1933–2004; a joint Kalanj–Rebrović stone; Vinko 1901–1961 and Paulina 1904–1984; Josip 1950–1983 with Franjo 1909–1991 and Zora 1923–1999; Tomislav 1935–2006; Judita 1934–2012 with Marijan 1931–2019; and Rozalija's own, with Anton 1897–1977, Marija 1898–1989 and Milan 1927–2006.

subs.h3: One stone carries the šahovnica, and nothing else here does
paras: **OBITELJ KALANJ — MARTIN 1905–1988 and MARTINA 1913–1995.** Two porcelain ovals, a stone cross standing in the gravel above — and propped against the plot, **a pink stone plaque cut with the Croatian chequy shield**.
It is the only national emblem on any stone in this whole set of photographs. It is worth recording as such and **nothing more**: a family put it there, and when or why is not on the stone.

subs.h3: Two photographs could not be stored
paras: They reached this archive inline rather than as files: **that one**, and **LOVRO 1906–1965** with Ana, Ivan and Marijan. They want re-sending if they are to be kept.

sections.h2: The stones

sections.lab: Four doors, and what is behind each
sections.h2: What is not known, and is worth asking for

asks.q: Are Luka, Kata and Rozalija Anna's brother and sisters?
asks.a: **Ledenice baptisms, 1855–1870.** Anna's own entry is number 2 of 1864 and has been read. Her siblings would sit within a few pages of it, naming the same father. This is the cheapest question on the page and the one that would turn four stones from proximity into a family.

asks.q: Where is Anna's baptism? — answered: on the wrong side of a line drawn in 1949
asks.a:
**The Blažević Archive is reading the Brinje registers now**, image by image, and has found Kalanj households in the village — houses 231, 249 and 118/189. *That is their work and [it is kept there](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/).* **What this archive asked is why none of it reaches Anna, and that now has an answer.**

**A decision of the NRH Ministry of the Interior of 13 May 1949 ordered that every parish register with entries UP TO 1860 be handed to the competent state archive** — while those **from 1860** stayed with the **matični uredi**, the registry offices that needed them for daily work. *(**doc** — Angelika Milić, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga u Hrvatskom državnom arhivu», Arhivski vjesnik 60 (2017), and again in its English abstract.)*

**Anna was born on 3 January 1864. Four years the wrong side of that line.** Her baptism was never going to sit in a state archive's register collection, *because the law that filled those collections stopped at 1860.* **It is not lost. It was left where it was being used.**

**The inventory proves the rule on Brinje's own doorstep.** The collection covers the **Senj-Modruš** diocese — Brinje's own — and its Lika parishes stop exactly where the rule says: **Gospić** runs from 1789 and ends **1858/1859**; **Senj** from 1678 and ends **1858**. *And **Brinje is not in the collection at all** — the word does not appear once in it.*

**So the door is not the film and never was.** *Anna's 1864 entry is with the registry office or the parish at Brinje; Brinje's pre-1860 books are unaccounted for and are either with the **diocesan archive of Gospić-Senj** or did not survive. **Three places to ask, and not one of them is a state archive.*** [The rule, the holdings and the two dead catalogues are in the search log.](/searched/)

asks.q: Who is the Ana Grubišić on the Crikvenica stone?
asks.a: The registers say Josip's wife was Ana Kalanj, four times. The stone said Ana Grubišić, 1863–1936. The stone is destroyed and the photograph is the record. Reconciling the two names is the oldest open question in this archive.
The šahovnica stone (Martin and Martina) and the Lovro 1906–1965 stone arrived inline and could not be stored. They are described here from the images as seen; they are not held.

sections.lab: The boundary between two archives
sections.h2: Where the family itself is kept
paras: The Kalanj genealogy proper — **215 published people, earliest birth 1734**, running through Klenovica and Povile — is kept in [The Blažević Archive](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/), and is not rebuilt here. That boundary is right.

It had one cost, and this page is the answer to it: **while each archive read only its own page, the two of them held one baptism and disagreed about the village for months.** What belongs *here* is the join, the evidence photographed on this side, and the disagreements between the two. What belongs *there* is the family.

sections.lab: Bribir death book, 2 October 1827 · «Kallay…»
sections.h2: A Kallayn of the Ledenice parish, thirty-seven years before Anna
paras: **5 November 2026.** Reading the death book of the Vinodol chapter at Bribir (FamilySearch waypoint 9RKB-JWG, image 503, left page, the last entry on it, house margin «N3»), the page gives: «*Die 2da 8bris 1827 mortua est proles dierum 23 ex convulsionibus Nomine Mathea filia Georgii, Dnae Annae* **Kallay…** *ex Parochia Ledenicensi*», buried in the Bribir cemetery. A baby girl, Mathea, 23 days old, daughter of Georgius and of «Domina Anna Kallay…», of the parish of Ledenice. *doc* for the words as far as they go.

**What is not settled.** The surname is cut by the edge of the page: **Kallay** and a last stroke that reads as an *n* (**Kallayn**), and the entry does not say whether it belongs to the mother alone or to both parents. **Kallayn is one of the forms the Record Atlas files as the same family as Kalanj**, so it is a name this archive must count; it is not shown to be Anna's family. The 1864 entry above puts her father Josephus at Klenovica, of the parish of Brinje, and the Ledenice parish is the book it was written in; **nothing here joins a Georgius and an Anna Kallayn of 1827 to him**, and a family of one name in one parish is not one family until a record says so. Kept as a lead for the Ledenice baptisms 1861–94 (waypoint 9R2H-RM4, one year read) and for any Ledenice book before them. **Answered on 5 November 2026, in the last section below: the baby's baptism stands in the Ledenice book of 1827.**

sections.lab: Ledenice births 1861–1894, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: Anna's brothers and sisters, on the page, and one godfather in 1894
paras: On 5 November 2026 the whole of the Ledenice baptism volume (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2H-RM4, two books, 1861 to 1894) was looked at once, page by page. The household of **Josip Kalanj and Rosalia Perković of house 22** had been listed on 20 September from the index; this is the same set read on the plates, with three corrections. «**Josephus Kalanj, et Rosalia**» appears as the parents of **Martinus** (born 8, baptised 10 November 1861; entry 59, the mother's cell «Rosalia nata Perković, ruricola»; Klenovica 22), **Anna** (1864, as above), **Lucia** (born 24, baptised 26 May 1866; entry 39), **Franciscus** (born 30 September, baptised 4 October 1868; entry 70, written over 67), **Josephus** (born 5, baptised 7 May 1871; entry 39), **Maria** (born 18, baptised 19 March 1874; entry 28) and **Joannes** (born and baptised 18 July 1877; entry 54, the mother's cell «Rozalia Perković», the first letter of the surname unsettled between P and F; a later note «+ 1877 19/7»: he died the next day). (**doc** for each entry; the left pages of the entries of 1861, 1866, 1868, 1871, 1874 and 1877 were looked at by me, the house cells of those years by a reader's zoom.)

**What the page corrects.** The September table gave Martinus as born on 10 November (that is his baptism; he was born on 8 November) and Maria as born on 19 March (born the 18th). The house is «Klenovica» in 1861, «Ledenice N° 22, in Kljenovice» in 1866, «Kljenovica» in 1868, and «**Povile**» (still N° 22) in 1871, 1874 and 1877: the number never changes, the hamlet's name does. **Only 1861, 1864 and 1877 write the maiden name Perković**; the entries of 1866, 1868, 1871 and 1874 say only «Rosalia ruricola», and that they are one couple rests on the two first names and the house number (**inf**).

**What the page does not show.** No child of the couple is baptised in 1865 (the whole year was read), so the Rozalija of the stone, 1865–1943, is not found here as their daughter: either the stone's year is approximate or she is another Kalanj's child. And a **second Josephus Kalanj**, with **Anna Miletić**, has children at the same house number in 1871, 1874, 1876 and 1881; the Josephus born on 19 September 1871 (not the one of 5 May) carries a later note that a baptismal certificate was issued to him on 24 June 1899 «vjenčanja radi». The identification of the Josip Kalanj who married at Crikvenica in January 1899 rests on his parents as that marriage entry names them, not on either baptismal page.

**Anton Rudolf and Marija Stjepanka again, and a godfather.** Entry 9 of 1890 (image 474, page 124) reads «Anton Rudolf, zakoniti, Josip Defranceschi i žena Ana Kalanj rođena», born **20 January** and baptised **9 February** 1890; the date this archive has often given as his baptism is his birth. Entry 83 of 1892 (image 518, page 166) is «Marija Stjepanka», born 8 and baptised 22 December, with a pencil «u Crkvenici» above the name, the father «Josip Defranceschi klesar». **New:** in entry 59 of 1894 (image 548, right page; Margareta, baptised 23 July 1894, Ivan Komadina and Jela Buneta of «Polje u Mjestu kbroj 39») the godparents' cell reads «**Josip de Franceschi klesar i djevojka Marija Komadina kći pok. Jure**». It is probably Anna's husband, in her own parish in 1894; that is **inf**, and no house is given for him. Nothing else of the name stands in any role in the 559 images, and nothing of Kovačina; the terms and what was not read are in the two rows of 5 November on the [searched page](/searched/).

sections.lab: Bakar baptisms 1770–1842, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: A Kallanj at Bakar in 1842: the double l, and a mother
paras: On 5 November 2026 the whole of the Bakar baptism volume of 1770–1842 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R26-HZC, 594 images) was looked at once. Its pages carry one entry in the name, and not from the household of this page: the printed «Liber Baptizatorum in Ecclesia Buccarensi» of 1842, image 580, left page (page 542), the last entry of April, house cell not read: «*Die 20mo Aprilis 1842 natam 16 curr: Mariam filiam illegit: Francisci B…ich & Antoniae n. Kallanj*», the baptiser Matthaeus Zurievich, the godparents Joannes Supancich and Maria Pavletich. The mother's surname was zoomed at level 13 and is **Kallanj**, with a double *l*; the child is an illegitimate daughter, the father is named only as Franciscus and his surname I did not zoom. **doc** for the words.

**What it adds.** It is a form the Record Atlas's catalogue did not hold (it had *Kalanj*, *Kalain* and *Kallayn*): **Kallanj**, a mother's maiden name in a Latin register of Bakar in 1842. It is now in the catalogue as met on a record (added locally; not yet published). It is **not** shown to be Anna's family: Bakar is a coastal town and Klenovica and Ledenice lie inland in the Vinodol, the mother Antonia has no parents named in that entry (a Hreljin baptism of 1851, told below, names her father as Mihovil Kalanj of the parish of Ledenice), and a surname of one spelling in two parishes is not one family until a record says so. Kept as a lead, and as a reason to read the Bakar baptism books after 1842 for the name (the baptisms after April 1842 are not in this volume's readings of the name).

sections.lab: Bakar baptisms 1843–1884, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: A Kalanj wife at Bakar in 1855 and 1857, the Kallanj of 1842 again, and two Kalain godparents in 1876
paras: On 5 November 2026 the whole of the Bakar baptism volume of 1843–1884 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2C-L23, 530 images) was looked at once; this is the book that follows the one in which the Kallanj of 1842 stands (above). It holds the name in **two households** and one set of godparents, each cell zoomed at level 13 on that day. **(1) A finance official's wife.** On **24 December 1855** (image 111, right page, page 198, entry 139) «*Antoniam Natalem filiam legitimam* **Francisci Barić** *c.r. financiae respicientis et Annae* ?**alanj** *jugalium*»: the father is an Imperial-Royal finance supervisor, the baptiser Petrus Car, cooperator; the godfather is an official of the imperial salt office. The ending «-alanj» is clear at the finest zoom; **the loop capital of the mother's surname I read as K or Z and do not settle**, and her first name reads *Anna* where the next entry has *Antonia*. On **25 March 1857** (image 124, left page, page 221, entry 39, at Krasica Inferior) «*Theresiam filiam legit. Francisci Barić pensionati financiae … et Antoniae* **Kalanj** *jugal.*»: the same father, now a finance pensioner, and a mother whose surname begins with a capital K, as the K of «Krasica» above it does; the baptiser is Peruzović. *doc* for both entries. **That the two are one couple is *inf*** (the same father in the same trade, and a Kalanj mother, in two years and one parish).

**It is probably the couple of 1842.** The Bakar book of 1770–1842 (above) has, on 20 April 1842, an illegitimate Maria, «*filiam illegit: Francisci B…ich & Antoniae n. Kallanj*». The father's surname there was not zoomed; the Christian names and the mother's surname agree with the Barić couple of 1855–57, and a Franciscus Barić who has an unmarried child in 1842 and is a finance supervisor in 1855 is a believable man. That the 1842 mother and the 1857 wife are one Antonia Kalanj, and the 1855 «Anna» her name misread or miswritten, is **inf**, and no entry says it. **What it does not do:** it does not connect these Kalanj to Anna's family of Ledenice and Klenovica by any entry. *Corrected 8 November 2026:* this paragraph first said that a finance official's wife was from wherever the service had posted her husband and that her parents were not named; a Hreljin baptism of 13 May 1851 (told below) names a mother Antonia as **a daughter of Mihovil Kalanj of the parish of Ledenice**, married to a Franjo Barić, so the wife of Bakar and Krasica is, by that entry and **inf**, of the Ledenice parish. That she is kin of Anna's family is still not said by any entry.

**(2) Two godparents in 1876.** On **2 January 1876** (image 404, right page, page 528, entry 1 of the year; Stephanus, legitimate son of Martinus Franiskovic and Helena née Pavletic, born on 1 January) the godparents are «**Ivan Kalain** / **Matejka Kalain**» of Višnjevica 52, the baptiser Joannes Bujan, cooperator; a later pencil note in the remarks column reads «umro 1880 4/10», the child's death. The spelling is *Kalain*, the form the Atlas already holds; zoomed at level 13, the two cells are written alike. *doc*. Višnjevica is a hamlet above Bakar; the two are *probably* husband and wife, a Kalain household there in 1876, and **that is *inf***. Nothing ties them to the Kalanj of 1855–57.

**Left open, and not counted:** a godfather «Dom.us Zalanyi / Kalanyi» on 10 January 1864 (image 243, right page, entry 4, zoomed: a loop capital that may be Z or K, then «-alany(i)»); a godmother «Jovana ro. Kalgna» on 22 November 1877 (image 425, right page, page 568, entry 100, zoomed at level 13: a loop capital, then «-algna» with a *g*, not the shape of Kalanj); a father «Celestin Kalnić(?), pomorski kapetan» in a late entry of 22 June 1881 (image 484, left page, not zoomed, read as Kalnić); mothers «rodj. Katnic» in December 1881 and January 1882 (images 487, 489, not zoomed). **Not Kalanj, zoomed or read twice:** Kalnic and Kalinic (godparents, 1856 and 1872), Kaluc, Kalčić / Kalcic (a mother, 1856), Kilvain (a godfather, 1866, read K-i-l-v-a-i-n). Nothing else of the name stands in the 530 images, and nothing under *Kallayn*, *Kalan*, *Calan* or *Calagn*.

sections.lab: Ledenice births, marriages and deaths before 1861, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: Josip and Rosalia are at house 22 by 1858, with a house full of Kalanj, and the baby of Bribir is found
paras: **5 November 2026.** The Ledenice volume that comes before the baptism volume above (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2F-4WP, 510 images) holds three registers of the same parish: baptisms from 1820 to 8 January 1861, marriages from 1826 to 26 November 1865, and deaths from 1824 to 12 October 1865, with a household list (*status animarum*, houses 1–165) between the first two baptism books. Every register image was looked at once, in sixes, by readers who quoted every Kalanj cell in the exact words; **I zoomed three of those cells myself at level 13**, and they are the three below. The surname turns up in all three registers under eleven forms: *Kalanj*, *Kallanj*, *Kalain*, *Kallayn*, *Kallaijn*, *Kallajn*, *Callajn*, *Kalanij*, *Kallanij*, *Kalany*, *Kalay*. In the baptisms alone it stands in about 150 entries (the readers' count), as father, mother, godparent and witness, and the marriage and death books add some forty and some two dozen cells more. **No Defranceschi and no Kovačina stands in any role in any of the three.**

**The household of Anna's parents is on the page three years before Anna.** Entry 8 of 1858 (image 249, right page, page 207; the last entry of the book in the Croatian form): a son, **Toma**, born 12 and baptised 15 February 1858 «u Klenovici ove župe», the father «**Joso Kalain N° 22 u povilah**», the mother «**Rozalia rođjina Perković iz Brinj**» — Rosalia, born a Perković, of Brinje — and the godfather «Dane Kalain i supruga istoga Mande Ostar… u Povilah». The first reader of the page wrote *Pestović*; at level 13 I read the surname as **Perković**, comparing its r and k with the *Ferković* in entry 7, just above it in the same hand (the third letter is the least certain). Entry 63 of 1859 (image 273, left page, page 254): **Andreas**, born 2 and baptised 4 December 1859, «*Josephus Kalay et Rosalia nata Brinje Perković, ruricolae*», house 22 at Klenovica by the reader; a reader had written *Fertović* there, and at level 13 it is **Perković** too. *doc* for both entries. That Toma and Andreas are the older brothers of Martinus (1861) and Anna (1864), and their parents the same Josip and Rosalia, rests on the two first names, the surname Perković, Brinje and the house number (**inf**); no entry says it. The 1864 entry's «Brinjensis Parochiæ» is therefore not new, but the family's arrival at house 22 is moved back at least to the winter of 1857–58, the first year in which the books write a house number at all. **What is not here:** the marriage of Josip and Rosalia. It is not in the Ledenice marriage book, and Rosalia was of the parish of Brinje, whose marriage books are the place to look.

**House 22 is a house of Kalanj, not of one household.** In 1858–60 the number 22, written at Povile or at Klenovica (the number does not change, the hamlet's name does), carries six Kalanj couples on the baptism page: **Josip and Rosalia** (Toma 1858, Andreas 1859); **Dane** (*Domnus vulgo Dane*) **and Magdalena** (Matthaeus, baptised 28 June 1858; Maria, 25–28 February 1860, «caupones in Portoteplo»); **Petrus and Magdalena Butković** (Victoria, 17 March 1859); **Joannes and Josepha Miletić** (twin girls, 2 March 1859); **Nicolaus and Maria Jovanović** (Lucas, 8 April 1859) and **Franciscus and Maria Jovanović of Zagon** (Ursula, 4 November 1859, read by me on the plate). The last two couples share a wife's name and a wife's village; one of the two husbands' first names may be misread, and that is not settled. Two of the couples can be followed back: a **Petar Kallain** and **Mande Butković** marry on 22 November 1857, with Dane Kalany a witness; a **Daniel Kalanj** and **Magdalena Ferković** marry in 1850, and the Fertović the readers wrote for Dane's wife in 1858 and 1860 is probably that Ferković (not zoomed). The deaths are on the same number: a **Johanna**, five months old, of Joannes and Josepha, in July 1859; a **Martha**, wife of Joannes, 61, in March 1861; a **Josephus**, ten months, of Nicolaus and Maria, in May 1862. And in the marriage book a **Martinus Kalanj**, 24, «Kljenovica No 22», marries on 12 November 1865 (the parents' cell crosses the gutter; the reader pairs it as Petrus and Joanna). All *doc* for the words; who is whose brother or cousin is **inf** and not asked of the pages here.

**The Bribir lead of 1827 is answered.** The page above kept the baby Mathea of the Bribir death book (23 days old, 2 October 1827, «filia Georgii, Dnae Annae Kallay…», of the parish of Ledenice) as a lead for the Ledenice books before 1861. Entry 24 of 1827 (image 31, right page, page 60) is her baptism: «*16 Septembris, Vincentius Maricich Parochus Ledenicensis Baptizavit Mathiam Legitimam filiam Georgii & Annæ* **Kallayn** *Jugalium Ledenicensium*», the godparents Vincentius Millosevich and Theresia, wife of Georgius Kerpan (read at level 13; the final stroke of the surname is hooked and I read it as *n*, as at Bribir). *doc* for the words; that the baby of the baptism and the baby of the burial are one child is **inf**, on the parents' names, the parish and the fortnight. It does not make Georgius and Anna Kallayn the grandparents of anyone in this line: the Ledenice marriage book is the next place to ask, and it has two **Kallaijn** brothers marrying two **Padijen** women on the same day, 26 November 1826 (Antonius and Georgius, sons of Michael).

**The rest of the parish, in outline.** The household list gives the surname as «**Callein**» for five houses (150–152, 157, 158; persons born 1752 to 1838, the notes «In Kermpothe», «In Zagon») and as «Callern» (unsettled) for house 159: the Atlas holds *Kalain*, not *Callein*, and nothing ties these houses to Anna's. The baptisms before 1858 carry no house number, so the Kalanj of 1820–57 cannot be placed on the ground. One household is worth a flag: a **Josip Kalanj** with a **Katarina** (the surname read *Merzljak*, *Marzljak* and *Matkaja* by different readers) stands in six baptism cells at Ledenice, from November 1847 to April 1855; whether that Josip is the Josip of Rosalia, widowed and married again, is **not shown**, and **answered on the same day in the last section below: he is probably the Josephus of house 23 who died in 1872, not Rosalia's husband**; the question as it stood was, and no death of a Katarina Kalanj stands among the Ledenice death cells read for 1855–58. **Not read:** the left page of image 277 (1860, entries about 9–13) lies under a pasted certificate and could hold a Kalanj; a loose slip covers entry 9 of 1853 in the marriage book; the readers had no zoom on most cells, so every reading outside the three above is a reading at the supplied resolution. The terms typed, the near-names and the unread cells are in the [searched row](/searched/) of 5 November 2026; the Ledenice deaths of 1866–1902 are next.

sections.lab: Ledenice deaths 1866–1902, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: The baby who lived a day is in the death book, and the other Josip of house 23 is a different man
paras: **5 November 2026.** The Ledenice death books of 1866 to 1902 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R28-7MW, 374 images) hold two registers: the book of 1866–1882 (images 8 to 164, with a tally of 878 deaths on image 165) and the book of 1882–1902 (images 171 to 371, the last written page the entry of December 1902), the two overlapping from January to March 1882. Every register image was looked at once, in sixes, by readers who quoted every Kalanj cell in the exact words; **I zoomed two of those cells myself at level 13**, and they are the two below that carry a point. **No Defranceschi and no Kovačina stands in any role in either book, and no priest called Josephus.** Kalanj stands in about seventy entries (the readers' count, 1866 to January 1902), as the dead child, the dead adult, the husband or the wife, in every year but 1869, 1881, 1883, 1887, 1892 and 1899. The spellings are *Kalanj* nearly always; **in 1890 the scribe writes *Kalani*, twice in one entry** (image 247, left page, entry 70, 14 October 1890: «Marija Kalani seljakinja», her husband «Anton Kalani», house «Zalipnik 120 odnosno Omar 74»; read at level 13, the last letter stops on the line where the same hand's *j* in *seljak* drops below it), and a reader gave the same final *i* to a child of 1891. *Kalani* is added to the Record Atlas catalogue as attested, locally and not yet published.

**Joannes, the baby who lived a day, is in the death book.** The baptism of 18 July 1877 (told above) carries a later note «+ 1877 19/7». Entry 34 of 1877 (image 115, left page) reads, at level 13: «**Joannes**», «**Josephus Kalanj, et Rosalia Per-/Rović parentes**», Povile N° 22, age «1 diei», the date of death written 18 July (the baptism's note says the 19th, one day apart; the buried-on date of 20 July is the reader's). The mother's surname runs across the line; the first syllable is **Per-**, so the first letter is a P and *Pestović* and *Fertović*, which readers wrote for her elsewhere, are out; the second capital is nearer an R than a K in this scribe's hand, and that it is the *Perković* of 1858, 1859, 1861 and 1864 rests on the same Josephus, the same Rosalia and the same house (**inf**). *doc* for the words. **It is the only death entry of 1866–1902 that names Josephus and Rosalia as parents:** none of the older children of the couple (Toma 1858, Andreas 1859, Martinus 1861, Lucia 1866, Franciscus 1868, Josephus 1871, Maria 1874) is a dead child in any Kalanj cell the readers quoted, and neither Josip nor Rosalia is a dead adult there: their own deaths are not in these two books, so they are elsewhere, after 1902, or written in a form the readers did not take for Kalanj. This is a statement about the cells read at the supplied resolution, not a nil for the people.

**The other Josip, with Katarina, is a different man.** The earlier page kept as open a **Josip Kalanj with a Katarina** in six baptism cells of 1847–55, house 23. A **Josephus Kalanj, 54, with a wife Catharina, Povile N° 23, died on 28 September 1872** (image 74, left page, entry 30; the reader took the second vowel for *a* at twofold zoom), five years before the last baby of Josip and Rosalia, so he cannot be Rosalia's husband (**inf**), and he is probably the man of the baptisms of 1847–55; a daughter **Vincentia**, 7, of «Josephus et Catharina», Kljenovica N° 23, died on 12 January 1868 (image 23, left page, entry 8). A widow **Kata Kalanj, 78**, «Pokojni Josip Kalanj cestar» her husband, Klenovica 23, died on 16 March 1897 (image 313, entry 13), and two young adults of house 23 are written «pokojni Joso» and Rata or Kata (Petar, 23, July 1879; Matejka, 23, May 1886); whether any of them belongs to the same pair is **inf**, not asked of the pages.

**House 22 in the death books.** The number that Josip and Rosalia gave in 1858 carries Kalanj deaths in every decade: **Nicolaus and Maria** lose Catharina (10 months, 1867), Rosalia (3, 1867), Antonius (6, 1873), Lucia (4, 1874) and Ana (1½, 1876); **Petrus and Magdalena** lose Antonius (1867), Antonius again (7 months, 1868), Mathaeus (6, 1874), and in December 1877 two more sons; **Daniel** (47, 26 June 1876, wife «Magdalena nata Frkovic», probably the *Ferković* of 1850 above) and, in April 1877, his daughter Anna (12). From 1888 a **Petar Kalanj, «kr. poštar»** (royal postmaster, in 1894 also «obć. načelnik», municipal head) and his wife **Roza** at Klenovica 22 lose Lovre Bogoljub (10 months, 1888), Roza Zorica (16 months, January 1891), Viktor (1 month, 1894), Marijan Frane (1 month, 1896) and Barbara (2 hours, December 1900, the word above the father's name probably *poštar*), and the widow **Ivka Kalanj, 86**, of a Petar, died at 22 on 7 October 1888, with a daughter **Kata**, unmarried, 61, in 1897. Nothing in these entries says that any of these couples is kin of Josip and Rosalia, and none of it is asked of the pages.

**A Kalanj of Klenovica who died at Rijeka.** On an unnumbered row between entries 50 and 51 of 1898 (image 330, left page) stands «**Martin Kalanj, seljak**», 54, born «Klenovica kbroj 23», living at «**Rieka (Fiume)**», wife «Anta Kalanj», died 29 November 1898 and buried in the Rijeka parish cemetery on the 30th; the remark says that the death was entered on a Royal Hungarian civil-registry notice of 14 December 1898, no. 997. That notice is the Rijeka civil death register of November 1898, which is not on this film. *doc* for the words; no link to the Defranceschi line is drawn.

**Not read, and what the counts rest on.** Image 101, right-hand columns, are hidden under a pasted letter from Široka Kula (the left page is legible); image 98 re-photographs the spread of image 97 with a slip lifted, and image 103 duplicates image 102; unnumbered rows stand at the foot of several pages (images 36, 301, 311, 330, 368) and were read as written; a few cells carry later notes (images 182, 184) that were not zoomed. Except the two cells above, every reading is the reader's at the supplied resolution, and the counts of Kalanj entries are theirs. The terms typed, the near-names seen and the unread cells are in the [searched row](/searched/) of 5 November 2026. **The Ledenice books of 1734–1825 (waypoint 9R2F-JW5) were read the same day: see the last section below.**

sections.lab: Ledenice 1734–1825: births, confirmations, marriages and deaths, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: The name is in the parish by 1735, and it changes its spelling with the priest
paras: **5 November 2026.** The oldest Ledenice volume on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2F-JW5, roll 155, 400 images, DGS 391885401) is one bound item of four books of the same parish: **births 1734–1795** (Croatian in Latin letters to 1760, Latin after), a run of **confirmation lists** (1733 to 1781), **marriages 1734–1825** and **deaths 1734–1824** (Croatian to 1760, Latin after), with four contents tables, and from image 354 a second item, **births 1796 to the first two entries of 1820**; the baptisms of 1820 go on in the volume told above (9R2F-4WP, image 7). Every image was looked at once, in sixes, by readers who quoted every Kalanj-type cell in the exact words, and I zoomed three cells myself. **No Defranceschi, no Franceschi and no priest called Josephus stands in any role in any of the four books, in 91 years of register** (the only clergyman with the name is the second given name of Adamus Josephus Mersljak, vicar of Zagon 1787–89, who is not the man, and the lay Josephi are children, fathers and a customs officer). **No Kovačina is settled either**, and two cells that could be mistaken for one are told here rather than hidden: a smeared surname of a one-year-old in a death entry of 1772 (image 329, left page, entry 28), which a reader could not read at 3× and I could not settle at level 13 (it ends *-vina*, it is not *Komadina*, I do not read it as *Kovačina*, and it is **not excluded**), and a faint word in a death entry of 13 April 1775 (image 332, right page, entry 8), which the reader could not settle at 4× and which I read at level 13 as the *Komadina* that stands in every book of the parish. The Kalanj cells are the readers' count, about 280 name-cells (the count is mechanical and good to about ten per cent); every reading below outside those two zooms is a reading at the resolution the reader was given.

**The surname before it is Kalanj.** In the 1734–47 baptisms (images 0–27) no Kalanj-type cell stands at all. The earliest cell in the volume is a burial: a line of **18 July 1735** (image 292, left page; the death book, Croatian, is bound at the back) with an interlinear «Luke kalany», which the reader enlarged at 2×. The first in the baptisms is **21 January 1748** (image 28, right page, entry 1): «sina Marka **Kalianj**(?) imenom Pavlo», the reader's form, which the reader enlarged at 2× and I did not zoom; three cells of **1754–58** write **Kalagnia** (a Marko and a Simun, both «Jurjev», of the people of St Stephen, the old town of Ledenice), and a marriage cell of 1740/41 (image 186, left page, entry 5) has «Marko Kalany» with a witness «Mikom Kalagnom»: my one crop of that page reached the page's head, not that entry, so **the 1740/41 and the 1748 readings stand on the reader's word**. The first plain **Kalanj** is the baptism of 4 May 1760 (image 58, left page, entry 10, «Georgij et Margarite Kalanj») and a marriage of 6 July 1760; the commonest forms of 1760–87 are *Kalanj*, *Kalany* and *Kalanij* (the last with a final *-ij*, in about twenty cells, among them three baptisms of 1762 in one hand), and the confirmations of 1770 and 1781 write the fathers *Kalanij* and *kalanj*. *doc* for the words.

**The spelling follows the pen, not the family.** In May and June 1787 a new parish priest, Caballini, takes over the books, and within a year the surname changes in his hand: *Kalan* (1784–87), then **Kalain** (1787), **Callajn** (1787), **Callain** (1788–90) and, from 1790 to the last entry read in 1816, **Callein** (about ninety cells, with *Kallein* in 1811–12); the *-ayn* spelling of the Bribir death entry of 1827 comes back in 1819–24 under Vincentius Maricich, and stands in the marriage of 21 November 1824 («Petrum **Kallayn** Georgii, et Joannam filiam Danielis Uremovich», image 214, right page, witnesses a Martinus Kallayn and an Antonius Komadina). That the Kalain, Callajn, Callain and Callein of Caballini are the Kalanj of Maricich and of his predecessors is **inf**, from the same couples and the same office written both ways, not from any entry that says it: a **Michael and Lucia (born Komadina)** are *Kalan* and *Kalayn* in 1783 and 1787 and **Callein** in 1790, 1792 and 1795; the **decurio Martinus** (the village headman) is *Kalanj* in 1771–72, *Kalany* in the marriage of 1779 and *Callein* in 1790–93, 1802 and 1807, his wife **Margarita** in 1771–81 (a Margarita, wife of Martinus Kalanj, is buried on 14 August 1781) and **Catharina, born Miletić**, in 1782–88 (a Martinus Kalanj, widower, marries a Catharina on 12 February 1782). The readers do not say that the wife's name changes; I do. A Martinus Callein is buried on 28 March 1815 aged 78 (image 278, right page); the readers do not say he is the decurio. A **Georgius Callein**, aged 78, is buried on 22 April 1812 (image 276, right page, entry 4) and on 17 May the wife of Georgius Callein *junior*, Antonia, aged 50 (entry 5); a Georgius Callein widower marries a Catharina Pajen on 22 November 1812. *doc* for the words; who is whose is **inf** throughout.

**What this does and does not give the Perković house.** Nothing in the four books is tied to the Josip and Rosalia of house 22: the volume stops in 1824 and the first of Rosalia's children is baptised in 1858, and none of the couples of 1819–24 (a Michael and Margarita Kalayn, a Marcus and Antonia, a Joannes *Callain* of 1821) is said by any entry to be a parent of a Josip. No pair named Georgius and Anna stands among the cells the readers quoted, so **the parents of the baby of Bribir (1827) are not found here** and are of the generation after the readers' last entries. What the volume gives is the **age of the name in the parish**: a Kalanj family in the old town of Ledenice by 1735 and several couples at once (the baptisms of 1760–68 alone name a Georgius and Margarita, a Marcus and Catharina, a Simon and Catharina and a Georgius and Anna), nearly a century before the couples of house 22 in 1858. **Bakar and Draga:** no Kalanj is said to be of Bakar, Draga, Fiume or Rijeka in any of the four books. The few mentions of Bakar (*Buccarenses*, 1760–1779: a family living at Zrnovnica and at a mill, a groom of 1773 and a witness of 1776, a young man of 1776 who had been under care at Bakar) are Akaich, Miletić and Bunetta people, not Kalanj, and a six-month-old child «Parochia Tersacensis», of Trsat, is buried at Ledenice on 15 November 1820; the Kallanj of Bakar in 1842 and 1855–57, told above, therefore has **no earlier link here**.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** The marriage book is covered by loose sheets in several places: page 196 (image 246, left) under a sheet numbered 198, the whole upper and middle of the page; image 239, right, under a letter of the Bakar chancery dated 10 August 1787 over almost the whole page; image 240, left, under a laid-on sheet; image 242, right, under a letter of 23 November 1787 over page 193; the upper page 190 on image 243, left, a ghost only; the body of page 199 (image 245, right) under a letter of Senj of 14 November 1790; and pages 191, 192, 197 and 198 are on none of the images of that stretch. The death book of 1801 is under pasted slips (images 263–266: about entries 8–12 of the year, and the first entries to 13 May; the Croatian slip of deaths 1800–1801 is mostly illegible); the births of 1808–09 under two loose slips (images 373 and 374, lower halves); the right-hand edge of image 28's left page (entries 16–21 of 1747–48) is cut off, so a name ending a line there could be lost; the contents table calls the deaths of **1785–87 «fale!»** (missing) though the readers read entries for those years on images 217–221, and the deaths have a gap from 18 August 1794 to 16 January 1795; four entries of 1784 on image 216 are under a card though the second photograph of the same page (image 215) shows them; and the great majority of the early Croatian hand was read at the supplied resolution only, so *Kalagn*, *Kolagn* and *Kalany* are the readers' words, not mine. The terms typed, the near-names seen and these cells are in the [searched row](/searched/) of 5 November 2026; the second copy of the same parish's 1734–1825 books on FamilySearch (waypoint 9RK1-SPP, DGS 391884502, births to 1822) is not opened, and the Brinje marriage books, where Josip and Rosalia are to be looked for, are the next place to ask.

sections.lab: Ledenice marriages 1866–1882 (9R2H-RMQ), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: No Defranceschi, no Kovačina and no priest Josephus in the Ledenice marriage book of 1866–1882; Kalanj in twenty entries, none of them a Rosalia and a Perković, and the book's own yearly tally agrees with the entries the readers found
paras: **9 November 2026.** The marriage book of the parish of Ledenice, **1866–1882** (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2H-RMQ, which the Atlas catalogues as «Marriages 1866–1882»; Croatian State Archives microfilm, **roll 65, item 3**, 63 images, 0–62) was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**: the first entries are on **image 5** and the last on **image 57**. **No Defranceschi-type surname, no Kovačina and no priest called Josephus** stands in any cell that the readers or I could settle (groom, bride, either set of parents, witness, priest, observations), and **Kalanj stands in twenty entries** (below). That is a reader pass and not a walk: the cells named at the end stayed open and none of them is counted.

**A control: the book's own tally.** Image 4 is a leaf in the parish's own hand, «*Sadržaj III. sv. matica vjenčanih od g. 1866–1881*», with the marriages of each year: 1866: 13, 1867: 12, 1868: 10, 1869: 32, 1870: 23, 1871: 16, 1872: 13, 1873: 12, 1874: 9, 1875: 9 (= 149); 1876: 12, 1877: 20, 1878: 11, 1879: 14, 1880: 16, 1881: 9 (= 82); **total 231**. **The last entry number the readers found in each year is the same number, for every one of the sixteen years**, and the numbers run on without a break across every boundary between the readers' six-image chunks (for example 1869 entry 14 on image 17 and entry 15 on image 18; 1877 entry 16 on image 47 and entry 17 on image 48). Entry 1 of 1882 is on image 57, below the tally. That is a check that every entry of the book was put in front of a reader; it is not a check that every name in every cell was read.

**What the book holds.** A printed Latin table, one page per image (left half: number, date, bride and groom with place of origin, domicile, religion, age and status; right half: parents, witnesses, priest, banns, observations), Latin through 1877 and Croatian from the entries of 1878 (image 50 reads «*Godina 18…*» and «*Srpnja 5*»). The priest is Joannes Bapt. (Ivan Krst.) Žanić, parish priest, throughout; Carolus Sekovanić, cooperator, signs some entries of 1876–1877. **Every *Josephus* in the book is a groom, a father or a witness; none is a priest.** Images 0 to 4 are the filming slate (Hrvatski državni arhiv, roll 65, «MATIČNA KNJIGA VJENČANIH 1866–1882, ITEM 3»), a resolution target, the outside cover (label «Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275»), the inside cover with its library card, and the tally leaf above; **5–57 the entries**; 57 carries a note at its foot that the register continues in a new book from 1882; 58 an end card and a slate for the locality; 59 the Zagreb «KRAJ» card, continued on roll 66; 60 an «END OF ROLL» slate, 61 a resolution target, 62 a blank grey frame. **Images 29 and 30 are two exposures of one page** (printed page 25, entries 3–6 of 1871; I put both in front of me), so the entry of 12 February 1871 below is one entry.

**Kalanj in twenty entries (read by readers; the cells I or a reader enlarged are marked).** **1866:** image 5, left, entry 5, 30 September 1866: bride *Catharina Kalanj* (Ledenice No 23, age 24), parents *Josephus et Catharina Kalanj*, groom Elias Tomljanović of Krivi put (enlarged by the reader); image 5, right, entry 2, 21 January 1866: witness *Martinus Kalanj*. **1869:** image 14, right, entry 1, 24 January: witness *Paulus Kalanj*; image 15, left and right, entry 5, 9 May: groom *Josephus Kalanj* (Ledenice No 74, age 19), parents *Antonius et Lucia Kalanj*, bride Magdalena Komadina; image 15, right, entry 4, 28 April: witness *Josephus Kalanj*; image 17, right, entry 14, 21 November: witness *Petrus Kalanj* (name and surname split across a line). **1870:** image 23, left and right, entry 2, 9 October: groom *Josephus Kalanj*, **Povile No 22**, age 29, unmarried, bride Anna Miletić (Povile No 19, age 22); the groom's parents «*Defunctus Petrus et Vidua Joanna Kalanj*»; witnesses Elias Cvitković and Georgius Miletić. **1871:** image 29 = 30, entry 3, 12 February: bride *Lucia Kalanj* (Kljenovica No 22, age 20), parents «*Daniel et Magdalena Kalanj*», groom Nicolaus Butković (Povile / Kljenovica No 13); the bride's first letter is a *K* that looks like an *R* (the same hand writes it so on image 50) and the surname is settled by the mother's cell, which reads clear when enlarged; image 31, right, entry 10, 12 November: witness *Antonius Kalanj*; image 32, right, entry 14, 19 November: witness *Martinus Kalanj, Decurio*. **1872:** image 33, right, entry 1, 31 January: witness *Petrus Kalanj*; image 34, entry 3, 4 February: bride *Anna Kalanj* (Ledenice No 74, age 20), parents «*Antonius, et Lucia Kalanj*», groom Antonius Krpan. **1873:** image 37, entry 7, 19 October: bride *Maria Kalanj* (Kljenovice No 23, age 23), parents «*Def: Josephus et Catharina Kalanj*» (*Def.* is *defunctus*), groom Marinus Miletić. **1876:** image 43, left, entry 3, 3 August: groom *Antonius Kalanj* (Ledenice No 74, a widower), bride Margaritha Miletić (Povile No 28); image 44, left, entry 11, 19 November: bride *Victoria Kalanj* (**Povile No 22**, age 17), groom Franciscus Butković. **1877:** image 45, right, entry 5, 3 August: witness *Josephus Kalanj*; image 46, left, entry 9, 4 November: bride *Maria Magdalena Kalanj* (Povile No 23, age 24), parents «*Mathias et Catharina Kalan[j]*», groom Blasius Romadina, a widower. **1879:** image 50, left and right, entry 2, 5 July (Croatian): bride *Kata Kalanj* (**Povile No 22**, age 22), groom Mile Miletić, bride's parents «*Pave Kalanj i Luca*», witnesses «*Petar Kalanj i Franjo Kalanj pok. Dane*» (the reader enlarged these); entry 3, the same day: bride *Marija Kalanj* (**Povile No 22**, age 22), groom Tome Miletić — **my zoom at level 13 reads the bride «*Marija Kalanj*» clearly**, with the same *K* as in *Kata Kalanj* above it. **1880:** image 55, right, entry 11, 7 November: witness «*mladić Petar Kalanj*» (enlarged four times by the reader: a capital *K* and a final *j* with a long tail).

**What that says, and what it does not.** (1) *Josephus and Catharina Kalanj* of house 23 have a daughter Catharina marrying in 1866 and, on 19 October 1873, a daughter Maria whose father is already *defunctus*; this agrees with, and does not prove, the death book's Josephus of house 23 who died on 28 September 1872 (told above). (2) *Antonius and Lucia Kalanj* of Ledenice No 74 are the parents of the groom Josephus (1869) and the bride Anna (1872); an *Antonius Kalanj* of No 74 is a widower marrying in 1876. (3) **House 22.** The Kalanj of number 22 in this book are at **Povile** (a groom in 1870, brides in 1876 and 1879) and **Kljenovica** (a bride in 1871), not named as Ledenice. **The book names no Rosalia with a Perković, Pestović or Fertović, and no Josip married to one**: the Rosalias the readers noted are a bride Rosalia Komadina (1866), a groom's mother Rosalia (1867) and a bride Rosalia Catharina Buneta, who marries Josephus Svetić of Ledenice No 50 on 16 January 1876. The Josephus Kalanj of Povile No 22 is unmarried at 29 in 1870, and so (inf) is not the Josip who already had children in 1858–59 with Rosalia of house 22; nothing in this book ties him to that family. (4) **A bride whose own cell and parents' cell differ, which I cannot explain:** on image 50, entry 3, the bride is *Marija Kalanj* but her parents' cell reads «*Roko Miletić i Mara. / Ivan Miletić i Cepa*» (the first pair the groom's; I looked at both halves of the page and agree with the reader that the second pair reads *Miletić*). On image 44, entry 11, the bride *Victoria Kalanj*'s parents' cell reads «*Petrus et Magdalena Butković*», the surname written once after the mother; whether the father is a Kalanj by ditto is the reader's inference and is not settled (not enlarged by me). Both brides are counted as Kalanj because that is the surname written in their own cells.

**One cell I enlarged that was not a surname.** Image 15, right, entry 3 (26 April 1869): the bride's parents' cell reads «*Gregorius et Vincentia Stilin | Def: Fran- | ciscus, et vivens Anna Culinović*» at level 13: ***Def.* is *defunctus* and *Franciscus* is the dead father's given name.** It is not a surname and is not counted. *Franciscus* as a given name occurs elsewhere in the book (Temper, Bunetta, Uremović, Butković) and is not counted either.

**Near-names and places, none of them counted.** Kovačić (image 53, entry 5, 16 June 1880: a sergeant, Ivan Kovačić of Švarča, and his parents Nikola Kovačić and Katica née Bračević); Frković (the commonest surname of the book, and not Franceschi); Karlović (Ledenice No 45, 1870), a different name; **Perpić** (image 53, entry 2, 18 January 1880: Ana Perpić of Krivi put, read at 2× as *Perpić*, not Perković); Cvitković, Komadina, Miletić, Butković, Svetić, Buneta and the other ordinary names of the parish. The villages named are Ledenice, Povile, Kljenovica (Klenovica), Krivi put, Krmpote and Švarča. **No Draga, Bakar, Trsat, Hreljin or Kraljevica; Rijeka once:** a witness «*Dionizio Montanari iz Rieke*» (image 54, right, entry 10, 7 November 1880); a place in a cell is a place and nothing more.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** Every cell at crop magnification except the ones enlarged above (by readers: image 5 entry 5, image 50 entries 2 and 3, image 55 entry 11; by me: image 15 entry 3 and image 50 entry 3 at level 13, and a look at the whole of images 29, 30 and 50); a witness cluster on image 7, right, entry 12 (read «Anton … Rois / Jos. Kr…», no letters of a target name); the date of a bishop's dedication on image 4, right (Wenceslaus of Senj, «Septembris 18…», not read). **This is a reader pass over every image and not a walk.** Terms typed to the readers: Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi (and any *De-/Di-* + *Fran-* cell); Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. The Atlas `cover` run exits 0 for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj with exactly these terms.

sections.lab: Kastav deaths 1774–1882 (9R2X-YW5), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: No Defranceschi, no Kovačina and no catalogued Kalanj form in the Kastav death books of 1774–1882, and the priests called Josephus are Kastav's own; the nearest names are Calan, Callay and the Kalac/Kalaž family of Punže, none of them counted
paras: **9 November 2026.** The death books of the parish of **Kastav (Castua)**, **1774–1882** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2X-YW5**, which the Atlas catalogues as «Deaths (Umrli) 1774–1882»; Croatian State Archives microfilm, **roll 52, items 1 and 2**, 565 images, 0–564) were looked at **once, image by image, by readers**: the entries run from **image 8** to **image 557**. **No Defranceschi-type surname, no Kovačina and no Kalanj form from the Atlas catalogue stands in any cell that the readers or I could settle** (the deceased, a father or a husband, a widow, the priest, the margin), and **none of the priests called Josephus is a Defranceschi**. That is a reader pass and not a walk: the cells named at the end stayed open and none of them is counted.

**What the volume holds.** Images 0–5 are filming slates (roll 52, continuing from roll 51; a camera slate of 25 November 1996 titled «MATIČNA KNJIGA UMRLIH 1774–1818, ITEM 1»), a blank grey frame and a resolution target. **Item 1:** image 6 is the cover («Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 209», hand label «Liber Mortuorum … 1774 … 1818»); **image 8 right is page 1, «Matrica, vel Consignatio Mortuorum Anno 1774 In Mense Maji»**, first entry 3 May 1774; the item runs to image 187 (one entry of 2 February 1819, then a blank page). **Item 2:** images 188–191 are the end-of-item slate, slates for item 2, a target and the cover («Liber Defunctorum 1819–1882, T. III, Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 210»); **page 1 is on image 192 right** (January 1819) and the book runs to image 557 (the last entry, no. 204 of 1882, is 28 December). Images 558–559 are blank printed forms with loose struck-out slips (one with «1873, 1 Jan–19 Apr», a pasted Trieste bookshop circular of 1859); 560 is the end-of-item slate and the item-2 title slate; 561 is «KRAJ», end of roll 52, continued on roll 53; 562 a target; 563 «END OF ROLL»; 564 a blank grey frame. The layout is a ruled Latin table (later a printed «Liber Defunctorum» form): date, house (village and number), the deceased and who they were the child, wife or widow of, age, cause, the priest who buried them. **Entry numbers appear from 2 January 1825 (image 225 right) and restart each January**; from the 1870s the printed form also carries a number that restarts each month beside the running annual number.

**A control: the running numbers.** There is no printed tally of the whole book, so this is a check of continuity and not a count: the last running number the readers found in each year, from 1825, is 1825: 173; 1826: 202; 1827: 187; 1828: 162; 1829: 256 (the printed tally of that year, p. 127, reads 127 men and 129 women); 1830: 359 (printed «mares 175, foemina 184», plus a late row); 1831: 213; 1832: 186; 1833: 166; 1834: 232; 1835: 220; 1836: 208; 1837: 210; 1838: 202; 1839: 216; 1840: 224; 1841: 193; 1842: 198; 1843: about 206 at 31 October; 1844: 225; 1845: 145; 1846: 224; 1847: 216; 1848: 211; 1849: 230; 1850: 198; 1851: 284; 1852: 259; 1853: 214; 1854: 239 at 11 November; 1855: about 552 (the cholera of August and September 1855); 1856: 209; 1857: 191 (104 men, 87 women); 1858: 245; 1859: 305; 1860: 202; 1861: 217; 1862: 251; 1863: 257; 1864: 108; 1865: 170; 1866: 149; 1867: 157; 1868: 148; 1869: 167; 1870: 194; 1871: 215 at 10 December; 1872: 221; 1873: 209; 1874: 188; 1875: about 190 (uncertain by one or two); 1876: 177 at 27 November; 1877: about 170; 1878: 167; 1879: 175; 1880: 160 at 5 December; 1881: 183; 1882: 204. The numbers run on across the readers' chunk boundaries, with a few slips in the book itself (1834 has the numbers 196 and 223/224 twice; the plate of 1875 reads 96 to 130 for 76 to 110 from 29 March, because the scribe's 7 looks like a 9; 1874 has a number 11 written twice in November). **Only 1829 and 1830 tie to a printed total.** For the years before 1825, entries have no numbers and the control is the dates and the pages.

**Gaps and oddities in the images, not in the book.** Image 331 is a second exposure of 330. Images 416 left and 422 left are blank unfilled forms. **Page 448 is not imaged** (images 450–455 are pages 438–447 and 449–450; the running number goes 247 to 248 without a break, so this is probably a foliation slip, not a missing leaf). Some pages carry a number twice. Before 1825 a second run of days with no month label stands on image 130 right (page 122), after 30 December 1803, and does not fit 1803.

**Calan, enlarged by me at level 13.** **Image 519, left page (p. 377), 31 December 1874, December entry 13, annual no. 188, house Zamet 12:** «*Calan Albina filia Joannis Textoris*», two days old, cause *trismus*, buried by Robert Seluši(ć), cooperator. The surname is a clear *Calan* with a final *n*. The entry above it on the same page (29 December, also house Zamet 12) is a Joanna, wife of a Franciscus, of another surname. **It is not counted.** Calan is not in the Atlas's Kalanj family (which holds Kalain, Kalanj, Kallayn and the forms met on this line's own records), nothing in the entry connects the family of a weaver of Zamet to Draga, Bakar, Ledenice or a Kalanj, and the nearest the Kastav books come to it is a spelling: it is left here so that nobody counts it later without a second construction (inf).

**Other near-names, read and not counted.** *Callay* (image 346 right, page 305, 23 May 1846, entry 53, «Andreas vid. … Callay», house 64, age 78: my level-13 zoom reads Callay clearly; not in the catalogue, nothing ties it to Kalanj). The **Pauž / Puuz / Punž Kalac, Kalas, Kalaž** family of Punže: Helena (15 July 1854, image 399 left, entry 134), Andreas, Helena and Maria (1868–69) and four deceased of Punže in 1872 (images 506 left twice, 507 left, 508 left): a Kastav double surname, **not Kalanj**. *Kalich*, *Calich Milohna* (1819), *Calic* (1849), *Calnich/Caluich* (1807, a reader's zoom: not Kalanj), *Kalbier* (a nickname, 1840). *Kovačić* (Jurdana *vulgo* Kovačić, 1854) and *Kinkella Povacich* (1819, Kovacich?): not Kovačina. *Franković, Francetich, Franovich, Franelich, Franich, Frankovich* (house Rubesi 14 and others) and *Franti Marcus* (see below): not Defranceschi. *Kukan, Kukuljan, Kukaljan, Kukanić.* *Fiamin.* *Carlavaris/Carlovaris* of Castua. **Franciscus** appears as a given name and a father's name only (and once as a patronymic, «Jurdana … filia di francesci», image 455 right, 18 November 1861, entry 19); «Defti/Defuncti» is *deceased*.

**Priests called Josephus: none is a Defranceschi.** Canon *Josephus Varglien/Vanglien* (named as burying priest from 1774–1782 on; his own death is an entry of 22 March 1812, aged 89); *Josephus Pobar/Cobar*, Cap. and administrator of the parish, who signs from 1819 to about 1831; *Josephus Vode* (cooperator) and *Josephus Sichich* (canon, died 5 February 1851), both burying priests in 1848–49; *Josephus Lobar* (dean, died 17 June 1848); *Joseph Janz* (expositus) and *Josephus Dutkich* (cooperator), 1854–55; *Joseph Vouk*; *M.R.D. Josephus Don Rubesa* (an entry of 29 December 1863 for a parish priest «pensione donatus»); *Josephus Dukić* (the same, 26 July 1877, Castua 70). On 10 October 1874 (image 518 left) the parish priest «M.R.D. Joseph …» is himself buried, the surname partly legible, perhaps Dukić (clergy only). The cooperators who bury in 1874–82 are Robert Seluši(ć), Andreas Šuštar/Sitar and Anton Paz/Puz.

**Places the books name, for the record.** *Fiume* very often (a «Flumine» in the house column, a death «mortua Flumine», «ex parochia fluminensi»; images 277–278 in 1832, 425 in 1857, 458 in 1862 and 479 in 1866 among them); **Buccari**: Joannes Turak «mortuus Buccari» (image 181 left, 18 July 1817). **Trsat (Tersatto):** 22 October 1838 (image 309 left, entry 154) and a Hott/Stott Josepha, 16 June 1855 (image 405 right, entry 10). **Hreljin:** a mendicant «ex Hrelin» found dead on 13 February 1830 (image 258 left, entry 50), and the house cell HRELJIN for Blazina Augustina, 11 September 1855 (page 434, no. 64, read at crop level). **Draga:** «Draga(e) in Istria» on 1 February 1833 (image 281 left, entry 24: the Istrian Draga, not the Kvarner one, unsettled); «Bapta Draga» in the cause column of Maria Host on 7 September 1843 (image 334 left, entry 135); Margaretha Mohorich «ut Draga» on 28 September 1850 (image 375 left, running 154); Francisca Petelia, «ed Draga mendicans», on 26 May 1852 (image 386 left, entry 14). All four are people said to be *from* or *at* a Draga, **none a Defranceschi, a Kovačina or a Kalanj**. Also Portore («in portu regio», two unnumbered rows, 1839), Delnice, Veprinac, Volosca, Grobnik, Lovran, Mattuglie, Marsiglia, Cres and Dalmatia.

**Open cells, named so nobody counts them as read.** Image 74 right, 13 February 1786, «Catharina Kaliha» (a K or an R; not enlarged). Image 15 right, 2 April 1775, «Helena Filia Defuncti» (struck, blurred). Image 49 right, margin, 15 October 1780, Andreas Bontich Flumine. Image 39 right, 24 September 1778, last entry, the surname scribbled. Image 115 right (p. 107), 27 May 1798, the house cell «Bufchi/Buschi» (Buccari?) for Michael Morott, submersus. Image 138 left, 17 March 1805, «Helena Fran[in/inc?]», faint; 138 right, 31 March 1805, «ex Paroch. Bo…ensi in Istria». Image 165 left, 30 July 1812, «Mathias Stavich s. Kal(n)jske?» (unsettled, not enlarged: **the one cell in the volume that could be a Kalanj-type form and was not settled**). Image 162 right, 22 September 1811, «..alalich/Lebalich». Image 159 right, 11 November 1810, «ex Ta?ralia Ducarense». Images 169 left (5 August 1813) and 172 left (3 July 1814), the parish words. Image 220 right, 23 February 1824, «Dregha/Bregha» (probably Breg). Image 230 right, 19 November 1825, entries 149 and 156 (the parishes «Bernova?» and «fluminensis»). Image 305 right, 2 January 1838, entry 2, «Helena ux. Andreae Pilus Callaz» (the reader enlarged it: ends in *-z*). Image 312 left, 30 April 1839, «Flumine(?)». Image 321 right, margin of entries 39 and 46, March 1841, «Pobar/Pobri». Image 362 left, 11 August 1848, entry 119, «Valimich/Kalimich?» (first letter a V or a K, Mattuglie). Image 394 left, 3 October 1853, «Flumen/Fluman». Image 497 right, 31 October 1870, entry 20, «Mohorić Kalinac(?)». Image 520 right, 19 February 1875, Jusici 19, annual 46, «Franti Marcus commissus vectigalium coelebs ex Bitkaja(?)»: the surname's end and the place are unsettled. Image 540 right, November 1879, entry 5, «Katić/Kalić Antonius». Image 554 right (p. 747), July 1882, one struck-through row, the name unreadable. **Every cell at crop magnification except those I or a reader enlarged is unenlarged**; the priests' surnames in several years were not enlarged either.

**Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi and any De-/Di- + Fran- cell; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. The Atlas `cover` run exits 0 for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj. **Not counted for Kalanj:** Calan, Kalan and Callay are typed extras, not catalogued forms. Nothing was added to the Atlas from this volume.

sections.lab: Kastav deaths 1729–1774 (9R2Z-C6F), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: No Defranceschi, no Kovačina and no Kalanj in the Kastav death book of 1729–1774, and the three priests called Josephus are Tomicich, Raicich and Varglien; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The earliest death book of the parish of **Kastav (Castua)**, **1729–1774** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2Z-C6F**, which the Atlas catalogues as «Deaths (Umrli) 1729–1774»; Croatian State Archives microfilm, **roll 51, item 4**, 129 images, 0–128) was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**; the entries run from **image 4** to **image 123**. **No Defranceschi-type surname, no Kovačina and no Kalanj form stands in any cell that the readers or I could settle**, and **no priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi**. That is a reader pass and not a walk: most cells were read at the readers' crop magnification and not enlarged, and the cells named at the end stayed open and none of them is counted. The book is the one that comes before the 1774–1882 volume told above it (9R2X-YW5): the two overlap, because this one's last dated entry is **22 June 1774** and that one's first is **3 May 1774**.

**What the volume holds.** Image 0 is the filming slate (roll 51, «Zupa Kastav, Umrlih 1729–1774, item 4»), 1 a resolution target, **2 the front cover** («Liber Mortuorum 1729–1774», signature «275 (K4) 208»), 3 the inside label and title leaf, **4 a blank «Liber Defunctorum» leaf and the first page (3 January to 11 March 1729)**. From there to image 121 left it is **freehand Latin running lines, no columns and no entry numbers**: the month in a heading («*Junius 1756*»), the day in the margin, then «*Obijt* N. *filius / uxor / vidua* …, *an.* 40, *sepultus in C. S. Luciae*» (the cemetery churches are S. Lucia, S. Helena in the town and S. Jacob *ad Pedem*), and, by 1771–72, a house number written beneath each entry (images 108–113). **Images 122 right and 123 left are a ruled printed table, «Formulare Sepultorum»**, 3 May to 22 June 1774 (the last dated entry); 121 right, 122 left and 123 right are blank; 109 right is a blank printed «Distinta consegnazione dei Morti» form. 124 is the end-of-item slate (roll 51) and the title slate of the next item; 125 is «KRAJ», continued on roll 52; 126 a resolution target; 127 «END OF ROLL»; 128 a blank grey frame. **Image 83 is a second exposure of image 82.**

**A control: the months run on without a break.** An unnumbered register has no tally to check against, so the control is chronology: the readers dated every image from its month headings and the run is continuous across every boundary between their six-image chunks. Image 5 runs to 29 August 1729; 6 is September to November 1729; 7 to February 1730; 9 to February 1731; 11 to October 1731; 17 to 25 May 1733; 23 to January 1735; 29 to October 1736; 35 to 8 January 1739; 41 to October 1740; 47 to 1 September 1741; 53 to 4 January 1743; 59 to 13 November 1745; 65 to 26 January 1748; 71 to February 1750; 77 to 17 July 1752; 82 to July 1754; **89 to July 1758**; 95 to 30 June 1761; 101 to October 1765; 107 to January 1770; 113 to about August 1772; 119 to December 1773; 121 left to 2 May 1774. **One correction to the readers:** the reader of images 84–89 wrote the years as 1724–1728; at image 87 left I read the month headings myself and they say **1756** (Junius to November 1756), so those images are **August 1754 to July 1758** and join the run on either side. Small irregularities in the book itself: a month heading mis-written on image 28 («*Martius 1735*» above later months), a month with no entries in 1737 (no October), a few «*obijt*» lines left blank (image 8 left, 16 February 1730; image 22 right, September 1734), day numerals cut off on image 23 right, and day numerals partly lost in the binding on images 84–89.

**Near-names, read and not counted.** *Kalich, Calich, Colich* (many cells from 1729 on, images 5, 10–11, 39 left 1740 «*Matthaei Kalich(?) dictus Pistto*», 92 right 1760 a *Kalich* written above the line, and others); *Camlich* (5 right, 1729); *Kolenda or Rolenda* (112 right, 6 January 1772, «*Vid. Georgij Filejich* …*olenda*, 56»: **my level-13 zoom** shows a first letter that is a K or an R and an *o* where a Kalanj has an *a*, so it is not a Kalanj-type form); *Kulana* (76 right, 31 March 1752, «*Helena filia Georgij Kulana(?)*», 3 years: a reader's zoom reads *Kulana*, not *Kalana*); *Calirez/Colirez* (58 left, 21 December 1744); *Kukuglian/Kukughian* of Grobnik (30 right and 33 right, 1737–38) and *Kukerin/Kubrin* (76 right, 1752); *Franich, Francich, Frankovich, Frenkovich, Franckich, Franvich, Funkovich, Fonkaich, Franscich* and similar **-ich** surnames (images 6, 10, 26, 48, 52, 53, 70, 75, 76, 90, 91, 95, 104, 107, 117), *Framen(?)* (87 right, 1757), *Fianin(?)* (113 right), *Fearin/Franin Dorich* (46 right, 1741): Slavic **Franić/Franković** types, not Defranceschi. *Kuich/Luich* and *Kuchiel(?)* (not Kovač), *Carlevaris/Carlovaris*, *Francisci* and *Franciscus* as father's and given names only.

**Priests called Josephus: none is a Defranceschi.** *Dominus Josephus Tomicich*, a priest aged 27, died 3 December 1767 (image 105 left, buried S. Helena); *Dnus Josephus Raicich* (canon or collegiate), died 14 November 1772 aged 76 (115 right, S. Helena); *Josephus Varglien*, canon, who is *provisor* on 15 May 1774 (122 right) and buries on 29 May 1774 (123 left). Every other Josephus in the book is a layman: a child, a father («*Dni Josephi*») or a stranger (Cragnet, Carnidus, Raicich, Corch of 1741; Creigna of 1740; Perka and Carlevaris of 1744–45; Luich of 1737). Clergy among the dead: *Paulus Cragnet* (46 right, 7 June 1741), the canons *Matthias Sirolla* and *Andreas Colich* (1741), *Andreas Milich* and *Georgius Cinchella* (1747), *Matthias Bleich* (66 right, 6 June 1748), *Dominus Vincentius* found dead in bed in June 1760 (93 right). The priest of image 18 right, 2 October 1733, is *Joannes Baptista Dobor/Oebor* (spelling unsettled).

**Places the book names.** No entry reads **Draga, Bakar, Fiume/Rijeka, Hreljin or Kraljevica** with confidence. Three cells could be **Trsat or Rijeka** and are open: *Georgius* and *Andreas Dillepich* «*Tergtina*» (19 right, 4 and 12 February 1734: a Tersatina byname?), *Joannes Tomasich*, 19, who «*vedijt i Tersubio(?)*» and died the same night (38 right, about 23 January 1740), and *Catharina relicta Lucae Bastian* «*ex Rejina(?)*» (81 right, January 1754: Rijeka or the Rječina). At **image 87 left, June 1756, third entry, I enlarged a faint cell** («*obijt* … *filia* … *Bakaro/Bakara(?)*, 1 year, *sepulta in C. S. Jacobi ad Pedem*»): it is a faint surname, not «*ex Bakar*», and is left open. Also *apud Bar(?)* (49 left, doubtful). Named places otherwise: **Grobnik** (January 1751, 1737–38), **Veprinac** (images 56 right, 65 right, and in 48–53), Istria, Dalmatia (48 right, 27 September 1741), *Sombor(?)* (38 right, 1740), and an Italian note of the bishop of Pola's visitor (52 right, 30 May 1742).

**Open cells, named so nobody counts them as read.** Image 5 left, 6 May 1729, *Georgius Calich* (read at normal magnification only). Image 8 left, 16 February 1730 «*obijt*» with the rest blank. Image 10 left, last line, «*Joannes filius Joannis Frenkovich/Frenhovich*», day 22 or 27. Image 15 right, the year digit of «*Annus 1733 Januarius*» under an ink blot. Image 16 right, 4 February 1733, *Vincentia vidua qm. Judicis Caroli Floria(ni?)*; 16 left, 3 February 1733, the place «*ord Kukerini*» (a guess at the letters). Image 18 right, 2 October 1733, the priest's name. Image 19 right, the two *Dillepich* cells above. Image 35 left, 9 October 1738, «*Antonius … filius … Agnete Kabaroni(?)*», faint. Image 38 right, 23 January 1740, *Tomasich* (above), and a *Josephi Harch(?) in Sombor(?)*. Image 51 right, 11 April 1742, *Lucia uxor Francisci Cuchiel(?)*. Image 49 left, *apud Bar(?)*. Image 56 right, 26 March 1744, a man «*ex Parochia Veprinatz*» whose surname reads *Cigante/Digranto*. Image 58 left, 21 December 1744, *Calirez/Colirez*. Image 63 left, about 23 January 1747, *Vrsula uxor Franisci Valentin Gergan(?)*, 80; image 64 left, 9 August 1747, *Maria filia Dni Francisci Harech(?)*. Image 70 right, 31 October 1749, last entry *Joannes filius Joannis Franvich(?)*, 19, and the same type on 68 right and 69 left. Image 71 left, 22 November 1749, two entries «*submersus est in mari*» with the place word unclear. Image 79 left, November 1752, «*Franciscus filius Francisci De[struck]/Nebrizich(?)*» and image 81 right, January 1754, «*Maria filia Francisci Debruich/Delmuich(?)*» (De- cells without a Fran- stem). Images 90 right (January 1759, *Georgius Br-/Franscich?*), 91 left (March 1759, two *Francich?* cells), 95 left (February 1761, *…Franchich?*). Image 99 left, September 1763, *Laurentius Hordin(?) alias Furich(?)*; 96 left, December 1761, frayed widow entries; 100 left, the month header after April 1764 blurred (May assumed). Image 89 right, 12 March 1758, first line *Gregorii Cameres(?) ve Aroelic(?)*, unreadable. Image 107 left, early August 1769, *Catharina vid. Sebastiani Fra?ich/Famich*, 76; 104 right, 15 September 1767, *Nicolaus Fra?in*, 46. Image 116 left, the cut-off top entry and a struck *Georgius Vlach*, 73 (31 December 1772); 118 left, the last entry; 118 right *Andree Jasich?*; 119 right, after 24 December 1773, a faint struck line and an unfinished «*28. o*». Image 108 right, foot, *Georgius Smogor Parochij(?)*. Several ordinary surnames of January–April 1774 (*Dratia, Jerion, Lerdoce, Frinaistich*). **None of these looks like a Defranceschi, a Kovačina or a Kalanj, and none was enlarged except where I say so; every cell at crop magnification except those enlarged is unenlarged.**

**Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi and any De-/Di- + Fran- cell; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. The Atlas `cover` run exits 0 for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj. Nothing was added to the Atlas from this volume.

sections.lab: Kastav deaths 1883–1905 (9R2Z-BZ3), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: Two hits in the Kastav death book of 1883–1905: a Kalanj child of Zamet who died on 29 July 1902, and a mother born De-franceschi in 1904 that the FamilySearch index had already carried as a lead; no Kovačina, and no priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The last of the Kastav death books, **1883–1905** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2Z-BZ3**, which the Atlas catalogues as «Deaths (Umrli) 1883–1905»; Croatian State Archives microfilm, **roll 53, item 1**, film 392070701, 312 images, 0–311), was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**; the entries run from **image 7** (page 1, 1 January 1883) to **image 309** (30 April 1905). **Two cells carry a target name and I enlarged both myself at level 13: a Kalanj, and a Defranceschi as a mother's maiden name.** There is **no Kovačina**, and **no priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi**. That is a reader pass and not a walk: most cells were read at the readers' crop magnification and not enlarged, and the cells named at the end stayed open and none of them is counted. The book follows on from the 1774–1882 volume (9R2X-YW5) told above it.

**The Kalanj.** *Image 253, right page (p. 580), entry 199* (the running number of the year 1902): «**Augustina** (*Maria* written small above the line) **Kalanj**, *filia Josephi et Annae natae Dučić, operar.*», house **Zamet 117**, died **29 July 1902** at 10 in the morning, buried 31 July, aged ten months (the age cell gives the birth as 26 September 1901), bronchitis; the burying priest is Joannes Žiganto, cooperator. The reader read it at crop level as *Kalanj*; **my level-13 zoom** shows the same, with the *j* clear and *Maria* a small interlinear word over the first name. **doc** for the death, the age and the parents' names as the clerk wrote them.
