Her parents are a **Josephus Kalanj and an Anna Dučić** of Zamet, a hamlet of Kastav parish. **Nothing here ties them to the Josip and Rosalia Perković of Ledenice house 22**, told above, or to any other Kalanj of this page; no relationship is claimed, and no other Kalanj-type cell in the book was settled. Kalanj is the headline form of the Atlas family, so this is a hit on the name and nothing needed adding to the catalogue.

**The Defranceschi, and what the archive already held.** *Image 286, right page (p. 646), entry 61 of 1904*, a page of six entries to the page (the 1904 form): «Mortuus die **5 Aprilis 1904** media nocte», **Kastav**, buried 7 April 1904, 9 a.m., at S. Lucia: «**Kleinmayer Fridericus Maria Petrus**, *nobilis, filius Ferdinandi et Emmae* [small *n.* above, for *natae*] **De-/franceschi**, *geomet.*», born **23 February 1897**, seven years old, *vitium cordis*, signed by Joannes Ev. Vrabec, administrator. The two readers' crops and **my level-13 zoom** agree: «*De-*» closes the line and «*franceschi, geomet.*» opens the next, so it is one word, **Defranceschi**, a line-break and not a spelling. It stands in the **mother's** place: Emma, born Defranceschi, wife of Ferdinandus Kleinmayer. The cell after her name reads *geomet.* (geometra); the page does not settle whose trade it is, and I do not say. **doc.** **This is verification, not discovery.** The archive already carried the record as a lead: the FamilySearch index entry for the burial of 7 April 1904, indexed as «Fridericus Maria Petrus **Kleinmager** and Ferdinandi De Franceschi» (the marker for Kastav on the map data, ark 1:1:6YB2-6Y3M), and the register file holds a «Ferdinandus Kleinmager», born 1854, with «Ema Defranceschi» among the others. The index title puts the surname on the father; the page puts it on the mother and writes the father's name as Ferdinandus alone. Which Defranceschi family Emma belonged to the page does not say, and nothing here places her in a line.

**What the volume holds.** Images 0–5 are slates and targets (the film-start plate, a blank grey frame, a target, the Zagreb State Archives' *Početak* label «reel 53, continued from reel 52», and the slate «Župa Kastav, matična knjiga umrlih 1883–1905, item 1»), **6 the front cover**, **7 the inside label and page 1**. From there to image 309 it is the **printed Latin form «Liber Defunctorum in Ecclesia parochiali S. Helenae Castuae»**, one spread to the image, left crop the left page and right crop the right page: columns for the running number, the time of death, the house and hamlet, the name and condition (with the parents, «n.» for *nata*, the spouse), religion, sex, age with the birth date, the cause of death with the burial, and the signature of the priest. The readers counted seventeen rows to a page in 1887 and 1893; I saw twelve on pages 479, 580, 598 and 601 (1899–1903) and **six from 1904** (page 646). At the end, **309 right is a blank form, 310 left a loose slip** (a Fiume baptism extract, issued 2 October 189-, mother «Klestanjak»), **310 right is blank, 311 left reads «END OF ITEM» (roll 53) and 311 right is the title target of the next item**.

**A control: the book's own year-by-year numbering joins at every boundary.** Each year restarts at 1 on 1 January, so the last number of a year and the first of the next, and the numbers across every one of the readers' six-image chunks, make a tally that cannot be faked by a skipped page. I compared every boundary in the readers' notes: **the numbers run on without a gap across every chunk boundary of all 23 years.** The last number of each year, as the readers read it: 1883: 324 · 1884: 316 · 1885: 276 · 1886: 391 · 1887: 323 · 1888: 317 · 1889: 307 · 1890: 462 · 1891: 357 · 1892: 371 · 1893: 315 · 1894: 428 · 1895: 416 · 1896: 430 (**my own look at image 162 left**: entries 426–430, then a signed «Concordat cum originali, Castuae 31 Decembris 1896», Antonius Turak, and the parish stamp; the reader's «476–480» was a misread of the tens) · 1897: 444 · 1898: 441 · 1899: 351 · 1900: 397 · 1901: 349 · 1902: 431 · 1903: 443 · 1904: 243 (page 677, the rest blank) · 1905: to number 83, 30 April. A signed **«Concordat cum originali»** of 31 December, by the parish priest (Antonius Turak, then Michael Laginja from 1899 to 1901, and Joannes Vrabec in 1903), closes the years the readers noted; I have no note of one for 1884, 1902 or 1904. **Irregularities in the book itself:** in 1883 entries 100–105 on p. 7 are crossed out and the numbering restarts at 100 on p. 8; in 1884 number 95 is skipped on p. 27 with no missing row; in 1886 p. 61 is unnumbered (counted 69–85), and on p. 88 of 1887 the numbers were not legible and are inferred; in 1883 a struck entry of 2 October is re-entered as number 243; entries are often grouped by the burying cleric, so the dates jump back within a page (1900, 1902, 1903). **Duplicate exposures:** image 49 repeats 48's spread; image 177 repeats 176 and carries a «CORRECTION» slip; **images 204–207 are second photographs of pp. 479–482 and 485–488** (I laid 199 left beside 204 left: the same page 479, entries 109–120 identical, a different frame), and pages 483–484 are on the film once only, at image 201; image 307 left has the page number «686» a second time. **One chunk read twice:** the first reader of images 258–263 treated each pair of crops as one page and read half the pages (it gave pages 589–594, September–October 1902); I saw that on page 598 (December 1902, entries 408–419) and on page 600 (January 1903, entries 1–12) and threw that report away; the second read, of twelve different pages 589–600, entries 300–431, then 1 to 12, is the one told here.

**Near-names, read and not counted.** *Kalčić* (Bernasi 1884, p. 24, entry 49; Jul 1888 and 27 Dec 1888; 1889; and in 1900, 1901, 1903 and 1905 as a mother's maiden name or a surname, e.g. image 229 right, 7 Dec 1900, Blažići 107, «*Ioannes Kalčić*»; image 268 left, p. 609, 21 March 1903), *Kalić* (Antonius, 29 Nov 1889; Maria, 1890; image 192 right, 25 Nov 1898, with *l* or *t* not settled), *Kalinić* (image 215 right, 9 March 1900), *n. [K]alafetić* (image 216 left, 21 March 1900, initial faint), *Kalafat* as a trade word (image 270 left, 30 April 1903), *Kalec* (Antonius of Matulji, image 287 left, 18 April 1904), *Kalioster/Kaliošter* (image 155 right, 2 July 1896), *Kolanjer or Kolonjor?* (image 153 left, 18 April 1896, a *Kol-*), the **Puž/Pauž Kalac/Kaluc** family of Punže («*Joannes Puz Kalue*», image 64 left, 16 September 1888: a reader's zoom, not Kalanj), *Skalamera* (image 111 left, 1892: a reader's zoom, *Kalamer-*), **Felan** (below), *Kukuljan, Kukanić, Kukurin, Kukuljen* (many), *Kinkela, Kućel, Rubeša* (common local names), *Kovačić* (the mother's maiden name on image 291 left, 11 July 1904; entry 52 of 1905) and *Kovačević* (image 133 left, 31 Oct 1894, «*Ivan Ferdo Kovačević*», a reader's zoom), not Kovačina; *Franković, Frankovic, Franki, Francetić, Frančetić, Franković(?)* (images 11, 47, 292 and others), *Frlan*, *Depoli* (entry 233, 27 September 1883, «*Francisca Vid. Depoli nata Flumine*»), *Delimar/Delmar-ta* (image 99 left, about 22 Aug 1891), and *Francisci* and *Franciscus* as father's and given names only: none is a Defranceschi. **The Felan cells.** The reader of images 144–149 flagged six «Felan» cells, the first letter read as *F*: image 146 right, October 1895, entries 323, 324 and 328, and an out-of-sequence foot row of 20 October, and image 148 right, entry 392, December 1895. **My level-13 zoom of entries 323, 324 and 328** shows a flourished capital *F* and *Felan*, not *Kalan* or any *K*; entry 334 (*Helena Felan*), the foot row and image 148's entry 392 were not enlarged and are the same name, not excluded one by one.

**Priests called Josephus: none is a Defranceschi.** *Josephus Janc/Jane*, chaplain at the Rukavac chapel, signs from 1883 to 1886; *Josephus Petrak (Petrák)*, cooperator and then chaplain, from 1890 to 1903; *Josephus Vodička*, chaplain, from 1891 to 1901; *Josephus Podlitka/Podička* (the spelling moves) in the 1890s; *Josephus Anićić/Aničić/Ančić*, chaplain of Sv. Križ, from 1902 to 1905; and *Josephus Gortan* among the curates of 1903. The parish priests are Antonius Turak, **Michael Laginja** from 1899 to 1901 and, as administrator, **Joannes Ev. Vrabec** from 1902. Priests among the dead: *R.D. Ernestus Telusić(?)* (image 23, p. 33, 8 September 1884, aged 44) and a *R.D. Vincentius* (entry 232, 2 August 1892).

**Places the book names.** No entry has **Draga, Bakar/Buccari, Hreljin, Kraljevica or Trsat** as origin or residence, except one word in a house column: «**marčeljeva Draga, inventus in via**» (image 271 left, 3 May 1903, entry 184), the suicide of a stranger from Vienna, a place where he was found. **Fiume (Rijeka) is named in a number of entries, none with a target name**: a woman *nata Flumine* (entry 233, 27 September 1883), a shoemaker *natione Flumine* (1885), the mother's residence «*Flumine via governo 2*» (image 181 right, 15 May 1898), a burial «*in coemeterio Fluminensi*» (image 194 right, 23 January 1899), «*e Flumine*» (image 178 right, 24 January 1898), and a margin note «*provisa Portin. Fiumen.*» on 24 January 1905 (not zoomed). Also **Volosko**, **Opatija**, **Pola** (image 160 left, 18 October 1896), Trieste, Vienna, Istria, Udine (a drowned man of Prata, resident at Cordenons, 21 July 1900); and Zamet, Rukavac, Matulji, Jurdani and the other hamlets of Kastav parish.

**Open cells, named so nobody counts them as read.** Image 179 right, entry 46, 21 February 1898, «*Franciscus Puž, filius Joannis et Theresiae n. K…*» (the mother's maiden name a dotted *K*, not read as Kalanj, not enlarged). **Image 260 right, page 594, entry 363, 16 October 1902, «*Matthaeus Katić/Kalić*»** (*k* or *t* not settled; pencil «88/1905» in the margin). Image 117 right, entry 116, April 1893, the deceased's name partly illegible with the father «*…Francisci*». Image 123 left, 25 December 1893, entry 305, «*Catharina … vidua defti Josephi Trlan/Orlan*» (a reader's zoom: the first letter *T* or *O*, not *K*). Image 141, entries 139, 147 and 155, 1895: *Kuvel(?)*, *Kahrovićac(?)*, *Kutkesić(?)*. Image 24 right, p. 35, 12 October 1884, «*Maria f. Francisci Dea…ić(?)*» (a *De-* with no *Fran-* stem). Image 238 left, entry 191, 27 June 1901, a sub-line under «Kastav 15» that reads like *mortua in Brajda 53* (a Rijeka quarter). Image 245 right, entry 4, 14 January 1902, a place cell read *Dagaste(?)*; image 291 right, entry 121, 20 July 1904, a margin note that looks like *Rieka … 1904*; image 207 left, entry 215, 25 August 1899, «*Jug. (Fiumine …)*»; image 287 left, entry 67, the foot-note «*e Kutegovo? p. Tersato?, Croatia*» (a possible Trsat origin) under *Kalec Antonius*; page 678, entry 5 of 1905, faint, read *Bulfon*. Dates on many pages were not readable at the readers' magnification, and the entry numbers on a number of right-hand pages are cut off at the crop edge and were read from the sequence; **several chunks (for example images 138–143, 150–161, 168–173 and 246–251) were read at crop level with no enlargement at all**. **None of these looks like a Defranceschi, a Kovačina or a Kalanj; every cell at crop magnification except the three I enlarged (the Felan row, the Kalanj child, the Defranceschi mother) and the few a reader enlarged is unenlarged.**

**Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi and any De-/Di- + Fran- cell; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. The Atlas `cover` run exits 0 for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj. **Nothing was added to the Atlas catalogue from this volume.**

sections.lab: Kastav births 1837–1882 (9R28-L24), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: Nothing in the Kastav birth book of 1837–1882: no Defranceschi, no Kovačina, no Kalanj in any role, and no priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi; a reader pass over all 696 pages of images, with two pages unread and the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The Kastav baptism book **1837–1882** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R28-L24**, which the Atlas catalogues as «Births (Rođeni) 1837–1882»; State Archives in Rijeka, two bound volumes on one roll of 705 images, 0–704) was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first register page to the last. **Item 1, 1837–1852** (cover on image 6, «Tomus V»; page 1 on image 8 right) runs to **image 300** (p. 577, «Finis anni 1852 et hujus Tomi»); images 301–305 are slates and the cover of the next volume; **Item 2, 1853–1882** (page 1 on image 306 right) runs to **image 699** (the year-end note «Finis anni 1882», after one entry of 31 December on the last page). Image 700 is the end-of-roll slate, 701 a Zagreb end target, 702 a second end-of-roll slate, 703 a resolution chart and 704 a blank leader: **the roll ends there, and no register page is missing at the end.** The book is a printed Latin table, «Liber Baptizatorum» (child, baptiser, parents, godparents, house and hamlet of Kastav), 8 to 17 entries to the page.

**Nothing.** In 1,045 pages of the book (pp. 1–577 of 1837–52, then 1853–82) **no cell carries a Defranceschi form, a Kovačina form or a Kalanj form of the Atlas family, in any role** (child, father, mother and her maiden name, godparent, baptiser, midwife, margin note). **No priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi.** The Josephus who baptises is **Dukić** («Josephus Dukić par. pend.», 25 November 1868 and 24 February 1875, and a «Josephus Dukich Coop.» in 1855). Four other «Josephus» baptisers were read at crop level only and their surnames left open, and are **not excluded**: «Josephus … Parochus» in 1842 (entries 212, 240, 259, 268, images 114–119), «Josephus Igbar(?) Cap. Parochus» in 1845 (image 183 right, entry 264), two cursive Josephus in 1846–47 (images 204–209), and «Dolej Joseph … Cappellanus» on a late entry of 3 December 1863 at the foot of p. 264 (image 452 right).

**Cells I enlarged myself (level 13) or looked at as whole pages.** *Image 542 left (p. 391), entry 136 of 28 July 1872*: the godfather «Ant. Vincenz. **defacius**, impiegato alla strada ferrata», of Dolina, a railway clerk (**Defacius**, which ends -acius and is not Defranceschi; not in the Atlas catalogue; the reader's «defacins» was the first reading). *Image 447 left (p. 255), entry 151 of 21 June 1863*: the second godparent «Catharina **Francetich**» (the Francetić of Hosti, the reader's «francesich/Franceschich(?)»). *Image 125 right (p. 233), entry 14 of 10 January 1843*: «Joannes f. **Franciski** Roce, piscator Fluminensis», **Franciski is the father's given name**, not a surname. Four pages that a reader reported covered I looked at myself on the second exposure of the same opening and found clear: **p. 184 and p. 185** (1860, entries 65–96, images 402 left and 401 right), **p. 224 and p. 225** (31 December 1861 and January 1862, images 425 left and 426 right), **p. 329** (July–August 1869, entries 70–84, image 497 left), **p. 330** (8 August–8 September 1869, entries 85–99, image 498 right) and **p. 316** (March–April 1868, entries 33–50, image 486 right): no target form in any.

**Near-names, not counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Kalanj, Kovačina or Defranceschi family, and none is catalogued): **Kalčić** in its many spellings (Kalcich, Kalicich, Kalich, Kalić, Kal-čich, Kaličich, Kalcic; many dozens of cells from 1853 to 1880), Kalzin, Kalucich, Kalaz/Kalac, Calaich, Kukanić/Kukuljan/Kukurin/Kutkanić, **Kovačić/Kovačević/Kovich/Kovač** (a trade word and a surname), Frankovic/Franković/Francović, Francetić/Francetich/Franciscich/Francicic, Franellich, Valentini, Dibetto, Defacius (my zoom), and the abbreviation «**Deftus**» (*defunctus*, «deceased», two cells, 20 June and 29 August 1875). **Not zoomed, named and not excluded** (read only at the readers' crop level, each begins Fran-, Fia-, Kal- or Kov-): 1838 p. 41 entry 20 and p. 42 entry 33 «Valentini Fran..»; image 31 left (p. 46) entry 62 mother «[struck] Fran-/Frank- Varglien»; image 50 left (p. 84) entry 64 mother «Fancina?/Francina?»; image 99 left (p. 180) father «Fiam-/Fian-ini?» and mother «Francica n. de Steffan?»; image 100 right (p. 183) godmother «Luigia Fr..»; image 152 left (p. 287) entry 111 and right (p. 288) entry 125; image 252 left (p. 480) entry 165 father «Kacic/Kalicic?»; image 270 left (p. 517) entry 318 «Kak?-rien»; image 274 right (p. 526) entry 70 «Calaich/Culaich(?)»; image 353 left (p. 92) entry 340 father «Fran-cesith/Francesich»; image 395 right (p. 175) entry 357 «Kalzin(?)»; image 509 left (p. 343) entry 120 «Franc[..]ens(?)»; image 537 (p. 183) entry 66 «Franz Kaladin/Kalošin»; images 649 left (p. 564) and 650 right (p. 567) «Franp-/Tranp-»; image 668 right (p. 593) and image 657–658 (p. 579) «Kalčić»; image 638 right entry 86 «Francicic».

**Places.** **Draga** is named twice, neither time as a target: a smith «Petrus Buddan(?), faberferraz a Dragach» (image 389, p. 163, entry 177, 26 May 1859), and a mother «Joanna de Finjano/Tinjano … Draga B. Kar:», margin «nata Joanna Filipić» (image 564 left, p. 423, 8 August 1873, Matulji; the surname and «B. Kar:» unsettled even at level 13). The hamlet column «Draghi/Dreghi» is a **Kastav hamlet, not Draga**. **Trsat** («Tersaito») once, as the home of a father (image 377 left, p. 140, entry 198, 6 August 1858). **Fiume/Rijeka** appears as a trade or workplace of fathers and godparents (customs, tribunal, railway, fishermen of Fiume; «Josip Luparina iz Kozala-Rieka», 14 August 1881) and in later margin notes of the 1930s–60s. No Bakar, Hreljin or Kraljevica as origin.

**Control and structure.** The book's own running numbers restart on each 1 January and **join across every chunk boundary from 1837 to 1870** (checked chunk by chunk); from 1871 the printed table has no number column (house numbers, and pencil numbers in 1872 and 1877–78), so the join is by date and by the printed page number, and no jump was found. Second exposures of the same opening are common (images 63, 167, 183, 225, 319, 398–399, 401–402, 454, 476–477, 506–508, 512, 514, 536, 539, 561, 564–565, 585–587, 660–665, 690–695, and more): each was used to read the page the loose sheet hid in the other. 1952 slips of the registry pinned in the margins give later civil-registration notes and are not part of the entries.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** **Page 614** (image 684 left: 11 entries, 25 September–5 October 1881, houses at Jurići, Castua, Spinčići and Zamet) is **covered by a pasted blank sheet over every cell right of the house column**, with no second exposure on the roll; I looked at it myself. **Page 360** (images 520 and 521 right: about 6 or 7 entries, 18 June–9 July 1871) is under loose paper in both captures. Partly hidden: image 557 right (p. 414, two rows, April 1873); image 593 right (4th entry, date and child; and the left cells of the last entry, 1875); image 647 right (p. 563, entry 17 of 26 January 1879: child and baptiser, while the father and mother are legible); image 594 (p. 470, row 4, 1875); p. 276 entries 9 and 13 (1865, one image). p. 343 entry 125 (21 August 1870) was under a white band in one image and, by the reader's report, read on its other exposure; I did not confirm it. Many margin notes of the 1900s are only partly legible. **This is a reader pass, not a walk, and the book is not recorded as walked.**

**Atlas.** The `cover` run exits 0 for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj. **Nothing was added to the Atlas catalogue from this book**: near-names are not evidence of a variant. **Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi (and any cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-); Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. This is the third Kastav book read for the three names and the only one that holds births of the nineteenth century: the deaths of 1774–1882 and 1883–1905 are told above.

sections.lab: Kastav births 1776–1836 (9R2F-C66), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav birth books of 1776–1836: Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Kastav (Castua house 60) on three pages, 1787–1789, the index lead made a page; no Kovačina, no Kalanj, no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi; a reader pass, with the gaps and the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The Kastav baptism books **1776–1836** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2F-C66**, roll 48 of the Croatian State Archives, 676 images, 0–675; the Atlas catalogues the waypoint as 1776–1836, the slate on image 4 reads «ŽUPA KASTAV, MATIČNA KNJIGA RODJENIH 1729-1784, ITEM 1», so the slate and the Atlas title overlap and neither says what the three items hold) were looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first register page to the last. The roll holds **three items end to end.** **Item 1** (images 6–87): March 1776 to 30 December 1784, folios 300–381; a ruled table to 31 December 1780, then **running prose lines** from January 1781 to 31 March 1784, then a ruled table again from 1 April 1784; image 88 is the end-of-item slate, 89 the Zagreb slate and the slate of Item 2. **Item 2** (images 90–371, «Tom III», labelled 1785–1818): the front board and title on 91–92, **folio 1 on image 93 right (2 January 1785)**, a printed ruled table (Religio, Sexus, Patrini, Conditio, Baptiser) to about **image 323 (February 1817)**; then, from image 324 to 368, **a later book of 1817–1819 that is mostly blank pages**, set out **by the initial of the surname** (D on folios 499–500, F on 522–525, G on 530–531, S on 708–710, T on 735, V on 759, Z on 771; the readers of images 330 and 342 first called it surname-ordered and hamlet-sectioned, and the S, T, V and Z blocks settled it as the alphabet); images 369–371 are the slates «END OF ITEM roll 48, item 2 1785-1818, item 3 1819-1836» and a target. **Item 3** (from image 372): the cover and endpapers of «Matična knjiga rođenih 1819-1836, Inv. IV (198)» on 372–374 and the register proper from **image 374 right, folio 1**, a printed Latin table «Liber Baptizatorum» (day, house and hamlet, baptiser, child, running number, parents and her maiden name, godparents and their trade), entries restarting at 1 each 1 January, **the last entry, 31 December 1836 (Ludovicus, about no. 374), on folio 588 (image 669)**; the leaf after it is a blank form; images 670 and 671 are the end-of-item slate of roll 48 and the Item 3 slate (671 repeats 670, re-framed). Image 672 is the filmer's end slate («KRAJ / MIKROFILMSKI SVITAK BR: [48] … NASTAVAK NA MIKROFILMSKOM SVITKU BR: [49]»), 673 a resolution chart, 674 «END OF ROLL», 675 two blank frames: **the film continues on roll 49, which was not opened** (the births from 1837 are a different waypoint, 9R28-L24, read and told above; that roll 49 is that volume is not checked).

**One finding: Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Kastav, on three pages of 1787–1789. It verifies and gives a page to a lead the archive already held; it is not a new discovery in that respect.** The index lead **6YBK-Y5R8** (`register.json`: «Constantinus Antonius Josephus», parents «Vicentius Blasius Defranceschi» and «Marianna», no year, no place, status lead) is **found on its page**: **image 125 left, folio 64, 12 March 1789, house «Cast. 60» (Kastav, Castua house 60)** — the child is **Constantinus Antonius Josephus**, the father **«D. Vincentius / Blasius / Defranceschi»**, the mother **«Marianna»**, the godparents «… Gram / Teresa Gram» (the first word unsettled), baptised by the canon Joannes Raicich; the father's name and the child's are clear at level 13, the father's trade cell («direct…/conco…») is not (doc, my level-13 zoom). Two earlier cells name the same man as a **godfather**, and the first of them is the one the reader got wrong: **image 122 right, folio 59, 6 October 1788, house «Cast. 12»**, Petrus Vincentius Fortunatus, child of Josephus Caporilla and Antonia, godparents **«Vin: Blas: Defranceschy / Anna Göpperle»**, his condition written «Sind.», baptised by Joannes Raicich (the reader had «Nicolas Defranceschy»; at level 13 it is **«Vin. Blas.»**, and the surname ends **-schy**); and **image 117 left, folio 48, 19 December 1787, house «Vol. 4» (Volosca)**, Franciscus Thomas, child of Antonius Varglien and Maria, godparents **«Vin. de Frameschij / Ellena Tomicich»**, condition «Sind.», baptised by the canon Lucas Chinchella (level 13: the **m of «Frameschij» is probably a joined n and c**, since the scribe writes *Franciscus* with a separate n and c on the same row; so «Vin(centius) de Franceschi», the letters not fully settled; **inf**). **The three agree on one man** (the name Vincentius Blasius, the sponsor's «Sind.»), who is **a sponsor at baptisms in 1787–89, with the condition «Sind.»** and, in March 1789, the head of a household at Castua 60 with a wife Marianna. **No other cell of the book names him or a child of his** (the readers, who from image 294 were told to look for him, and the notes of the earlier chunks report none). House 60 in Kastav is held by other households before and after (Cambron/Samson in 1809, Dubricich in 1816–18, Marotti from 1825 to 1832). **The surname spelling has been added to the Atlas** (Defranceschy, attested, from a 1788 baptism register of Kastav; *added locally, not yet published*). **Nothing ties him to a line of this archive**; that is not claimed.

**Nothing else of the three names, in any role.** No Kovačina form and no Kalanj form of the Atlas family stands in any cell the readers or I could settle; **no priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi** (the Josephus who baptise are the canons **Varglien** (1776–1790s), **Rubessa** (1809–1819), **Sichich**, **Pobar(zan)**, **Pichich**, a **Schöpf** in 1836 and a Josephus Caroly(?) in 1812). **Cells I enlarged myself (level 13), other than the three above:** *image 104 left, folio 22, 28 May 1786*, the godmother «Margarita **De Fra-/nel Wachsenheim**» (a German double surname of a lady, read by the reader as «De Fra-/nsel»; not a Defranceschi form, the second line is *-nel Wachsenheim*); *image 417 left, 28 June 1822, entry 132*, the first godfather «Franc. Jos. **Dzekeitzky(?)**», condition «Chirurgo ad Osp. Locale», with «Francesca ux. Antonii Gradich» (the reader's «Degekeko»; not De Fran-); *image 410 right, folio 37, 14 and 24 November 1821, entries 276 and 287*, the infant cells «Andreas **Franc: Xav.**» and «… **Franc: Xav.**» are **Franciscus Xaverius**, a saint's name (the readers' «Franc.-Kov.» is an X, not a K), with parents Mathias Sirola Dovicich and Anna née Jellovich. **Near-names, none counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj family): **Kalčić** in many spellings (Kalcich, Calcich, Calich, Calerich, Kalich, Colcich; very many cells), **Franul de Weissenthurn** (the captain of Kastav, godparent 1776–1783), Francovich/Francetich/Franich/Francich, Fracasso, Frizzul, Dukich/Duchich the surgeon (the Franciscus given name before it is not a surname), **Dubricich/Dubrojcich/Dzebricich** (every Vincentius D. of 1810–1836: Dubricich, a different name), Zamlich, Tomasich, Trinajstich, Kovacich/Covacich, Kon-/Kov-ich (a canon of Veprinac, 1799), Kukuljan, Kinkella, Carina, De Stefani, Marceglia, **Calinar/Calinari/Kalinae/Callinax** (a woman's surname, 1817–1831, and a word after the patronymic Mohorich: not in the Atlas and not a Kalanj form), **Kalaz** («Joannes Luux Kalaz», 23–24 August 1832), **Calaj** (image 554), Kalnich.

**Places.** **Draga**: a godfather «Sartor ex Draga» (21 September 1822, entry 195), godparents «ex draga» (folio 272, 30 December 1827) and a conditio «Sacerdos Draž/Drag.o» on image 176 left (21 November 1796, unreadable); none a target, none zoomed. **Bakar/Buccari**: «Canonicus Buccarensis» Kucich (image 128 left, 19 October 1789), a baptism at Buccari by the archpriest Chinchella (image 130 left, 7 March 1790), «Joanny Fracassa Cpt Buccarani» (1800), «Martinus Borcich de Buccari» (1832). **Tersatto/Trsat**: a loose baptism certificate of 14 September 1798 tipped into folio 189 (names not read), a mother «Tersat(i)» (image 268 right, 8 May 1809). **Fiume/Rijeka** as home or office of godparents and fathers throughout (Fiume parish godparents 1779, 1786, 1802, 1803, 1814, 1823 at Fiume by a canon of the Fiume chapter, 1835). No Hreljin or Kraljevica as origin.

**Structure, control and what this reader pass is not.** The running numbers of Item 2 and 3 restart each 1 January and were followed from page to page (year totals read: 272 in 1810, 297 in 1811, 261 in 1814, 227 in 1815, 304 in 1832, 299 in 1830, 319 in 1828, 330 in 1835, 360 in 1825); numbers used twice or off by ten are named in the reports (November 1822, 1833, 1836). The layout changes on 5 November 1812 (the mother's maiden name «nata», the hour of birth). Images 297 and 298 and 436 and 437 are the same opening twice; images 186–191 hold folios 188–189 twice. **This is a reader pass, not a walk, and the book is not recorded as walked.** **Gaps, not nils:** in the 1817–1819 book the openings are **not consecutive** (folios 487→498→500→522→525→530; 488–497, 502–521 and 526–529 are not on these images), so the **«Fr-» block (Franceschi would stand after Fa-, Fi- on folios 526–529) is not on the film I read, and a Defranceschi block under D (folios 497–499) is not seen except for Dubricich, Dukich and Dergnevich on folio 499–500**; folios 586–591 of the sectioned book lie between images 344 and 345 and are not on any image; the parallel runs of 1817–1819 on folios 458–465 and 483–485 are a second copy. A name born in those two years is not excluded by this pass.

**Not zoomed, named, not excluded** (read at page size, or at the reader's crop, and each begins De-, Fra-, Fr-, Kal-, Kov- or a flourished Vincentij): image 94 left (February 1785, Joannes Bercich, godfather «Giovanni Fr?z?nich»); image 109 left (folio 32, 1 January 1787, godparent scrawl ending «…ancescogi»); image 176 left (21 November 1796; the condition «Sacerdos Draž/Drag.o»); image 205 left (folio 222, 14 January 1801, godfather «Joannes Franc…», the last letters lost in a flourish); image 213 right (folio 239, 14 June 1802, godfather **«Vincentius Dnus Sam…»**, the surname flourished; the reader says it is not Defranceschi, I did not zoom); image 255 right (31 October 1807, godparents «Franc. Xav: Re[?]schini» and **«Catharina Samson uxor Dni Vincentij»**, no surname after Vincentij, flourish only); image 274 left (10 January 1810, father «Caporito in Lago Franci/nelli»); image 322 left (29 December 1816, godfather «D. Franc. Blanich/Blasich?»); image 559 left (folio 368, December 1830, entries 16 and 19, «Franciscus Dr. [?]/Sinich(?)», read «Dr.» not «De»); image 554 right (folio 359, September 1830, entry 203, godfather «D. Joannes Čalaj/Calaj», first letter unsettled); image 342 right (folio 581, 10 November 1817, entry 8, father «Josephus Kalich(?) fil. Josephi»); the unsettled baptisers «Franciscus Coverlizza Beneficiatus» (1835–36); image 634 right; image 652 right (entry 95 of 1836, German cursive, illegible); image 665 right (14 November 1836, «Helena fa … Pint Calez/Calay»); image 666 left (folio 582, 22 November 1836, godfather «Giovani Kal/Kul-esso, fabro», the first letter K or R); image 667 (folio 585, 20 December 1836, house cell «Pu?/Cova?ni 43»); image 668 (folio 586, 8 December 1836, father «Andreas Francovich», a near-name); image 644 right (4 December 1835, entry 294, Castua 78, «Vincentius Dubreich/Dubrcich Arcularius», read unzoomed); and the **Fran-/Kal- cells of the reports 6–671 that are listed in the notes of the readers and that I did not enlarge**, mostly Franul, Francovich, Francetich, Franz-, Calich, Kalcich. Many other cells were read once at page size.

**Atlas.** `cover` exits 0 for **Defranceschi** (after the addition of **Defranceschy**), **Kovačina** and **Kalanj**. **Added locally to the Atlas catalogue: Defranceschy (attested, a 1788 baptism register of Kastav; no person in the evidence); not yet published.** Nothing else was added: Calinar, Calinari, Kalinae, Callinax, Kalaz and Calaj are not catalogued and were seen only as near-names, which are not evidence of a variant. **Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi (and any cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-); Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn (and, from image 534, Calinari, Kalinae, Callinax, Kalaz); from image 294 the readers were also given **«D. Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi / Marianna (Castua house 60)»** as an extra target. This is the **fourth Kastav book** read for the three names, after the deaths of 1729–1774, 1774–1882 and 1883–1905 and the births of 1837–1882; the births before 1776 (9R2D-44M, 9R2D-4W5) and the marriages are not opened.

sections.lab: Kastav marriages 1729–1806 (9R2Z-GPT), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav marriage books of 1729–1806: three Defranceschi marriages — Josephus son of Joannes (19 January 1744), Franciscus son of Leonardus (14 October 1751) and Vincentius Blasius of Castua 60, bachelor of 24, with Marianna Theresia Tomicich, a widow of 29 (24 July 1788); no Kovačina, no Kalanj, no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The Kastav marriage books **1729–1806** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2Z-GPT**, roll 50 of the Croatian State Archives; the Atlas catalogues the waypoint as «Marriages (Vjenčani) 1729–1806») were looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first register page to the last; the ark list of the waypoint holds **200 distinct images (0–199)**. **Images 0–7** are the filmer's slates, resolution targets and the vellum cover («Liber Matrimoniorum ab anno 1729 usque ad annum 1774 Kastav») and inside board of the first book. **Item 1 (1729–1774)**: the register begins on **image 8** (flyleaf and page 1, 26 May 1729), Latin prose, one paragraph per marriage, the marrying priest Joannes Baptista Dobor/Pober throughout the readers' reports, about 8–12 entries a page; the last written entry is on **image 104 left, 22 January 1774**; 104 right and 105 right are blank, 106 is the back board, **107 is the end-of-item slate** («Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1729-1774, Item 1»). **Item 2 (1774–1806)**: image 108 is its slate, 109 a resolution target, 110 the cover, 111 the inside label and page 1; a **ruled table** (day, officiant, groom and bride, witnesses, place, number) from 1774, running prose again from February 1781 (image 143 left), a printed table of groom, bride and two witnesses with age, status and house number from 1784 (image 151 right, page 41) and 1788; the last written entry is on **image 198 left, 19 March 1806** (Georgius Ferlan with Antonia Guinich?), 198 right is a blank, water-damaged folio 87, **199 left is the end-of-item slate and 199 right a slate that again reads «Item 2, 1774-1806»** (the same title as image 108; the reason is not known to me). Several spreads are photographed twice (images 25–26, 85–86, 176–177 are second exposures). The reader pass covered **images 8–198**; images 8–23 were read at page size in an earlier pass of this session and the rest in 6-image chunks.
**Three marriages of a Defranceschi on the pages; each cell was enlarged by me at level 13 (doc), and one of the three is the marriage the archive had been looking for.**

**1. 24 July 1788 — Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua house 60 and Marianna Theresia Tomicich (image 161 left, ark 3QS7-899X-5RD).** The printed-form register of 1788 (house, groom, religion, age, bachelor or widower, bride, witnesses): house column **«C. 60»**; groom **«Vincentius / Blasius / Deframeschi»** — my level-13 zoom shows the surname as **D-e-f-r-a-m-e-s-c-h-i** with a flourish after the last letter, the **n of «Franc-» written as minims that read as an m** (the same joined n and c that the Kastav baptism book of 1787 gave, «Vin. de Frameschij», see the births of 1776–1836 above); **age 24**, Catholic, single; bride **«Marianna / Theresia / Tomicich»**, Catholic, **age 29**, the widow's column marked 1 (a cross-like mark stands in the single's column; I take her for a widow, **inf**). The entry stands between 19 July 1788 (Matthaeus Sirola and Helena Marcovich) and 1 October 1788 (Andreas Slavich and Catharina Kaszal), under the signature of the archpriest Antonius Chinchella at the foot of the page. **The witnesses' cell is scrawled and I did not read it** (the first line begins «And.? Sor?…», the last «Gioan Soppe?… Remin Demic?»: unsettled). **This is the marriage the births of 1776–1836 pointed to**: house 60 is the **«Cast. 60»** of the baptism of Constantinus Antonius Josephus on 12 March 1789, whose father is «D. Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi» and whose mother is «Marianna» (the index lead 6YBK-Y5R8 in `register.json`), and the baptisms of 6 October 1788 and 19 December 1787 where the same man stands as a godfather, which are told above; **the marriage is eight and a half months before that baptism** (inf, from the two dates). A «Helena Tomicich» is the godmother of the baptism of 19 December 1787 (read in that pass): a name in common with the bride, **not a relationship; not claimed**. That a Defranceschi of **24 in 1788** was born about **1764** is a reading of the age column, not a birth record; his baptism was not found in the Kastav baptism books read so far (the book of 1729–1776 was read at page size, which is not a nil for him), and a first husband of Marianna Theresia (she is a widow) is not looked for here.

**2. 14 October 1751 — Franciscus son of Leonardus De Fran-… and Maria, daughter of Joannes Be[r]ninich (image 59 left, last entry, ark 3QS7-899X-597Y).** Latin prose, the priest Joannes Baptista Dobor; the entry reads «Franciscus Filius Leonardi **De Fran[…]** ex Parochia **Gol[…]** … copulatus … cum Maria filia **Joannis Be[r]ninich** ex mea Parochia». At level 13 (the ink is pale; two earlier crops of mine landed a row high) the surname is **De Fran-** and four or five letters that I read as *-esch-i* but **do not settle** (a *c* and an *s* in this hand are close); the word that follows «ex Parochia» begins *Gol-* and its end is not read. **This is very probably the marriage behind the index lead 6YB2-WGQK** (`register.json`: «Franciscus», with the names «Leonardi De Franceschi», «Joannis Berninich» and «Maria», no year and no place): all four names agree. **It verifies and places a lead the archive already held; it is not new in that respect.** I did not see the index record itself. The register of the archive's tree also holds other De Franceschi of Croatia named «Leonardo» (e.g. a Leonardo and Eufema, a Leonardo and Maria Corva); **none is tied to this man; not claimed**.

**3. 19 January 1744 — Josephus son of Dominus Joannes [Anton…?] de Fran-… and Helena, daughter of the judge Georgius [Faich?] (image 42 right, page 33, entry 2, ark 3QS7-899X-59KL).** The second entry of the day, **underlined** on the page: «Josephus Filius Dni Joannis [Anton…?] **de Fran[…]** ex Parochia **Gol[…]** … copulatus … cum Helena filia Judicis Georgij [Faich?] …». At level 13 the word after *de* is **Fran-** and four or five minims and a final letter that I read as *-eschi* or *-esii*: **the ending is not settled** (the same *-ex Parochia Gol…* as in the entry of 1751). **Not in the archive's index leads** (`register.json`, `fsrecords.json`: no Josephus, no Joannes Antonius, no Kastav entry of 1744 was found by grep): a new find in that respect, **inf** for the family, **doc** for the cell. **A Josephus born about 1715–1725 would be a child of the Kastav baptism books of 1700–1728 or 1729–1776, both read at page size with nothing settled; that is not a nil for him.** **Nothing ties any of the three men to another, to a line of this archive, or to the name of the Atlas families, and no relationship is claimed.**

**Nothing of Kovačina or Kalanj**, in any role, in any cell the readers or I could settle. **No priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi.** The priests called Josephus are the canons **Josephus Roicich** (1736–1738), **Slach**, **Cuich** (a dispensation of 20 May 1748, read at page size), **Varglien/Verglien** (canon of Lovran, 1760s–1790s, also «A.R.D. Jos. Vatglien» 1797), **Josephus Bobar/Pobar/Cobar** (1783–1804, chaplain on 12 November 1804), **Josephus Spingarolli** (canon of Fiume, 23 November 1774) and **Josephus Macerovich** (parish priest of Grobnik, December 1774); the marrying priests of the book are Joannes Baptista Dobor (to about 1773), Lucas and then **Antonius Chinchella** (archpriest, from 10 January 1779), canons Mihelich and Letisich, **Mathias Spincich** (administrator from 1803) and, in 1806, Mathias Guinich and Andreas Marcaglia.

**Cells I enlarged myself (level 13), other than the three above:** *image 85 right, top of page 76 (an entry of 2 November 1762)*, the witness **«Excellentissimo Dno Francesko-»** with the hyphen at the end of the line: **a given name** (Francesco) of a doctor of both laws, not a surname — the continuation on the next line was **not** zoomed; *image 65 left, foot, 10 January 1754*, a dispensation line naming **«Ludovici De[…]ntorich/-ovich»**: **De + f or s + about five letters + -rich/-ovich, no Fran- shape**, letters not settled, not counted. **Near-names, none counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj family): **Kalčić** in many spellings (Calich, Kalich, Kelich, Colich, Calcich, Karlevanj-Kalcich), **Franul** (the captain of Kastav; canon Michael Franul, «Marchio de Weisenberh», 1777), Frankovich/Francovich/Francetich/Franich/Francich/Franza/Franza of Volosca, Fianin, **Kulena/Kalena** (image 68 right and 70 right, 1755, a family; the reader enlarged it: the letters are *Ku-l-?-na*), **Kielan/Kiclan** of Halubje (image 121 left, 1776, enlarged by a reader: not Kalan), Descovich, Fricgul, Cetina/Cotina (17 February 1806), Tarcina (1735). **Places:** Fiume/Fluminensis in very many cells; **Bakar/Buccari**: Michael Rabbicich «ex Parochia Buccarensi» (9 November 1754), Mathias Rofich widower «ex Parochia Buccarensi», keeper of the tobacco monopoly (11 September 1781, image 143 left) and a canon of Buccari delegating (28 January 1788); **Trsat**: a groom «Franciscus Cuvicius?/Corvinus ex Thermanensi/Tersattensi?» (image 81 right, 26 February 1760), unsettled and not enlarged; **Draga, Hreljin, Kraljevica: none**.

**Not zoomed, named, not excluded** (read at page size by the readers; each begins De-, Fra-, Fr-, Kal- or Kul-): image 46 right (2 November 1745, last entry, the witness «Joanne **Kulaca/Kalaca**(?)»); image 64 left (5 March 1753, «De Prace»); image 62 left, top («Franco-/bilovci»); image 81 right (26 February 1760, the Trsat origin above); image 89 left (13 February 1765, groom «Nicolaus Finarlich/Franarlich? Merkelin?»); image 101 right (20 July 1772, first entry, witness «Franciscum Kowans?/Franel/Franul?»); image 116 right (15 January 1775, the copulans «Petrus Fran(?)dus Guilo?hi, Archidiaconus et Vicarius… a portu Austriae», a priest, not De Fran-); image 134 right (23 November 1778, no. 198, «Antonius Franicich», perhaps Ivanicich); image 153 left (26 January 1785, groom «Franciscus De[s/f]covich»); image 174 right (15 October 1795, witness «Franc° Franel/Franul»); image 172 left (27 November 1793, foot, witnesses «Francesco Plesichma?» and «Franciscus … Radeskin?»); image 184 left (23 November 1800, bride «Helena Fran?cich/Grancich»); image 185 left (26 November 1800, witness «Greg. Franotich/Francsich»); image 110 (the front cover of the second book: a pencil word that looks like «De fran…» at page scale, **not part of the register**); and the parish word after «ex Parochia» in the entries of 1744 and 1751 («Gol…»). Many other cells were read once at page size.

**Gaps, not nils.** Images 8–23 were read in an earlier pass at page size and are not in the 6-image chunks. **This is a reader pass, not a walk, and the book is not recorded as walked.** Illegible or overwritten at page size: image 136 left (11 January 1779, the whole entry over-written with ink loops), image 131 (February 1778, a sixth entry whose date and names are obliterated), the witness lines of 23 November 1777 (image 128 right, partly scribbled out), the dating of the pages around **1801–1802 (images 185–187)** was not cross-checked between the two readers who covered it (one reports no 1801 entries, the other a first page of February 1801), **April 1778 is not on the images 132–137** (a reader's note), and the witness cells of the 24 July 1788 entry. A name in one of those cells or in an unzoomed cell is not excluded by this pass.

**Atlas.** `cover` exits 0 for **Defranceschi** (typed: Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Defranca, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defranci, Defrancheski, Franceski), **Kovačina** (Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich) and **Kalanj** (Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn); the readers were also given «De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defrancesco, Di Franceschi, plain Franceschi» and any cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-, and the priest Josephus. **Nothing was added to the Atlas catalogue by this pass**: the spelling **Deframeschi** is a reading of a joined n and c in the same hand, not a spelling of the clerk, so it is not catalogued; **Defranceschy** (the births of 1776–1836) is *added locally, not yet published* until the publish below. This follows the Kastav deaths of 1729–1774, 1774–1882 and 1883–1905 and the births of 1700–1728, 1729–1776, 1776–1836 and 1837–1882; the marriage books 9R2Z-J43, 9R2Z-JWB, 9R2Z-ZNL and 9R2S-44C are not opened.

sections.lab: Kastav marriages 1806–1841 (9R2Z-J43), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav roll 9R2Z-J43, marriages 1806–1831 and the leaves of 1831–1841, with the deanery circulars bound between: nothing of Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj settled, no child of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua 60 and no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The last Kastav marriage roll that carries 1806 onward (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2Z-J43**, roll 50 of the Croatian State Archives, **175 distinct images, 0–174**; the first slate calls it Item 3, the cover note «Liber III copulatorum 1806–1818», «also 1831–1841», Povijesni arhiv Rijeka) was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first register page to the last slate. **It is not one book, and I have not settled how its parts relate**: **images 0–3** are slates, a target, the cover and the flyleaf; **images 4–29** are a ruled Latin table of marriages from **26 April 1806** (image 4 = ark 3:1:3QSQ-G99X-5K2) to **17 January 1819**, with one lone entry of 25 November 1822 on image 28, the marrying priest canon Josephus Benedictus Rubessa as delegate from 1815; **images 29–114** are **not marriages**: they are the book of **deanery circulars** («Decreta et Circulares», Latin, Italian and German, the Ordinariate of Trieste-Koper to the Deanery of Castua, forwarded by the pro-dean **Josephus Pobar/Cobar/Tobar**), from 1826 to 1834, with printed folio numbers, tax and benefice tables, a status-animarum form (image 35 right), and nothing that names a person of the three families; **image 115 right** begins a Latin marriage register again, page 219, **6 February 1831**, to 6 February 1835 on image 119 (about 115 entries in one hand; some January–February 1834 entries are dated «1832»); **images 120–131** show a spread whose two bound pages (a page of 1835 on the left, a page of **1806** on the right, the readers' pencil numbers 280 and 229) are **covered by shingled loose leaves** with marriages of **1835 to December 1841** (I looked at the leaf over the right page of image 123: it carries entries of 20 July to 22 November 1836; image 129 is an upside-down re-photograph of image 128); **images 132–169** are a bound Latin register again, from the **1806** entry of 27 October 1806 on image 133 (a loose 1841 slip of six entries lies over the heading on image 132) through 1811 (image 142), 1818 (image 150), 1821 (image 154; image 155 is a second exposure with a folded letter over p. 273), 1825 (image 162) and 1829 (image 167) to the **last entry of 30 January 1831 on image 169 left**; 169 right is blank; **images 170–173** are loose leaves lying over p. 298 (student-stipend attestations, a German salary table of the Decanat of Castua of 5 April 1830, a circular of 9 June 1832); **image 174 left is the end-of-item slate** and 174 right the target of the next item («vjenčanih 1806–1818, Item 3»). **The dates of images 4–29 and of images 133–169 overlap (1806–1819), and the page numbers the readers took from the later images (230–298) do not continue those of images 4–51; I did not compare the two runs entry by entry**, so I do not say whether they are two copies, two registers or one register in two parts. The marriage entries of images 4–29, 115–169 and the loose leaves were read; the circulars were looked at only to see that they carry no marriage.

**Result: nothing of the three families settled, in any role.** No Defranceschi form and no cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran- was seen by a reader, and I found none in the cells I enlarged; **no marriage, witness or note of a child or a daughter of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua house 60** (Constantinus Antonius Josephus, born 1789, and any sibling), the extra target of this pass, was seen; **no Kovačina** form; **no Kalanj** form. **No priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi**: the Josephus of the roll are the pro-dean **Pobar/Cobar/Tobar** (1826–1834, signing every circular), the delegate canon **Josephus Benedictus Rubessa** (1815–1820), **Josephus Varglien** as a witness (27 October 1806), **Josephus Vlach** and **Josephus Rubessa** as delegates (1808–1811), **Josephus Lobar** (1814–1815) and a deceased priest Josephus of Tomaj (a circular of 1831).

**Cells I enlarged myself (level 13, and 3–4× on the word):** *image 142 right (p. 249), 25 July 1811*: the bride's father, which a reader took at page size for «Mathei **Kalian**(?)», reads **«K-u-k-a-n»** (a hooked K, a u, a second hooked K, a, n): a **Kukan**-type name, **not** Kalan or Kalanj, not counted. *Same page, 26 June 1811*: the witness **«Joannes Francetich»** (Fran-ce-tich, no De-): a near-name, not counted. *Image 22 left (p. 36), 24 November 1814*, house R.606: the groom's house-name **«pul Francichi»** (the pattern «pul X» is a house-name pattern in this book): Fran-ci-?-hi, no De/Di, letters after Fran- not settled, not counted. *Image 123 right, 21 November 1836, a loose leaf*: «Ioannes Susan Antisich … filia sua Catharina cum Ioanne filio Andr. Dni **K?lag**», the first letter a hooked K, the second a u or an a, then **l-a-g**, **no n**: **«Kalag»/«Kulag», unsettled, not an Atlas Kalanj form** (the Atlas holds Kalagnia, with -nia, from another parish), not counted. *Image 128 left (a loose leaf), 16 February 1840, entry 5*: «Andreas **Pauz ?llag/?llay**», the first letter of the second word lost in an ink smear (F, K or J), ending in -lag/-lay like the 1836 cell: **unsettled, not counted**; the same name appears twice in the entry of 14 February 1841 (image 130 left, «Antonius Pauz Fabay/Falay», which a reader enlarged at about 5× and read with a looped F/J/K first letter); **I did not enlarge that cell**.

**Near-names read by readers, none counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj family): **Kalčić** (Calcich, Calich, Calika?), Francetich/Franetich/Franich/Francovich/Fancovich/Frandich/Francin (Pinder), Kovachich/Covacich, Falan, Kinchella Covacich, Mathias Francetich (image 119 left, 14 September 1834), Destaffori (De- but not Fran-), Kalnich (image 147 left, 10 July 1815, «Jacobus Kalnich pul Milohari»), Kambizh, Juranich, Arnichievich, Cabeich/Cabich. **Places named in cells:** Fiume/«fluminensis» in many entries (for example images 136 right 17 May 1807, 142 left 16 February 1811, 162 left 9 February 1825, 117 right 6 December 1832, 118 right 26 November 1833, 128 left 4 February 1840, 130 left 1 December 1841); **Draga**: image 135 left, 10 January 1807, «Josephus filius qdm Francisci **Saroquinaz** ex Draga Parochia S.ti Antonij» (the Draga father's surname unsettled), image 161 left (12 April 1824), image 124 right (29 January 1837, «ex Draguch»), image 22 left (14 August 1814, a margin origin «Parochia Dra?en?i», unsettled), image 9 right (a tag «s. Dragh(i)» after Kuchiel/Stanich, 25 November 1807 and 22 February 1808, **unzoomed**: a place or a house-name); **Bakar/Buccari**: image 150 left, 7 November 1818, «Gregorius Ghergarich Bucarensis», image 167 right, 26 February 1829, groom Ioannes «Kesel» of «bucc?ensi»; **Trsat**: image 154/155 left, 23 January 1821 (written «1824»), «Francisci Cergner ex Corochia Dersachiensi(?)», unsettled; Trieste, Pisino, Lovran, Volosca, Rukavac, Clana in single entries. **Hreljin and Kraljevica: none.** No place word was read as a person's name.

**Not zoomed, named, not excluded** (read at page size by the readers; each begins Fra-, Kal-, Cal-, Kul- or Pauz): image 115 right (9 February 1831, witness «Andrea **Cabeich/Cabich**»); image 118 left (25 May 1833, a margin witness «**Calich**»); image 147 left («Jacobus **Kalnich** pul Milohari», 10 July 1815); image 148 left (26 November 1816, «Chinchella **Calika/Galiha**», and 9 January 1817 «Colcich/Coleich»); image 130 left (14 February 1841, the **Pauz Fabay/Falay** above); image 165 left (3 February 1828, witness «Giuseppe **Calich**», and «Francetich/Franceelich»); image 151 left (15 February 1819, witness «Joanne **Fran..hich**»); image 145 left and right (31 January and 6 August 1814, witness «Josephus **Kavin/Kacin**»; 1 April 1815 «Josephus Cassin/Caffin»); image 159 right (3 February 1823, «Calcich», zoomed by the reader; 16 October 1823, the surname of Antonius Mohorcich «Colipar/Calipar»); image 168 left (24 October 1829, an entry cut at the edge of the crop: «Matthaeo filio Andreae Stefan flumin/sis»: Fiume or a surname); images 10 right (15 February 1808, groom «Josephus Gregorius Calcich» of 45 and «Fiamin»), 12–17 (p. 27, 9 June 1811, groom Andreas «Fran-/Dana», and p. 18, 4 February 1809, a bride «Kalinich(?)»). Many other cells were read once at page size.

**Gaps, not nils.** **This is a reader pass, not a walk, and the roll is not recorded as walked.** Images 0–3 and 170–174 are slates, covers and loose leaves; images 29–114 are circulars (not marriages), seen at page size. Image 96 left is a ghost page (show-through only) and 169 right is blank. The entries under the loose leaves of images 120–131 are covered by the leaves; I saw the leaf entries and the visible part of the 1806 base page, not the base page of 1835 beneath. The readers' printed page numbers do not run through the roll (the later images are numbered 219–298, the earlier 1–51), so a page number here is the reader's, not mine. A name in one of the unzoomed cells above is not excluded by this pass, and **no cell was compared between the 1806–1819 run of images 4–29 and the 1806–1831 run of images 133–169**.

**Atlas.** `cover` exits 0 for **Defranceschi**, **Kovačina** and **Kalanj**; the terms the readers were given: Defranci, Defranca, Defranceschy, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, plain Franceschi, any cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. **Nothing was added to the Atlas catalogue by this pass**: «Kalag/Kulag» and «Pauz ?llag» are readings I could not settle, not spellings a clerk was seen to write for the family. This follows the Kastav marriage book of 1729–1806 (9R2Z-GPT) and the Kastav births and deaths of 1700–1905; the marriage books 9R2Z-JWB (1819–1881), 9R2Z-ZNL (1881–1912) and 9R2S-44C are not opened.

sections.lab: Kastav marriages 1819–1881 (9R2Z-JWB), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav roll 9R2Z-JWB, two marriage books of 1819–1848 and 1842–1881: nothing of Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj settled, no child of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua 60 and no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi; a family called «Puuž Kalaz» of Puuži, written without an n; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The second Kastav marriage roll (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2Z-JWB**, roll 50 of the Croatian State Archives, **298 distinct images, 0–297**) was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first slate to the last target. It is **two books on one roll**, and I did not compare them: **Item 4, «Vjenčanih 1819–1848»** (a typed archive card on image 3 gives «Liber copulatorum», 95 leaves): **images 0–5** are slates, a target, the cover, the pastedown and the card; the register is a printed Latin «Liber Copulatorum» table from **page 1, 17 January 1819 (image 4 = ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-PPPC)** through **images 84–86 (1841, pages about 160–165)**, **image 87 blank**, **images 88–89 (1842, pages 166–169, running Latin prose, one paragraph an entry, the house column empty)** and **images 90–95 (pages 170–181, 4 February 1843 – 27 February 1848)** to **image 96 (last spread: 8 entries of 27 February – 15 July 1848, one of 25 August 1848 and two Italian consent declarations of 5 and 27 October 1848; ark 3:1:3QSQ-G99X-PGLW)**. **Images 97–101** are slates (End of Item, roll 50; the Item 4 title; the Item 5 slate «1842–1883»), a resolution target and the covers of the next book. **Item 5, «1842–1883»**: **images 102–292** are a printed Latin «Liber Copulatorum» table, **page 1, 25 January 1842 (image 102 = ark 3:1:3QS7-899X-PPZ7)** to **page 229, 19 November 1881 on image 292**; the left half of a spread holds the groom, the bride and the groom's father, the right half the rest; one hand through a run of parish priests (Josephus Pobar to 1847, then **Aloys Vlach**). **Image 293** is an end-of-roll slate and a title slate «Vjenčanih 1842–1883, Item 5» for the next roll, **image 294** the Croatian end slate «KRAJ», roll 50, filmer Božidar Vrban, «NASTAVAK na mikrofilmskom svitku br. 51» (continued on roll 51), and **images 295–297** a resolution target, an «END OF ROLL» target and blank grey leader (image 297 = ark 3:1:3QS7-899X-PGSQ). **The two books overlap in date (1842–1848) and I did not compare Item 4 pages 166–181 with Item 5 pages 1–60**; so I do not say whether they are two copies or two registers. **I did not open roll 51**; the register here stops at 19 November 1881, and the slate's «1883» is the next roll's to show.

**Photographed more than once.** Images **168–173** show **one spread six times** (a page of 1857 with entries of 18–23 February 1857, 17 marriages; the loose papers differ by image: an envelope to Vlach, a German letter from Rukavac of 27 August 1866, witness slips of June–November 1857); images **204–211** show the **page of 3 February – 16 October 1864 (entries 21–39) again and again** with different loose papers laid on the right page (an envelope «Br. 37» of Castua, a Croatian letter of 15 September 1887, a Veprinac letter «Br. 133» of 22 November 1882, a Latin banns list of October 1882, a Fiume letter of 4 December 1882); image **242** repeats page 180 with a loose Estratto of Fiume, 3 June 1883. Which entries of 1864 (22–37) are hidden by the loose leaf on images 210 and 211 is in the readers' notes; the same rows were read on the others. **Not counted twice**: the entries of those repeated images were read once as one spread. (The readers' page numbers are theirs: two reports meet at printed page 120 of 1857, and page 206 of 1875–76 is printed on two images; neither was reconciled.)

**Result: nothing of the three families settled, in any role.** No Defranceschi form and no cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran- was seen in any register image (4–96 and 102–292; every Fran- cell a given name or another surname); **no marriage, witness or note of a child or a daughter of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua house 60** (Constantinus Antonius Josephus, born 1789, and any sibling), the extra target of this pass; **no Kovačina**; **no Kalanj**. **Castua house 60 appears as a number in four marriage cells and in none is it a Defranceschi**: a bride Catharina Marotti of Castua 60 (the reader of images 126–131 dates it 24 November 1847, the reader of images 120–125 files a «Marotti, house 60» under 1847 no. 22; I have not settled whether these are one entry or two); a bride **Helena Marotti** «Sarbix» of Castua 60 on page 150, entry 37, 31 August 1864; a bride **Vincentia Dukich Pauletich** of Castua 60, 25 October 1865 (entry 46); and, **not Castua**, entry 51 of 26 November 1827 (image 37 right, page 67, which I looked at myself): the house column reads «Cuchie(?) 60», a village and its number. **No priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi**: the Josephus of the roll are the parish priest and administrator **Pobar** (1822–1847), the canon **Josephus Benedictus Rubessa**, **Josephus Sichich/Si?kich**, **Josephus Duchich** (parish priest, 1841–44) and **Joseph Dukić** (a pensioned parish priest, 1871–74), the cooperator **Josephus Voda**, the chaplain at Rukavac **Joseph Jane/Janc** (1854–1879, by delegation), **Joseph Sinkovič** (1868) and the visiting **Josephus Jong/Jur?/Jus?** (1854, 1869).

**A family written without an n, not counted: «Puuž Kalaz» of Puuži (written «Pausi» in 1840), house 72.** One family, by-named after the village word Pauz/Puuz/Puux/Puuž, appears in this book from 1840 to 1872 under a second word that is **Kalaz, Kalag, Kallaz, Kalay, Kalac** and never has an **n**: *image 81 left (page 154), 19 February 1840, entry 21 — **my own level-13 look, three times enlarged***: «Matthaeus f. Andreae **Pauz(?) Kalaz** et Helena n. Pauz», «Pausi 72», the father's assent noted, the bride Maria dau. of Matthaeus Sepich Mastoncich; this is the **same marriage as the loose leaf of the Kastav roll J43 (image 128, 16 February 1840, «Andreas Pauz ?llag/?llay assensit …», entry 5)**, so the smudged first letter of the J43 cell is a K and its word is Kalaz/Kalag (inf; the three-day difference between 16 and 19 February is not resolved), and the J43 cell of 21 November 1836 («K?lag») is probably the same family (inf); *readers, page scale, not enlarged by me*: January 1842, page 167, «Joannis **Puus Kalay**» twice, a witness «Joanne Puus **Kollay**» and «Andreae Puus Kalay» (Kalay or Kolay unsettled); 3 February 1847 (image 123 left, page 43, entry 2) the groom «Antonius Pauz / **[looped initial]caluz**» and his father «Ioannes Pauz / [looped initial]calay» (Pauši 63: the loop read as S, so Scalaz or an ornate Kalaz, open); *readers' level-13 or 3× zooms*: **14 February 1849** (image 133, page 63, entry 28) the bride «Maria **Puux Callaz**», house Puuži 72, father «Andreas Puux Callaz», mother «Helena Puux»; **28 November 1860** (page 135, entries 37 and 40) the groom «Matthaeus Puuz Ka-/laz», the bride «Margaretha Puuz Ka-/laz», the father twice «Andreas Puuz **Kalag**» (g or z unsettled); **6 February 1861** (page 136, entry 9) the groom «Andreas Puuz Kal-/lak» (k or z), the father «Ioannes Puuz **Kallaz**», a witness «Mathias Puuz Kallag»; **14 July 1869** (page 172, entry 48) «Franciscus Punz **Kalae**»; **23 November 1870** (page 179, entry 88) «Ioannes Puuž **Kalac(e?)**»; **29 November 1871** (entry 106) the bride «Maria Puuz **Kalac**» and her father Joannes (K-a-l-a-c at 3×); **1872** (page 191 left, entry 87; page 191 right, entry 95 «Kala?», č or ē) groom and father **Kalac / Pauž-Kalac**. **This is not a Kalanj and I do not say it is related to one**: the Atlas Kalanj family holds Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn and the forms seen on the Ledenice, Bakar and Novi books, **none without its n**, and the Atlas family does not list Kalaz, Kalag, Kallaz, Kalac or a plain Kalay among the forms to search (the readers were given them as near-names to report; they are not catalogued). Other Puuž/Pauž entries the readers read (for example 1844–45, 1851–52, 1857, 1862–66) carry no second word.

**Near-names read by readers, none counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj family): **Kalčić** in several spellings throughout (Calcich, Calich, Galcich, Kalich, Kaliči, Kalitich, Kalinić, Kalić, Katić; zoomed: Antonius/Andreas Kalich of Bernasi 55 on 2 March 1859, Kalčich 29 January 1862 and 1866, Antonius Kalčič 6 November 1867, Maria Kalić 24 November 1875), **Kukan/Kukanić/Kukaljan** (Ku-, zoomed 1867, 1871, 1876), **Kovačić**, Kovasich, **Francetich/Francetić**, Franul-type (Franulić 1876, Fri-zul 1820), Frankovich/Frankovic, Franelich/Francelich, Franovac/Franovec, Frančičić, Franko, Franko-/vich, Mulaz/Mullaz, Kalin/Kalir (page 167, 1868), «Perich alias **Kale-stria**» (page 66, 1 August 1827, reader-zoomed), «Stephanus ?rcovina» (page 35, 1823, a flourish for the initial), Smokvina, Destefano, Dekman, Carlevaris/Calavaris, Calegaris, Collakio. **Places named in cells:** **Draga** (a witness «Ex Draga», 28 November 1827; «**Borine 69, in Parochia S. Antonii Draghae**», 1 June 1842, page 7, a groom of that surname — I looked at the page image, not enlarged; «Villa Draxiga» 23 October 1843; Petrus Paulatich of «Draga superior» 25 November 1852; Valentinus Baretincich, house 17, 26 November 1856; «Draguch Castua commorans» 18 November 1857; a Peričić of Draga 11 October 1862; the bride Ursula Grozić of Draga 40, 17 April 1877; Matthaea Pauletić ex Draga, 17 October 1877); **Bakar/Buccari** (22 June 1842, page 7, the domicile cell «… sub Parochia Buccari», looked at not enlarged; Stanislaus Margitich of «Bucari», 16 February 1852; Krasica of the parish of Bakar, 22 October 1862; Franciscus Josephus Buonconpagni of Buccari, 7 March 1859); **Trsat** (a Czergnar, 19 January 1831; Marcus Philipovich of «Tersattum/Sersattum», 27 November 1848, T or S unsettled); **Hreljin** (Casimirus Grubisich, 22 February 1854; «Ex Hreljin nunc in Zamet», 21 July 1875; «Plase ad Par. Hrelja», 29 September 1869, unsettled; a customs clerk «Rehglini et Drag…» on page 163, entry 44, 1841, cut at the foot of the crop, **not enlarged**); **Kraljevica: none**. Fiume (Flumen, «Territorium fluminense», «Plase par. flumin.») in many cells, Pola, Koper, Trieste, Veprinac, Volosko, Abbazia, Lovran, Rukavac, Zamet in single entries. No place word was read as a person's name.

**Not zoomed, named, not excluded** (read at page size by the readers; each begins Fra-, Kal-, Cal-, Kol-, Pau-, Pa- or Ka?-): image 91 left (26 November 1843, a second witness «Andreja **Kalew?i**», ends -wi or -ui); image 78 right (4 November 1839, entry 51, a witness «**Kalbau**»); image 105 left (page 7: the Draga and Bakar cells of 1842 above); the two Kollay/Kalay cells of January 1842 and the 1847 «[loop]caluz/[loop]calay» cell; the J43 cell of 14 February 1841 («Pauz Fabay/Falay», J43 image 130), which I did not look up here by date (the readers of images 78–83, to February 1841, report no other Kalay/Kalaz form); the Kal-/Ka?- cells **«Kalin/Kalir»** (page 167, 1868), **«Ka?zin/Katzin»** and **«Kalzin»** (brides of Castua 53 in 1873 and Castua 48 in 1880), **«K?lana»** (page 206, 12 January 1876, a Kocevar bride's domicile), **«Ka?ić»** (page 195, 1873, t or l), **«?alich»** (page 108, 30 October 1854, K or W/V), **«?alkasić/hotkapel»** and **«Luca Kalić?»** (a banns sheet of 1882 on image 209, crop level), the 1881 «**Ka…ić**» of page 228; a Fran- witness «**Franciscus ?aiich**» (page 148, entry 84, 1863), a groom and father «**Joannes/Antonius Frank…**» on page 226 (inserted row 76, year 1881 or «1887»), «Fian/Franjin Findez» (page 43, 29 June 1824), «Franc./Franz D?r…Sieb?ch» (image 58 left, 25 November 1833), «Fri-zul» (page 13, 9 September 1820); the priest cells «Josephus Jong/Jur?/Jus?/Jane?/Ivan?» whose surnames are cut or unsettled; and the many Calcich/Calich witnesses of 1820–1835 (pages 8, 12, 18, 25, 40–47, 54, 63, 90–99, 106–107, 113, 124), all «Kalčić» in the readers' notes, none enlarged by me. Many other cells were read once at page size.

**Gaps, not nils.** **This is a reader pass, not a walk, and the roll is not recorded as walked.** The 1842 prose pages (images 88–89) and pages 170–181 (images 90–95) have the right-hand witness and condition column cut off on the left pages; month cells on pages 88 and 92 (1830) and 64–65 (1827), an «August» on page 124 and an entry on page 135 are approximate; the page numbers of Item 4 are the readers' own. Two exposures of the page of 1864 hide mothers, brides' parents and witnesses under a loose leaf. **Item 4 (1842–1848) and Item 5 (1842–1848) are not compared**, nor is **roll 51**. A name in one of the unzoomed cells above is not excluded by this pass. **My own enlarged cell is only image 81 left (19 February 1840)**; the other «zoomed» cells above are the readers' own enlargements, which I did not repeat.

**Atlas.** `cover` exits 0 for **Defranceschi** (the printed leads not typed: Dafranceschi, Deffranceschi, Defrancaschi, Defrancejchi, Defranceshi, Defrancesshi, Defrancischi, Defrancoschi, Defrancschi, Dofranceschi, Sefranceschi), **Kovačina** and **Kalanj**; the terms the readers were given: Defranci, Defranca, Defranceschy, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, plain Franceschi, any cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. **Nothing was added to the Atlas catalogue by this pass**: «Kalaz/Kalag/Kallaz/Kalac» is a by-name of a Puuži family seen without an n, not a spelling a clerk was seen to write for the Kalanj family, and nothing about a person goes in. This follows the Kastav marriage books of 1729–1806 (9R2Z-GPT) and 1806–1841 (9R2Z-J43); the marriage books 9R2Z-ZNL (1881–1912) and 9R2S-44C are not opened.

sections.lab: Kastav marriages 1881–1912 (9R2Z-ZNL), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav roll 9R2Z-ZNL, the marriage books of November 1881 to December 1912: Emma Defranceschi, schoolmistress of Kastav, marries Ferdinand Kleinmayer on 12 March 1893 (her parents, the late Philippus Defranceschi and Josepha Kalin, and her house, Sugulj 83); and three Kalanj of Klenovica, children of Josephus Kalanj and Anna Miletić, marry at Kastav in 1899, 1907 and 1908 — the first is the Josephus baptised at Ledenice on 19 September 1871. No Kovačina, no child of Vincentius Blasius of Castua 60; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The third Kastav marriage roll (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2Z-ZNL**, roll 51 of the Croatian State Archives, project CRO 00008, **452 images, 0–451**) was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, and the last two images by me. It continues the book that stopped at 19 November 1881 on the previous roll, and holds **three books**: **images 0–5** slates and targets (taken as such, not read for entries); **Item 1, «Vjenčanih 1842–1883»**, **images 6–21**: the printed Latin «Liber Copulatorum» table from **page 230 on image 6 (Nov 1881, entries 56–72; ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-PDDH)** to **entry 101 of 29 November 1883 on image 21 (ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-PFC2)**, with the 1884 heading and two **cancelled** entries struck through at the foot; the hand changes at entry 65 of 22 November 1882 (image 11, page 235), still Latin, the parish priest **Aloys Vlach**; **images 22–23** the end-of-item slate, the Item 1 slate (1842–1883), the filmer's data slate (Vrban Božidar, Zagreb, 26 November 1996) and the Item 2 slate; **image 24** a resolution target, **images 25–26** the cover (label «275 (K4) 206») and the inside board («Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1884–1904, Inv. br. VI (206)»); **Item 2, «Vjenčanih 1884–1904»**, **images 27–207**: «VI. Liber Copulatorum», a printed two-page table (the groom and bride on the left, the parents, witnesses, the dispensation numbers and the priest on the right), Latin headings and forenames, Croatian surnames and, from the 1890s, witnesses' trades in Croatian, to **29 August 1904 on page 212 (image 207; ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-PXN7)**; **images 208–212** the end slate of Item 2, the microfilm slate, the Item 3 slate («Vjenčanih 1904–1912»), a target, the cover («275 (K4) 207») and the inside board with a blank flyleaf; **Item 3, «Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1904–1912», Inv. br. VIII (207)**, **images 213–450**: the printed Latin form «Liber matrimoniorum celebratorum in parochia S. Helenae – Kastav anno 190_», five marriages to a page, the year's last digit written in, Latin forenames and Croatian surnames and trades, dates written «17. Jan. 1879», the groom's and bride's birthplace, house and birth date given ; **image 450** (ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-PD1G, **looked at by me, page scale**) is page 237, the last: 30 November – 28 December 1912, entries 145–146, the rest blank; **image 451** is the «END OF ITEM» target, roll 51. **Not reconciled:** the readers' page numbers for the first images of Item 3 (213–215 called pages 1–3) differ by one from the offset the later images show (image 312 = page 99, 438 = page 225, 450 = page 237); and which entries of 1904 lie under the paper slip pasted on image 203 (a note of 13 February 1904 about Rubeša and Frlan) was not settled. Of the **Item 1** pages the readers say the entry dates on pages 230–231 follow the order of the banns, not the weddings.

**Emma Defranceschi, schoolmistress of Kastav, married on 12 March 1893.** *Image 101, entry 23, printed page 119 (ark 3:1:3QS7-899X-PXY4), enlarged by me at level 13, the bride's cell and the parents' cell*: the groom **Ferdinandus Kleinmayer**, *Geometra communalis*, Kastav, 33, bachelor, the son of the late *Josephus Kleinmayer, civilis*, and Josepha (her maiden name read «Grossl»-like by a reader, unsettled); the bride «**Emma Defranceschi, Magistra Scholae**», 31, unmarried, Kastav, house cell «**Sugull / Sugulj 83**» — the village word is Sugulj, not «Castva» and not house 60; her parents «***defuncti Philippus Defranceschi, possessor***» and «***Josepha Kalin***»; the witnesses «***Josephus Kalin***» (*possidens*) and a Franciscus whose second word a reader could not settle, with «Općinski glavar» (the mayor) beside; documents «Acta Matrimonialia sub N. 69, 77, 84, 97 de 1893»; the parish priest **Antonius Turak**. **doc.** She was therefore born about 1861–62 (inf, from the age). **What it settles:** the Kastav burial of 5 April 1904 (image 286 right, page 646, entry 61, told above) names her as the mother of Fridericus Maria Petrus Kleinmayer, born 23 February 1897, and the archive then said that **which Defranceschi family Emma belonged to was not known**. **Now it is: the family of the late Philippus Defranceschi, a landowner of Kastav (Sugulj 83), and Josepha Kalin** (doc). The index's «Ferdinandi De Franceschi» for the child's burial put the surname on the father, the page puts it on the mother, as the earlier page said; and the register file's «Ferdinandus Kleinmager, born 1854» does not agree with the age of 33 the page gives in 1893 (born about 1859–60): which is wrong I have not checked. **Two things the pass does not square.** The Kastav births of 1837–1882 (9R28-L24, read once by readers for the three names) recorded **no Defranceschi baptism**, though a girl born in the parish about 1861–62 should stand there (two of its pages, 360 and 614, are unread): so either Emma was born elsewhere or the pass missed her. And **neither Kastav death pass (1774–1882, 1883–1905) recorded Philippus**, who was dead by March 1893: he died elsewhere, or the passes missed him; neither pass is a walk. **What it does not settle:** who Philippus was (no roster row names him, and the earlier Kastav passes were not looking for the given name Philippus, so that is not a nil); how he stands to the Defranceschi of Castua house 60 and to the marriages of 1744, 1751 and 1788 told above; and whether Emma had brothers (the witness Josephus Kalin is her mother's kin or her mother's brother — the page does not say). **Not a Kalanj and not a near-name for this archive's Kalanj family:** Kalin is Josepha's own maiden name, read letter for letter K-a-l-i-n at level 13 (it is also a near-name the readers were told to report). **No other Defranceschi stands in any cell of the roll**: the readers were given the Sugulj 83 family, the names Philippus, Josephus Kalin and Josepha Kalin and Emma as targets for every later chunk (images 102–449), and none of them recurs. The house number 83 appears once more, as «Castua 83», for the bride Rubeša Maria Albina, born 4 April 1888 (images 264–269, entry 39, 1906): a different surname, a house-number coincidence only, not counted.

**Three Kalanj of Klenovica, children of Josephus Kalanj and Anna Miletić, marry at Kastav; the first is the Josephus the Ledenice baptism book sent to his wedding.** (1) *Image 157 (ark 3:1:3QSQ-G99X-PXDY), page 164, entry 77, 4 November 1899; my reader's level-2× crops of both halves, the groom's and parents' cells, the spelling plain Kalanj with a hook on the j*: the groom «**Josephus Kalanj**», *operarius*, domicile **Zamet 192**(?) (last figure unsettled), «natus **Klenovica** 23(?)» (number unsettled), «Parch: **Ledenice**», born **19 September** 187- (the year digits are not settled in the cell), unmarried; the bride **Anna Dučić**, *famula*, Zamet 192, «nata Hume 51», born 12 August 1879(?); his parents «***Josephus Kalanj, rusticus***» and «***Anna Miletić***», hers «Petrus Dučić, agricola» and «Helena Mihačić»; the witnesses Josip Host (status written «Kalafat», a trade, not a surname) and Mate Marčelja; the documents «V. Act. Matr. 259, 260, 294, 227»; the parish priest **Michael Laginja**. **doc** for the cells, **inf** for what follows.
