(2) *Image 312, page 99, entry 132 of 1907, 30 November 1907 (ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-PX9F), the reader's crops of both halves*: the groom «**Kalanj Antonius**», *faber serrarius*, born **Ledenice / Klenovica 22**, **17 January 1879**, political commune Crikvenica («Cirkvenica»), parish Ledenice, 28, bachelor; the bride Marija Ćikovič, *operaria*, of Turčići 24, born 9 December 1879; his parents «***Kalanj Josephus*** agric. / ***Anna n: Miletić***»; the witnesses «Joseph. Kalanj, operar.» and Vinc. Ćikovič, *murator*; banns at Castua 10, 17 and 24 November; the parish priest Franc. Ryšlavý. (3) *Image 323, page 110, entry 53, 1 June 1908 (ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-P6Y4), the reader's crops, which I looked at*: the bride «**Kalanj Catharina**», *operaria*, born **Klenovica 22**, «(Croatia)» **19 June 1876**, commune Crikvenica, domicile Zamet, 32, unmarried, with the groom Tibljaš Petrus, *operarius*, born Pola 71, 1 May 1879, of Zamet 199; her parents «***Kalanj Josephus*** agric. / ***Anna n: Miletić***»; the witnesses Franković Emilij and «Kalanj Joseph.»; banns at Castua, Sv. Križ and Fiume; the officiant Gabrielić Joannes, cooperator, by delegation. **What the three entries show together (doc):** one father, Josephus Kalanj, *agricola*, and one mother, Anna Miletić, on three marriage entries 1899–1908, all with Klenovica house 22 as a child's birth house in two of them; and **a Josephus Kalanj of Klenovica, called a witness («Joseph. Kalanj») in 1907 and 1908**, probably the groom of 1899 or his father, not settled (inf). **What they tie to what the archive already held (inf):** (a) the **Ledenice births 1861–1894**, told above, hold «a **second Josephus Kalanj**, with **Anna Miletić**» at house 22 with children in 1871, 1874, 1876 and 1881, and the **Josephus born on 19 September 1871** carries a later note that a baptismal certificate was issued to him on **24 June 1899** «*vjenčanja radi*» (for his wedding). The **groom of 4 November 1899** has the same father's and mother's names, the same day and month of birth (19/9), the same village and parish; the certificate of June 1899 was issued for **this marriage**, five months before it. It was **not** for the Crikvenica marriage of 22 January 1899 (Josip Kalanj, born 5 May 1871, of Ledenice house 37, son of Josip and **Rosalija Perković**, told above), which is the *other* Josip of 1871. The earlier page said the Josip who married at Crikvenica rests on his parents as that entry names them; this entry now does the same for the Josephus of 19 September. (b) The **Kastav death book of 1883–1905** (image 253 right, entry 199, told above) holds **Augustina (Maria) Kalanj, daughter of Josephus and Anna née Dučić, of Zamet 117, dead on 29 July 1902 aged ten months**; the earlier page claimed no tie to any Kalanj. **Her parents' names are those of the groom and bride of 4 November 1899, and the child fits their marriage (inf)**; the house numbers differ (192 in 1899, 117 in 1902; the 1899 figure is unsettled) and the entry of 1902 does not name Klenovica. (c) The 1907 groom's birth date, **17 January 1879**, is **not** among the Ledenice births the earlier page listed for the couple (1871, 1874, 1876, 1881): either that pass missed a baptism, the child was baptised elsewhere, or the groom's date is wrong; and the birth date of 19 June 1876 for Catharina **was not compared** with the child of 1876 I have in the Ledenice notes (the name and day are not in my text above). Both are checks on the Ledenice births 1861–1894 book, not done here. **What it does not tie:** these are **not** the Josip and Rosalia Perković of Klenovica house 22 whom the archive follows for Ana Kalanj's wife-line — Rosalia is a different woman from **Anna Miletić**, and the Ledenice marriage book of 9 October 1870 (told above) shows **Josephus Kalanj, Povile 22, aged 29, and Anna Miletić of Povile 19** marrying: this is the Anna Miletić of the roll. The coincidence of house number 22 is the only link to Perković and I do not claim it.

**No Kovačina, no child of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua 60, no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi.** Not one cell of the roll (every groom, bride, parent, mother's maiden name, witness and priest of images 6–449) was read as a Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina or Kovachina. **Castua or Kastav 60** in the village-and-house column appears only once: *«Baćić Anastasius, Vinc. purgator caminorum»* (a chimney-sweep), «born Kastav 60, domicile Kastav 60», page 66, entry 109, 21 October 1906; **Baćić, not a Defranceschi**; and Kastav 59 and 53, 54, 41 and others belong to other surnames. **Priests called Josephus**, all chaplains or cooperators by delegation from the parish priest, none a Defranceschi: **Josephus Tanc** (Cap., 1883, zoomed), **Josephus Jane** (Cap., 1884), **Josephus Petrak/Petrák** (chaplain of Zvonećа and Rukavac, 1893–1912 on a long run of pages), **Josephus Vodička** (chaplain of Rukavac, 1896–1901) and a **Josephus Podlečka/Podlitka** (1893–94, the spelling moves), **Josephus Prdička(?)** (1897, the surname unsettled), **Josephus Aničić** (chaplain, 1902–1912), **Josephus Miličić** (cooperator, 1905–06), **Josephus Lukšić** (chaplain, 26 August 1912). The **parish priests** seen are Aloys Vlach (1881–82), Antonius Turak (the 1890s), Michael Laginja (1899), Antonius Ellner (1905–1907) and Franc. Ryšlavý (1907–), with **Dr. Andreas Rački, parish priest of Trsat** (written Tersati, Tersat, Tersacti), marrying by delegation between 1907 and 1910 (the word Tersati was read at page scale and is not settled for the first). **Places in cells that bear on the Kvarner questions:** **Trsat** only as the officiant's parish (above) and in a note «Copulati Tersacti» (20 November 1912); **Rijeka** (Flumen, Fiume, Rieka, «Plase … S. Nicolo») in a number of entries each year; **Pola** (Tibljaš's birth, 1879, above; Valerianus Dukić, 1895; page 225, 1912); **Zamet, Rukavac, Matulji, Veprinac, Volosko, Opatija and Klenovica** often. **Draga and Bakar do occur, in single entries, and none is a target name** (reader readings; the 1908 cell I did not enlarge): a groom Joannes Krivičić of «Oslići 8 (par. **Draga**)», 23 January 1884 (item 2, entry 2; the same marriage is entered and struck through on image 21 as «pri Draguć», unsettled); a bride Maria Pavletić of «**Kratice (Bakar)** 91», 20 February 1884 (entry 20, zoomed by a reader); a groom Philippus Pavletić whose place cell reads «Bukar/Rukar» (page 140, entry 22, 23 February 1897; unsettled between Bakar and Rukavac); a groom Natalis Ciganović, locus «**Draga**» 52/48 jug., 19 November 1902 (page 193, entry 75; which Draga is not settled); a groom Pascotto of «Draga 49 / Azzano / Udine», 2 October 1904 (image 215, entry 81: the Draga of Friuli, banns «Castua / Draga / Italia»); a groom Pajek resident at **Bakar**, 19 November 1905 (page 38, entry 103, banns «Castua / Pola / Bakar»); a bride Mohorovičić Maria, born «**Bakarska Draga St. Antonii**, Croatia», 10 May 1886, commune Bakar, 21 November 1908 (image 337, page 124, entry 120, a reader's zoom); a groom Senac Joannes born «Draga 36, Croatia», commune Sušak, 24 July 1909 (entry 78); and **Kraljevica** once: a groom Franciscus Balthasar Gauš, merchant, «Volosko 24 / Kraljevica 110», 4 July 1903 (entry 60), his father a *nauta*. **Hreljin: none.** (One officiant's place, «a parocho Bu?-ca?ensi» on page 134, 1896, may read Buccarensi; unsettled.)

**Near-names read by readers, none counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj family): **Kalčić** in many cells in every hand (Kalcic, Kalucic/Kalcic Antonius 1887, Josephus Kalčić 1884, 1901 and 1907, Helena Kalčić 1883 and 1903, Lucas and Joannes Kalčić of Berguđ 1882), **Kalić** (Joannes Srok Kalić 1881, Anton Kalić 1903), **Kalinić** (Margharetha 1906, page 64), **Kalister** (Zalog, Carniola, 1898), **Kalafat** (a trade written after a witness's name, 1883 and 1899), **Kalc** (Franciscus Kalc of Kuteževo, 1906), «Kallmünz» (Bavaria, 1906), **Kalan** with no j (page 171, entry 65, 15 June 1910: Josepha n. Kalan, the mother of Ostrogović Josephus; reader's zoom K-a-l-a-n; not a form in the Atlas Kalanj family, and **nothing was added**), **Kalac** and **Halac** (the Puuži by-name of the previous roll, again written without an n: «Kalac Joseph., operarius», a witness, image 306, 16 November 1907; «Catharina n. Halac» of Hum, image 290, 6 February 1907; a groom's father with a smudged first word «…eus Kalac», image 6 left, 23 November 1881), **Kalzin/Katzin/Kalin** (Castua 53, 1882; **Kalin** is also Emma's mother's name, above), **Kukan/Kukanić/Kukuljan/Kukavić** (Ku-), **Kovač, Kovačić, Kovačević, Kavčić** (Kovačić Joanna of Brdoc 1906, Kovačić Jacobus 1907, Kovač Nicolaus of Mostar 1904, Josephus Kovačević 1902), **Francetić, Franković/Frankovich/Franki** (Zorica-Camilla Franki, schoolmistress, 1912), **Franulić/Fanulić**, Franko, Frank, «**De Castro**» (Dominicus De Castro, a witness, 1884: De- but not Fran-), **Kinkela, Puž/Puži** (a surname and a village, no second word, no Kalac). Mohorovičić, Pavletić, Ciganović, Senac, Gauš and Pajek are surnames of those entries, seen for their places and not counted.

**Not zoomed, named, not excluded** (read at page scale by the readers; each begins Ka-, Kal-, Kol-, Fra-, Dei-, Pau- or has a first letter unsettled): image 7 left, 13 February 1882, **Josephus Ka(?)l-/zin and father Antonius Kalzin(?)** of Castua 53 (the letters after Kal are z or j, then -in); image 6 left, 23 November 1881, groom's father **«Ka-/turin(?)»** (page 230, entry 72); image 9 left, page 233, entry 38, 9 September 1882, the father's cell **«Joannes Ka?a(l?)-/?ić»** (K or R, zoomed twice, probably not Kal-); **«Kalmica/Kalwica»** (page 55, 4 July 1887, an annotation under «Jurčići 19», zoomed 8×, K-a-l-m/w-i-c-a, no n); image 334 left, 21 October 1908, entry 104, the groom **«?alinčić/Valenčić Natalis»** (the father's cell reads Valenčić; the first letter of the groom's cell is K or V); image 97 left, 23 November 1892, entry 64, **«Josephus Kravoč/Krawoč(?)»** of Santa Croce (a reader's zoom; could be Kovač, not settled); the priest's cell of image 444 right (entry 116, 4–11 November 1912, **«Petrak(?) Joseph.»**, first letters unsettled); the officiants **«Frankovič(?)… coop. Frsatii(?)»** (image 399 right, 16 February 1910; Trsat, not settled); the Josepha of the groom's mother of the entry of 1893 on image 101, whose maiden name a reader read «Grossl»-like; and every cell the readers read at page scale in the many hundreds of entries. **Gaps, not nils.** **This is a reader pass, not a walk, and the roll is not recorded as walked.** The 1912 book ends on image 450 at entry 146; **the pages after 1912 are in another book**; **images 0–5 and the slates and covers (22–26, 208–212, 451) were not read for entries**; the readers' count of the entries of 1883, 1893 and 1904 was not checked against any printed tally; **the two 1884 entries struck through on image 21 are cancelled; the reader quoted entry 2 only**. A name in one of the unzoomed cells above is not excluded by this pass. **My own enlarged cells are those of Emma Defranceschi (image 101, level 13); the Kalanj cells of 1899, 1907 and 1908 are the readers' own 2× or 3× enlargements, which I looked at (1908 and 1893 crops) and did not repeat.**

**Atlas.** `cover` exits 0 for **Defranceschi** (the printed leads not typed: Dafranceschi, Deffranceschi, Defrancaschi, Defrancejchi, Defranceshi, Defrancesshi, Defrancischi, Defrancoschi, Defrancschi, Dofranceschi, Sefranceschi), **Kovačina** and **Kalanj** for the terms the readers were given: Defranci, Defranca, Defranceschy, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, di Franceschi, plain Franceschi; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalan, Calan. **Nothing was added to the Atlas catalogue by this pass.** The Kalanj and Defranceschi forms on this roll are plain **Kalanj** (with the long j) and **Defranceschi**, already catalogued; Kalac/Halac/Kalan are by-names or maiden names seen without the family's n and nothing in the roll ties them to it. This follows the Kastav marriage books of 1729–1806 (9R2Z-GPT), 1806–1841 (9R2Z-J43) and 1819–1881 (9R2Z-JWB); **9R2S-44C** (births 1672–1699, marriages 1673–1699) is not opened.

sections.lab: Kastav births 1729–1776 (9R2D-4W5), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav birth book of 1729–1776: nothing of Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role, no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi, and no baptism of Vincentius Blasius at page size; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The Kastav baptism book **1729–1776** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2D-4W5**, roll 47 of the Croatian State Archives, 310 images, 0–309; the Atlas catalogues it as «Births (Rođeni) 1729-1776») was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first register page to the last. **Layout.** Images 0–2 are the filmer's slates, a resolution target and the front cover (Povijesni Arhiv Rijeka); **image 3 left** is the inside cover with the label «MATIČNE KNJIGE RIMOKATOLIKA, ŽUPA KASTAV, MATIČNA KNJIGA ROĐENIH (1729-1784), INV.BR. II.(196)» and a canon's dated notes of his own career; **the register begins on image 3 right, page 1, 2 January 1729**, and runs to about page 300 (24 April 1776) on image 304. It is a **handwritten Latin prose register**, one paragraph to a baptism (child, father, mother, the hour, the baptiser, «patrini fuerunt …»), headed by «Die … » and the month; the page numbers stand top right on the right-hand pages only, 10–20 baptisms to a page, and in blocks by baptiser (the archpriest Joannes Baptista Pobar/Dobor, the canons Tomicich, Gerbaz, Hauch/Harch, Bleich, Raicich, Cinchella, Varglien and others), so **the dates run out of order inside a page and often through two or three years of the same page**; the year digit in the headings is unreliable (the last digit reads 1735 on a long run of pages, 1747 on others, until a heading «Annus 1748»), and the dates in these notes are the readers' and mine, not the book's printed order. From **8 October 1773** the book changes to a **ruled table** (Dies, Baptizans, Infans, Parentes, Patrini, Religio, Locus, Numerus; images 282–305, from about page 278). **The end of the roll:** image 305 left is the filmer's «continued on another roll» card and 305 right the title card of the item (1729–1784); images 306–307 the Croatian State Archives slate «KRAJ … NASTAVAK NA MIKROFILMSKOM SVITKU BR: 48» (with «47» written for this roll) and a resolution target; 308 «END OF ROLL»; 309 blank film leader. **The same book goes on, on roll 48:** the next waypoint, 9R2F-C66 (read and told above), opens with the slate «ŽUPA KASTAV, MATIČNA KNJIGA RODJENIH 1729-1784, ITEM 1» and its first register page is dated 12 March 1776, so **the last dates of this roll (to 24 April 1776) and the first of roll 48 overlap**; the entries of the overlap were read on both, not compared.

**Result: nothing of the three names, in any role, in any cell the readers or I could settle.** No Defranceschi form, no Kovačina form, no Kalanj form (the terms are listed at the end), no plain Franceschi, no cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-. **Priest called Josephus:** the canon **Josephus Raicich** (written Raicich, Reicich, Roicich, Moicich; baptises from 1730 through the 1760s, a lay Vincentius Raicich, a councillor, is a sponsor in many years) and, from the early 1750s, the canon **Josephus Varglien** (Vaglien, Verglien, Vazghien, Vergliem: baptises throughout the 1760s and 1770s); neither is a Defranceschi. **The extra target of this pass, the baptism or the parents of Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi** (the man who appears in the Kastav book of 1776–1836 as a sponsor in 1787–89 and, in March 1789, as head of Castua house 60; the readers were told to look for «Vincentius» with a second name Blasius, or a child of a Defranceschi): **none at page size.** Every Vincentius the readers met is a child of other parents (Raicich, Vlach, Sirotich, Pomerich, Pobar, Carlevaris, Spinicich among them) or a father or sponsor of another name, and the one «Blasius Antonius» (image 41 right, 2 February 1734) is a child of Valentinus Tomicich, **Blasius** only as a given name; «Blasius Matthias» (image 203 right, p. 201, 2 February 1761) is a child of Matthias and Helena Gerbaz/Perlas, again a given name; no entry with the three names in the parents' cells. **This is not a nil for the man.** He is likely to have been born in the book's years (the reader brief put his birth in about 1735–1768), and a baptism at page size can miss a surname in a flourished cell; the cells that begin Fran- are named below.

**Cells I enlarged myself (level 13), three.** **Image 48 left (6 April 1735, the first entry of the page, ark 3:1:3QSQ-G99X-1XLC):** the reader had the mother as «Dnae Mattiae Franceschae/Franciscae?» and the sponsor «nata Fran[ul]?»; at level 13 the word in the mother's cell and the one at the end of the sponsor's cell («Anna Rosa eius uxor nata **Franul**») are **the same word in the same hand: Franul**, the noble family of the captains of Kastav (a child of the noble Franciscus Xaverius Hauch; inf, the same hand writes both). Not a Defranceschi form. **Image 17 left (23 March 1731, ark 3:1:3QSQ-G99X-1XXN):** patrini «Nobilis Dnus Joannes Petrus **Fran.**» with «Maria Antonia filia qm Dni Joannis Pauli Paulinich»; the surname is **abbreviated after four letters with a stop**; no particle before it, so not De-/Di-; the Franul of the captains is the likeliest (the same family sponsors in 1731–1776), but the abbreviation **is not settled and not excluded** (inf). **Image 44 left (9 January 1734, first entry):** the baptiser is written «Canico Matthaeo **Fra?ta**»: five or six letters, a flourished initial, read by the readers as Franta, Frasta, Franka, Frata and Frasca; the zoom does not choose between them; **a canon Matthaeus, not Josephus, with no particle**, not a Defranceschi form, letters not settled. (My level-13 zoom of image 87 right, 10 July 1740, earlier in this pass, settled «Defuncti», 'deceased', in the line «Mariae filiae Defuncti …»: not a surname.)

**Near-names, none counted** (none is a form in the Atlas Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj family): **Franul** (Franciscus Xaverius Franul de Weissenthurn, captain of Kastav, and his wife, as sponsors 1735 to 1776, and a son of his baptised on 30 April 1772, image 272 left), **Franta/Frata/Frasta/Franka** (the canon Matthaeus), Francovich/Frankovich, Franich/Francich/Franicich/Franichich, Francetich/Francesticich, Franticich, Franscich, Franovich, Frempich, Franelich/Francelich, Frangich/Frantich, Franko/Fraello (a godmother Margaritha filia Dni Baptistae, 1767–69, letters unsettled), Franza/Frantz (a Josephus Franza «nauta Volosce», 12 February 1776), Fravin/Framin/Fiamin, **Kalčić** in many spellings (Calich, Calcich, Celich, Colich, Kelich, Cadich), Calinich/Kalinich (image 294 left, 10 March 1775), Margan (image 82 left, 28 October 1739, «Matthaei Margan ex Draga»; Margan is a different name), Pancina, Dobrovich, Blasich (a surname, image 255). **Places in the cells (none a target):** **Draga**, as the home of the Margan above (image 82 left, 28 October 1739); **Tersatto/Trsat** (a sponsor «Antonius Seguglia Tersatensis» and a woman «ex Tersato» on image 25 left, 28 May 1732; a priest Georgius Delika at Tersatto on page 100; «ex Parochia Terrouenij», 20 May 1738, unzoomed, read as a possible Tersatto); **Fiume** as an adjective on godparents and fathers in many years («Fluminensis», 1729, 1731, 1742, 1749, 1753, 1759, 1769, 1775; a Capuchin of Fiume baptises on 13 March 1769; «Comendator Civitatis Fluminensis», 15 July 1749); Senj (1733–34), Veprinac, Volosko, Abbazia, Rukavac (the margin on image 283 left, 18 December 1773, reads a cut «Bucca/Buccar…» that could be Buccari; not read further), Grobnik, Pedena and Berseč; a child from «Dalmatia» (23 May 1753, mother unsettled) and «in Dalmatia» (1773). No Hreljin and no Kraljevica as origin.

**What this reader pass is not.** **It is a pass at page size, not a walk; the book is not recorded as walked.** The readers had no zoom (they read each page as one half-page picture); every name above is the letters as they stood at that size, and I enlarged only the three cells above and the 'Defuncti'. **Not zoomed, named, not excluded** (each begins De-, Fra-, Fr-, Kal- or a flourished Vincentij, or is a place in the margin): image 18 left (1731, first entry) the godmother «Franciscae filia qm Mathei Fra…fa/Frasa»; image 62 left (24 February 1737, godparent «Franciscina(?) Todi Hrozinensi/Herzinensi(?)», a place adjective that could be Hreljin; unzoomed); image 62 right (19 May 1737, «Lucae Giankovich», G or F); image 69 right (20 March 1738, godfather «Georgius Franich/Fr?arich»); image 70 left (20 May 1738, «ex Parochia Terrouenij»); image 77 right (3 October 1738, sponsors «Dominus Franciscus [unreadable] et Domina Francisca Gazarzki(?)»); image 82 left (28 October 1739, Margan ex Draga); image 79 right (p. 76, 21 January 1739), the godfather «Josephus Jancovich(?) Fluminensis»; image 119 left (11 February 1747, godfather «Matthias Fran?elich ex Hidena», the place unread); image 126 right (15 February 1748, sponsors «Antonius Fronzale? et Josephus Belli Zipanences/Fiumanences?»); image 142 left (Andreas son of Laurentius and Maria Pirka, patrini «Georgius Strolla et uxor relicta Matthei Srochi» and a word «fluminie/flumine»); image 152 right (1752, «Franicich/Francich»); image 156-161 (the mothers' surnames «Fravin/Framin» on 7 November 1753, 6 March and 23 March 1754, and a child's first word «Vincentius?» on 19 January 1754); image 172 left (17 November 1755, godmother «Maria filia Antonij Vaclot(?) Fluminensis(?)»); image 188 left (8 March 1758, father «Francisci Dvenaist(?)», godfather «Franciscus Dinher(?)»); image 194 left (29 January 1759, «Antonii [Furule/Jurule?] Fluminensis»); image 201 left (23 October 1760, «Matthias Franello(?)»); image 204 right (25 March 1761, a long name «Matthias V/Laurentius? Franciscus … Nepomucenus»); image 284 right (23 March 1774, «Maria uxor Josephi Fran-[?]sa»); image 287 left (29 July 1774, a soldier's regiment unreadable); image 300 right (9 November 1775, patrini «Josephus Fran[?]e/Franza(?)»); image 303 right (5 March 1776, a mother «Ka-/kan» after a struck word); and the **Fran-/Kal- cells of the reports 0–305 that are listed in the readers' notes and that I did not enlarge**, mostly Franul, Francovich, Franich, Franta and Calich. Many other cells were read once at page size. **Gaps, not nils:** images 264 and 265 are the same spread photographed twice; some pages repeat others (image 7 left and 9 left repeat entries from other pages; image 262 left and right repeat 261 left and p. 259, with a Scrobogna family slip laid over p. 259); image 258 right (p. 256) is a blank printed «Distinta Consignazione» form; image 120–125's year digits, the months written 7bris/8bris/9bris/Xbris, and a block of January 1775 struck out on image 291 left and rewritten on 291 right in a new hand with a new «Religio» column are noted in the readers' reports.

**Atlas.** `cover` exits 0 for **Defranceschi**, **Kovačina** and **Kalanj**; nothing was added to the catalogue from this book (Franul, Franta, Calinich, Kalinich and the rest were seen only as near-names, which are not evidence of a variant). **Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defranceschy, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi (plain Franceschi quoted, the decision left to me) and any cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran-; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. This is the **sixth Kastav book** read for the three names, after the deaths of 1729–1774, 1774–1882 and 1883–1905 and the births of 1776–1836 and 1837–1882; the births before 1729 (9R2D-44M) and the marriages are not opened.

sections.lab: Kastav births, marriages and deaths 1700–1728 (9R2D-44M), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: The Kastav bundle of 1700–1728 (baptisms, marriages, deaths): nothing of Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any cell a reader or I could settle, no priest Josephus who is a Defranceschi, no earlier Defranceschi generation seen; a reader pass, with the unzoomed cells named
paras: **9 November 2026.** The Kastav parish book of **1700–1728** (FamilySearch waypoint **9R2D-44M**, roll 47 of the Croatian State Archives, 207 images, 0–206; the Atlas catalogues it as «Births (Rođeni) 1700-1727 · Marriages (Vjenčani) 1700-1729 · Births 1727-1728 · Deaths (Umrli) 1713-1727 · Births 1700-1723») was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**, from the first register page to the end of the roll. It is a **bundle of several books end to end, in handwritten Latin prose** (a paragraph to an act, headed «Die … » and the month), and the readers describe the changes of book as follows (page numbers stand top right on the right-hand pages only). **Baptisms, January 1700 – 1727:** image 0 is the filmer's slate and a resolution target; **image 2 right** is the title «Praesens hic Liber Baptizatorum ac Matrimoniorum in Anno Sancto incepit … 1700, die 9 Januarii …», which names the captain of Kastav as «Dno Horatio Franceschoti» (Franceschotti, a noble family of captains, a near-name); image 4 right is page 2, 9 January 1700; the baptisms run to image 141 left (pp. 2–138), with **the parish priest Joannes Matthesich (Matesich) and the canons Blecich/Bleich, Vlah, Pober/Pobar, Paulinich, Haunel/Hauch, Tomasich/Tomicich and Staunich in parallel runs**, so the dates go out of order and one page may hold two or three years; the digits 6 and 8 are alike in the hand (entries headed «1708» on one run are 1706 by their place in the sequence), and the book runs through 1727 (the baptisms of 1727 begin at image 137, «Baptizata Adnotata huius Anni»). **Marriages, 13 January 1700 – May 1729:** **image 141 right** (page 139) begins «Liber … Matrimonium» from 13 January 1700 (image 142 is a second exposure of 141 with a label card over the lower left page); image 143 reaches February 1701, images 144–149 run 1 May 1701 – 17 June 1705, 150–155 21 July 1705 – 28 October 1709, 156–161 22 January 1710 – 28 October 1714, 162–167 1714 – November 1721, 168–173 26 October 1721 – 1 May 1727, and image 174 to 175 left May 1727 – May 1729 (Matthesich, then Pobar from 12 February 1729); about 17 entries to a page, one hand, the groom, the bride and the witnesses named. **Then, out of order:** images 175 right – 179 left (pp. 172–175) are baptisms of December 1727 – July 1728 («Sequuntur Baptizati post Festas 2 Paschae»); **image 179 right (page 176) is the first page of the DEATHS, headed «MORTI»**, December 1727 – February 1728, and image 180 holds deaths of 1728 (page 177), image 181 baptisms of April–December 1728, image 182 left baptisms, and **image 182 right (page 179) a new death book, «Liber … Mortui … 1713»** (images 183 left and right are a second exposure of 182); the deaths of **June 1713 – April 1715** are on images 184–185, **December 1714 – February 1718** on 186–191 (pp. 181–185; image 186 right carries loose tally slips), **March 1718 – January 1724** on 192–197 (pp. 186–191) and **January 1724 – December 1727** on images 198 to 202 left; a book of extra-marital baptisms of 1700–1723 (Matthesich) fills image 202 right (page 196) to 203 right, whose foot carries the first four legitimate baptisms of October–November 1728 by Canon Bleich; image 204 holds the last baptisms of 1728 (about 39 entries, page 198), **image 205 left is a page of Latin chronicle notes** (1715, 1723, 1726, 1728), 205 right is the blank end page «199», **image 206 left is the filmer's «END OF ITEM, CRO 00008, roll 47»** and **206 right the slate «Župa Kastav, Matična knjiga rođenih/vjenčanih 1700-1728, umrlih 1713-1728, ITEM 2»**. About 15–23 entries stand on a page.

**Result.** **No Defranceschi form, no Kovačina and no Kalanj in any role** (child, father, mother and maiden name, groom, bride, witness, godparent, baptiser, the deceased, a margin note) in any cell the readers or I could settle, on any of the 207 images; **no priest called Josephus who is a Defranceschi** (the parish priest is Joannes Matthesich throughout and the canons are those named above; a Josephus stands only as a child, a groom, a lay godfather, a witness or a sponsor, for instance a «Dns Josephus» godfather on image 72 right (page 70) in December 1712, a «Josephus Cragnaz/Cvagnaz/Rajcich» sponsor in 1725–26, a «Dns Joseph Ant. Staunch» godfather on 2 October 1719, and a struck «Josephus Cragnaz» on 20 March 1714). **Nothing for an earlier generation of the Defranceschi of Kastav** (the Vincentius Blasius Defranceschi of Castua 60 is met in 1787–89, on the births of 1776–1836): no «De Franceschi», «de Francesco», «di Franceschi» or any other cell beginning De-/Di- + Fran- was read in this book, and no Vincentius or Blasius with such a surname; this is a page-size reading and not a nil for him or his parents. **The captain of Kastav** in the cells is read variously Pini, Pei, Peri, Pisi (Joannes Dominicus), Heri, never Franceschotti, and Franul, the commonest Fran- near-name of the later books, does not occur.

**My level-13 zooms (saved with this archive's working notes).** **(1) Image 10 right, entry of 25 January 1701** (a baptism with the patrini «… Vicentij Calenarj/Calenanj et Fiuma uxor eius»): the sponsor's surname reads **«Calenanj»** with the letter before the j a minim or an r (unsettled which); **image 11 right, 14 May 1701** names again a sponsor, the wife of «Vicentij Calenanj» (the same letters, written once more); and **image 112 right, 31 October 1721,** a godmother «Ephemia uxor Vicentij Co?auny» (the surname begins Co- or Ca-, then one or two minims, a, u/n, y; unsettled), with the reader's «Eufemia uxor Vicentij Calcuonj» on **image 113 right, 1 January 1722** (not enlarged). It is probably **one couple from 1701 to 1722 (inf)**, a Vicentius and an Ephemia/Fiuma, and the surname is a **Cal-e-na-nj** (extra e, a second n) that is **not a Kalanj form in the Atlas family** (no such spelling is catalogued) and is **not counted**; it is a near-name, not excluded as a name of the same family either, because the two readings are not settled. **(2) Image 11 right, 10 April 1701:** the councillor «Andreae Celenach» among the patrini is plainly **Celenac**, and the recurring godfather «Laurentij Celenaz/Calenaz» of the baptisms of 1721–22 (images 108–112) is most likely the same Celenac, though those cells were not enlarged. **(3) Deaths, image 194 left (January 1720)** «Lucia filia Michaelis Lucich ?alan, aetatis annorum duorum» (a capital with a flourish before -alan, C, E or F; unsettled) and **image 196 right (13 November 1722)** «Margarita filia Michaelis **Falan** (Palan/Talan?) dicti Raldu/Kaldu, praemunita extrema unctione, anno 10»: the first letter of the second is not a K, and the baptisms of 1701 on image 10 right already hold a Georgius Falan/Felan, so this is the Falan family of Kastav, **not counted** (inf, one father Michael in both). **(4) Image 38 right (page 36), 4 October 1706,** «Margarita filia legitima Matthiae ?adan» (a capital resembling R, then a, d/l, a, n; read **Radan, Kadan or Kalan**, **unsettled, not excluded**, not counted): a Kalan reading cannot be ruled out here and the cell is named for a later sitting. **Not Kalanj on the letters:** Ku-/Cu-kulan (images 148 left, 165 left, 173 left), Kalika/Kaliha (images 177 and 178), Colcich, Covalcich, Cukunin.

**Near-names not counted** (read at page size, not enlarged unless stated): Franceschotti (the captain's title), Franceschina/Francischina (a woman's given name, images 60 left, 83 left, 97 right and 189 left), Franich/Franichich/Francich, Frankovich/Franković (several), Franić, Francovich, Fran(c)sa/Franša/Franza (a «Matthias Franc…/Franša/Francha» in the marriages of 14 January 1702 (image 144 right, as a councillor), 30 November 1702 and 1 February 1703 (images 146 left and 146 right), and a «Matthias Franz?» in the baptisms of 20 March 1703 on image 21 right), «Fran?chich alias Mladenich» (14 February 1700, image 141 right), Framin («Jacobi Framin», images 159 and 161), Francini/Franceini (image 68 left, 23 August 1712), Valentin «Francini», Ivancina/Tvancina (image 152 right, 7 March 1707; not Kovacina), Kinkella, Kukulan, «Francischina filia Matthiae Fa?» (image 60 left), and the «Petro Franci… Fluminense», a guardian of the Fiume friary in the chronicle on image 205 left (8 September 1715). **Places in cells:** Fiume (Fluminensis, several: sponsors in 1713 on image 76 left, grooms in 1703, 1704, 1706, 1708, the Collegium of Fiume «de Lopacha» on 2 March 1723, a canon of the Collegiata of Fiume in July 1719, and «filia N. Zandonati Fluminensis» on image 185 left, 11 August 1714); **Bakar** («ex Parochia Buccerensi», 29 June 1722, image 168 left, enlarged by the reader); **Trsat** («ex Tersato», 10 April 1717, image 191 left; the Tersatto of the chronicle on image 205); **Draga** («… Draga» cut at the right edge of image 139 left, 22 May 1727, **which Draga is unsettled** and the cell was not enlarged); Volosko (20 March 1714); Veprinac (1723); Novalj and Lipa (marriages 1710–14); Grobnik, Zamet and Rukavac as in the later books; no Hreljin, no Kraljevica. **Terms typed to the readers:** Defranci, Defranca, Defranceschy, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi and any De-/Di- + Fran- cell; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. The Atlas `cover` run exits 0 for all three families (Defranceschi, Kovačina, Kalanj); no spelling was added to the Atlas from this book. **Gaps, not nils:** a reader pass at page size, not a walk. **These cells were not enlarged and stay open:** image 14 left (22 January 1702, «Matthaeus Fran?a»), image 21 right (20 March 1703, «Matthiae Franz?/Franh»), image 24 right (29 January 1703, an alias «Fran…ich»), image 60 left, image 68 left, image 70 left (5 June 1713, a captain's child whose surname is illegible), images 144 right, 146 left and 146 right (the Matthias Franša/Francha cells), image 139 left (the Draga), **image 11 right, 19 May 1701, «Laurentij Kalanin/Kalamin?»** (a patrinus; a Kalan- reading is possible and the cell was not enlarged), image 201 left (28 January 1727, «Matthias filius Andreae Calunin(?) Zietich/Ledich, anno 5», Calan-type, not enlarged), image 201 right (5 May 1727, «Georgius Tancina», T or K), image 200 left (17 October 1725, a «Fran…» probably a religious), image 203 left (a margin note at 6 October 1708, «dixit ipse Pater … Franc?…nich») and the smudged lines at the foot of image 202 left (12–19 December 1727) and the inked-out line on image 201 left (20 December 1726); image 82 left (5 August 1715, «Franc?ij …»), image 99 right (3 October 1719, «filius Gregorii Fran?sa/Fraucsa») and the entries of images 90, 107, 115, 116 and 164 named by the readers as unsettled Fran- or Calan- cells. This is the **seventh Kastav book** read for the three names, after the deaths of 1729–1774, 1774–1882 and 1883–1905 and the births of 1729–1776, 1776–1836 and 1837–1882; the marriage books of 1729 onwards are not opened.

sections.lab: Bakar marriages 1691–1738, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj in the oldest Bakar marriages, and a neighbour of the name at Draga in 1727
paras: **8 November 2026.** The oldest Bakar marriage book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2C-GPX, roll 3 item 3, 134 images, 1691 to 27 November 1738) was looked at once, page by page, by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj. **None stands in any listed spelling**, in any role (groom, bride, parents, kum, priest), and no priest of the Defranceschi name; the clergy called Josef are the canon Josef Kovacich and a layman, the Rentmaster Josef Ernestus de Lebenech, neither of them a target. The book is not walked: its sponsor lists (images 7–11 left, 124 right–127) were read only at the supplied resolution, the end of the 1694 title is under the binding, and the volume goes on on roll 4, which is not opened. The unsettled cells are listed in the [searched row](/searched/) of that date.

**A neighbour of the name, not the name.** One family of the parish carries a by-name that is one vowel from Kalanić: **Stipkovich, alias Kulanich**. It appears from 1701 (a kum at the ring, 30 October; again in 1704, 1706 and, with the alias spelled out, on 8 May 1707) and in June 1715 (a groom, «Sijn P. Juanna Stipkovichia, alias Kulanichia Thoma», image 42 right; **read at level 13, the first vowel u**); on **2 June 1727**, at **Draga in S. Antun's church**, the bride Margareta is the daughter of the late «Mattea Stipko-vichia, **alias Kallanichia**» (image 71 right; **read at level 13**, a-l-l-a-n-i-c-h-i-a, the word split by the line end; groom Jakov Sop…ichia, son of Bartol; married by Luka Kovacich, canon, dean and vice-vicar); and on 2 November 1738 a «Bartola **Kullanichia** sin Jua(n)» (image 122 left, the reader's enlargement). *doc* for the words. The ending is a Croatian patronymic -ić, and the vowel moves between u and a. **No entry says Kulanić or Kallanić is Kalanj**, so the form is not in the Atlas's Kalanj catalogue and nothing on this page rests on it; it is told here so that the question is not lost if a later register writes the two together. No Kalanj is named at Bakar or Draga in these 47 years, and nothing in them touches Josip and Rosalia of Ledenice house 22.

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1650–1804: births, marriages, deaths and confirmations, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: One Martin Kal·ny «of Klenovica» in 1769, and no other cell of the name at Novi
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Novi Vinodolski volume of 1650–1804 (FamilySearch waypoint 9RK1-3Y7, roll 217, 463 images) holds four parish books and the lists bound between them: **births 1650–1786**, **marriages 1674–1786**, **deaths 1704–1782**, lists of the **confirmed** (1699 to 1770), the annual counts of communions and confessions, and, from image 376, **births 1784–1804**. Every image was looked at once, in sixes, by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj; I zoomed at level 13 the cells that could be one. **The name of this page stands in one cell only.** On **image 173, right page, 19 January 1769**, the canon Anton Kabalin baptised **Margarita**, daughter of Toma Radetić and Margarita, and the godparents are «*Martin **Kal?ny** od Klenoviśe*» and *Katarina*, wife of Marko Radetić. **Zoomed by me (*doc* for what I can see):** *Kal*, then a blot of ink over the middle, then *ny*, so the word is *Kal·ny*; the readers read it *Kalany*, and the form is one the Atlas already holds as a Kalanj spelling; the place, *od Klenoviśe*, is read at page size and is **Klenovica**, the village of house 22.

**What it is worth.** The oldest cell I have that puts a Kalanj at **Klenovica**, 89 years before Josip and Rosalia are at house 22 in the Ledenice book (1858) and 129 years before the Martin Kalanj of Klenovica who died at Rijeka on 29 November 1898, told above; a *Martin* again is a coincidence of a common name and not a thread. That it is **the same family** as house 22 is *inf* at most: the name, the village, a century. Nothing else of the name stands in the whole volume: **no Kovačina, no other Kalanj-type cell in any book or list**, in 154 years of births and 80 of marriages, in deaths to 1782 and in the births to 1804. That is the readers' count, good to about ten per cent, and a list of the near-names, the unread cells and the terms typed is in the [searched row](/searched/) of this date. **Three near-names I settled at level 13 are not Kalanj:** *Kala-/fatička od Bribira*, the widow of a Juan Kalafat, a godmother on 14 August 1744 (image 107, right page; the two halves of the word are on two lines, *Kala-* and *fatička*); *Ivan K·kaly*, 60 years old, who died on the Senj mountains in the storm of 10 December 1749 (image 305, left page; a blot over the letter after the *K*, and *kaly* on the next line: the *Kukaly* of the book, who stands there in many entries), and the *Kolanich* the readers read twice (image 408, left page, 12 January 1794, «*vulgo Kolanich*»), not zoomed by me.

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1784–1859: births, marriages and deaths read · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: Josephus «?allanj», parishioner of Ledenice, marries Catharina Merzljak in November 1841
paras: **8 November 2026.** The second Novi Vinodolski volume (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2M-82L, 573 images) holds births 1804–1852 (images 5–325), then marriages (a first book 1787–1815 from image 327, a second book 1815–1859 from image 359). The births were read to the end (images 5–325) with no Kalanj-type cell; **the marriages, read to their end (image 424, the last entry of 24 January 1859), hold one; the deaths (images 429–569) hold none.** On **image 399, left page (p. 73), entry 18, November 1841** (the date column names *Novembris 21* beside entry 17 and none beside 18), the groom is «*Josephus **?allanj** Parochianus Ledenicensis*», the bride «*Catharina Merzljak Antonii*» (a Merzljak, daughter of an Antonius), and the witnesses, in the readers' reading, *Joannes Butorac* and *Joannes Malina*, whose condition cell reads «*Confiniarius Ledenicensis, Parochianus Segniensis*».

**Zoomed by me at level 13 (*doc* for what I can see):** the word is plain from the second letter on, *-allanj*, with the *-nj* ending of the Kalanj entries elsewhere in the Ledenice books; **the first letter is a looped capital that I cannot settle between K and L** (it is shaped like the L of *Ledenicensis* in the line below; the readers took it for K). I have written it *?allanj* and counted it as a Kalanj-type cell, **not** as proof of the spelling. **What it may be (*inf*):** a man of Ledenice parish named Josip with a wife Catharina, 1841, in the parish whose Kalanj families are at house 22 and 23; the Ledenice death book of 1866–1902 has a Josip Kalanj with a Katarina at house 23 (baptisms 1847–55 of their children), the man who probably died on 28 September 1872 (told above). The name, the parish and the wife's given name agree; **that this is that couple is not established**: the mother's surname in those baptisms (Merzljak?) has not been looked for, and the groom's own surname begins with a letter I have not settled. **Not done yet, and where to look:** the Ledenice baptisms 1842–46 (the first children, and the mother's surname) in the Ledenice births 1820–61 (waypoint 9R2F-4WP), which I read for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj but not for this mother.

**Near-names in the same stretch, not counted:** *Kukalj* (many), *Kabalin* (very many, the Novi family of canons), *Kaladin / Caladin* (a witness, 1833, and 1804), and, in the births, *Antonia **Kalaj*** (godmother, 26 May 1836, image 239 left, p. 226, entry 37, «Plebea Selcensis»; zoomed at level 13, *Kalaj* plain, not Kalanj). **Not Kalanj:** the Kalaj and Kaladin cells; no form I would add to the Atlas on one cell (Atlas: nothing added). **Near-names added when the volume was finished, none counted:** *Antonius Kalinić(?) of Senj*, the father of an illegitimate child baptised 25 November 1844 (image 281 left, p. 306, entry 98; zoomed at level 13: the line breaks after *Ka-* and the rest reads *lalinić* or *linić*, ending *-nić*, not *-nj*); in the deaths, *Anna, daughter of Antonius «?kalja»*, 25 days old, 28 August 1807 (image 491 left, fol. 122; zoomed: a curled first letter, then *-kalja*, no *n*); and two baptism fathers of 1848 written across a line end, «*Joannes Ko-/Callin Petri*» (image 300 right, entry 21) and «*Lucas Ka-/Callin*» (image 301 left, entry 39), both zoomed at level 13: the first part is *Ko-* or *Ka-*, the second begins with a capital that is a *C* or a *B* in this scribe's hand; in the same book he writes the Kabalin family *Kabal-/lia* and *Kaballia* (images 301 right, entries 41 and 50), so I take them for **unsettled, probably Kabalin**, and neither counted nor excluded (*Callin* is not a form the Atlas holds, and the two cells are not enough to add one).

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1852–1874: births, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Novi Vinodolski births of 1852–1874
paras: **8 November 2026.** The third Novi Vinodolski volume on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R28-T3K, roll 84 of the Croatian State Archives, item 6; the cover is stamped *Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 357*) is one book, **«Matica kèrstna», the births of the parish church of Novi, from the first entry of 24 November 1852 on image 3 to the last of 26 December 1874 on image 260**, in one printed form with one run of entry numbers a year. Every image was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (child, father, mother, godparent, baptiser, margin note); I zoomed at level 13 the cells that could be one. **None of the three names stands in it**, and no priest called Josephus. The families are of the town (*oppidani Novi in Vinodol*, later *Novi u Vinodolu*); one entry of 1874 names *Mala Draga* (image 242, left page, entry 14, 17 March: the readers differ on whether it is the place of the baptism, by a midwife, or the parents' residence), and nothing else names Bakar, Rijeka, Trsat, Kraljevica, Crikvenica, Bribir or Hreljin as a place of origin. The baptisers are the canon **Joannes (Ivan) Potočnjak**, the canon **Antonius Mudrović**, the pensioned parish priest **Antonius Celigoj**, the provost of Modruš **Vincentius Merzljak** and, in 1870–71, a canon *Kalman* of Modruš.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kabalin* is very frequent from the first page to the last, and is written with its *b* (the name the Atlas lists as a near-name of Kalanj). **Zoomed by me at level 13:** the *Kukalj* of the book, three times where the reader had written *Kalj*: image 75, right page, 28 October 1862, entry 64, godmother «*Francisca nata **Kakalj***»; image 246, right page, 8 August 1874, entry 37, the mother «*Kate Ku-/**kalj***» (the word breaks across the line); image 258, right page, 8 December 1874, entry 112, the father «*Vicko Ku-/**kalj** Tomin…*». Image 75, left page, 14 October 1862, entry 57, a godmother «*nata Ka-/**calin** Josephi*» (the end of the first line is cut by my crop): *Ka-* then a *c*- or *k*-shaped letter and *-lin*, a surname of the *Kakalj* kind and not *Kalanj*, **unsettled, neither counted nor excluded**. Image 226, left page, 8 April 1873, entry 19, a godmother «*Magdalena **Kalen***»: a plain *e* in the middle, so *Kalen*, not *Kalan*. Image 146, left page, 9 August 1869, entry 43, a father «*Joannes ?oljan*»: the first letter is a capital shaped like the *Ž* of the same page (*Žanić*, entry 39) and not like its *K* (*Kabalin*, entry 43), a reader gave the same *Zoljan(?)* with a Z-shaped capital to a godfather of 1866 (image 116, right page, entry 46); unsettled, **not Kalanj**. The canon *Antonius Kalman* (or *Kallman*), the *custos* of Modruš, who baptises in 1870–71 (image 155 right, entry 1 of 4 January 1870, is the one cell where the first letters are unsettled), is a priest of that name and a different name from Kalanj. Also seen and not counted: *Kargačin*, *Vončina* (the schoolmaster, with a *V*), *Margan* / *Margačin*, *Deranja*, *Kriškovic*.

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1875–1900: births, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, has five children baptised at Novi in 1893–1900, and in 1898 the godparents are «Josip i Ana Defrancesco»
paras: **8 November 2026.** The fourth Novi Vinodolski volume on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R28-YWG, roll 85 of the Croatian State Archives; the cover is stamped *Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 358*) is one book, **«Matica kèrstna», the births of the parish church of Novi from 4 January 1875 (the first spread, image 8) to entry 90 of 30 December 1900 (image 396)**, ending «Nastavak Krštenih u novoj knjizi: E.» with the year-end signature of the canon Mate Cvetko. Every image from 6 to 399 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role; I zoomed the Kalanj and Defrancesco cells below at level 13 (one, entry 35 of 1896, I saw at level 12, the whole page). **No Kovačina stands in it, no priest called Josephus, and no Defranceschi of the old spellings; there is one Kalanj household, five times, and one Defrancesco, once.** Every residence cell reads *Novi*; the baptiser is the chaplain Vinko Sokolić almost throughout.

**Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, and Marija, born Peršić or Peričić** (*doc* for every word; the parents' cell and the page each time). **Entry 32 of 1893** (image 291, left page, p. 265): *Rozalia*, daughter, born 4 and baptised 5 July 1893, parents «*Martin Kalanj / Josipov, rođen iz / Klenovice, žena / mu Maria rodj. / Peršić težaci*» (zoomed by me at level 13: the father **born at Klenovica**, the mother's surname *Peršić*, where the reader had *Petrišić*); godparents, as the reader gave them, «Milutin Kvaranović (?) / Maria Kriskovic». **Entry 71 of 1894** (image 308 left, p. 278; image 309 is a second exposure of the leaf): *Ana*, daughter, born 5 and baptised 11 November 1894, «*Martin Kalanj Josipov, žena mu Marija rodj. Peričić*» (zoomed, level 13; the date from the half-page crop). **Entry 35 of 1896** (image 329, left page, p. 293): *Francika*, daughter, born 29 July and baptised 2 August 1896, «*Martin Kalanj Josipov, i Marija rodj. Peričić*» (seen by me at level 12, the whole page; godparents as the reader gave them, Andrij Zoričić and Elisabeta Zanić). **Entry 10 of 1898** (image 356, left page, p. 314): *Zora*, daughter, born 4 and baptised 13 March 1898, «*Martin Kalanj Josipov, Marija r. Peričić, polj.*» (zoomed, level 13). **Entry 1 of 1900** (image 382, left page, p. 333, the first entry of the year): *Ivan*, son, born 3 and baptised 6 January 1900, «*Martin Kalanj Josipov, Marija rodj. Peričić*» (zoomed, level 13; godparents as the reader gave them, Andrij Sokolić and Marija Matičić).

**The godparents of Zora, 13 March 1898.** On the right-hand leaf (p. 315) the fourth row, which is entry 10 (the left leaf, p. 314, holds entries 7–13), reads, at level 13: domicile «*Novi*», godparents «***Josip i Ana / Defrancesco** rk.*», baptiser «*Vinko Sokolić, Kapelan*», no note in the remarks column (the three rows above it carry later notes of 1976–1982, which belong to entries 7–9). That is **a Defranceschi-type surname in a Novi baptism of the nineteenth century, written with an *o*, the form the Atlas holds as *De Francesco* (typography only: nothing added to the catalogue), and the godparents of a Kalanj child.** What the cell does not say: the woman's maiden name, a trade, a house, a relationship to the child. **What stands beside it on this page (inf):** the Ledenice baptisms told above give a **Josip Defranceschi, klesar, and Ana Kalanj** as the parents of Anton Rudolf (1890) and Marija Stjepanka (1892, «u Crkvenici»), and a godfather «Josip de Franceschi klesar» in 1894; and **Ana Kalanj** is, on this page, the Anna of 1864 at house 22 of Klenovica, a daughter of Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia, whose son **Martinus** was born there on 8 November 1861. A *Josip and Ana Defrancesco* standing godparents to the daughter of a **Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, born at Klenovica** is what her family would look like: the two given names, the surname, the father's name and the village all agree. It is **inf**, not *doc*: Josip and Ana are common names, and nothing in either entry names the other. If it holds, **this is the first entry in which the Defranceschi husband and the Kalanj family stand together, and the first time either is met at Novi in this archive.**

**Which Martin.** Told apart from the two other Martin Kalanj of Klenovica on this page: the groom of the marriage of **12 November 1865** (24, house 22; the parents' cell crosses the gutter and the reader pairs it as Petrus and Joanna, so he would be *Petrov*), and the **seljak, 54, of Klenovica 23, who died at Rijeka on 29 November 1898** (wife *Anta*; told above): a man whose wife is called Marija and who has a son baptised on 6 January 1900 is not him. That the Martin of 1893–1900 is the **Martinus of 8 November 1861**, son of Josephus and Rosalia Perković of house 22, rests on the name, the patronymic, the village and an age of thirty-one at the first baptism (**inf**; his own baptism entry is not a Novi cell and no entry says it). The wife is *Peršić* in 1893 and *Peričić* in the four later entries: the same woman by the husband and the first name, the spelling is the scribe's (**inf**). Where and when they married (before July 1893, and not in these baptism books) is not known.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kabalin* in very many entries from the first page to the last, always with its *b* (zoomed by me, image 333 left, entry 64 of 1896, 4 October: the father «*Dobrotin Kaba-/lin Petrov*», where the reader had written *Kala-/lin*); *Kukalj* (a mother in 1896, a father in 1897, a godfather in 1897, a mother in 1900, among others); *Kargačin*, *Smokvina*, *Demartini*, *Frkovic*, *Zoričić*, and a **Janko Kovačić** (image 333 left, entry 63 of 1896, with a *ć*, «činovnik kod kr. kot. oblasti», a clerk of the royal district office). No Draga, Bakar, Fiume, Kraljevica, Crikvenica, Bribir or Hreljin as a place of origin in any baptism cell; Rijeka, Trsat, Zagreb, Senj and Crikvenica stand only in later registrars' notes and in one entry born at Trsat and entered in 1928 (image 341). **Not read, and so not a nil:** the cells under pasted slips (among them the godparents of entry 52 of 1897, image 351 right, and the baptiser of the same entry on 350), the note beside entry 68 of 1897 (353 right), the faint stamped note of 1915 on image 341 right, a 1917 witness's surname on 343 right (read *Rroscecchi*, not Franceschi-like); **page 62, entries 51–57 of 1878, which is not on the film between images 70 and 71**; the slip over the observations of entry 63 on image 136; one entry on image 44 left that the reader could not read; and the cells readers marked as a *Kukalj* broken at the line end and did not zoom (images 69 left e39, 199 right e65, 217 right e45, 240 left e2, 241 left e7, 243 left e23); and two place cells I did not zoom, «*iz Kale Drage*» (image 157 right, entry 20) and «*iz Bakra*» (image 258 right, entry 20). Images 0–5 were not sent to the readers and I have not looked at them; the readers' first image is the front cover (6), the first spread is 8, and images 397–399 are a blank form leaf and the end-of-item target and title slate (398 and 399 came back identical from the decoder: whether the film shows them twice is not known).

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1888–1899: deaths, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Novi Vinodolski deaths of 1888–1899
paras: **8 November 2026.** The last third of the Novi Vinodolski death book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2C-82J, roll 86 of the Croatian State Archives, item 1; the title slate reads *Matična knjiga umrlih 1859–1899*, and this waypoint begins in the middle of 1888, at **entry 27 of 9 August 1888 on image 6**, because the earlier part is the waypoint 9R28-YW1, not opened) runs to **entry 50 of 30 December 1899 on image 101**, closed by the canon Mate Cvetko with «*Godina 1900. slijedi u novoj knjizi D.*». Every image from 0 to 102 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (the deceased, the husband or wife, the parents, the burier, the remarks); the entries run on without a gap from 1888 to the last page, and the year changes fall on images 8/9, 17, 26, 33/34, 44, 55/56, 61, 69/70, 77/78, 86/87 and 93/94. **None of the three names stands in it, and no priest called Josephus.** The buriers are the provost Ivan Potočnjak, the canon Mate Cvetko, the chaplain Vinko Sokolić and now and then a priest from elsewhere.

**What this nil says about the Kalanj of Novi.** The man of the baptisms of 1893–1900, **Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, and Marija, born Peričić** (told above), does not die in this book, nor does his wife, nor any of his children Rozalia, Ana, Francika, Zora and Ivan before the last page of 1899; nor do **Josip and Rosalia Perković** of Klenovica house 22 (they are not in the Ledenice death book of 1866–1902 either), nor Ana's husband, the klesar Josip Defranceschi, nor Ana. A **Marija Peričić** does die on **30 December 1899** (entry 50, the last entry of the book, image 101, left page, which I saw whole at level 12): «*Peričić marija, selj.*», aged 36, the parents' cell «*Roko i marija Peričić, roditelji*», *Novi*, buried on 31 December by Cvetko. **She is not Martin's wife:** the cell names her parents, not a husband, and the wife of Martin Kalanj bore a son on 3 January 1900, four days after. A Peričić family of Novi, with a Roko, is what the entry shows (**inf**: that Marija the wife is of it, and the dead woman her sister, is a guess nothing in the pages supports).

**Places, as the readers found them (not counted).** *Klenovica*: image 85, entry 52, 10 December 1897, «Katarina Miletić, selj. udova, 64», the cell «*Kljenovica Kbr. 19 z. Ledenia*» (Klenovica, house 19, of the parish of Ledenice; a Miletić woman: the surname of the *Catharina, born Miletić* of the Callein household told above is the only link, and it is a coincidence of a common name until a page says otherwise). *Ledenice*: image 6 left, entry 33, 10 October 1888, a child of «*Matij Ferković, rodom iz Ledinic[a]*» (the last letters run over the line); image 60, 1894, entry 34, 4 October, «*Josip Perković (?) Antonov, težak, 28*», wife Juliana, origin Ledenice («Ledenice 30») with words struck out about his coming to Novi; neither is Rosalia's husband, and *Perković* as a surname of the Novi books (image 54, entry 72, 16 November 1893, «Blaž Perković (Ferković), 36») is common. *Bakar*: image 13, entry 36, May 1889, Polde Veljačić, 12, whose father is a royal finance inspector; image 27, entry 9, 3 February 1891, «Sv. Kuzma kod Bakra». *Bribir*: image 22, entry 43, 10 October 1890; image 52, an unnumbered row of 3 August 1893 (Josip Piškulić, died at Bribir, copied from a certificate of 7 August); image 58, 1894, entry 20 (16 June, an Anton Veljačić). *Rijeka* («Rieka»): several, among them image 9, entry 7, 21 January 1889, and image 53, entry 62, 1893. *Kraljevica*: entry 22 of 3 June 1892 (a Baić; images 33–38), image 48, entry 26, 1893 (a royal sub-county physician). No Draga, Trsat or Hreljin.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kabalin* in very many entries from the first page to the last, always with its *b*; *Kukalj* (image 39 left, entry 38, 3 August 1892, a child of Ferdinando Kukalj and Lucia born Kabalin, which a reader zoomed and read *Kukalj*, not *Kalanj*); *Kargačin* in a dozen entries (the mother of entry 44 of 18 June 1893, image 50 left, is written *Karga-/čin*); *Kovačić* (entry 41 of 12 November 1888, images 6–8, Stanislav, a child of Ivan Kovačić, a clerk; image 67, entry 49, 1895, Amalija Kovačić; entry 27 of 17 June 1892, images 33–38, Petar Kovačić of Zagreb); *Peršić* and *Peričić* (the Novi families of the wife; 1894, entry 28, Ivan Peršić; 1895, entry 3, Anton Peršić; image 72, entry 28 of 1896 and image 73, entry 38, Peričić); *Smokvina*, *Vončina* (image 26, entry 1, 3 January 1891, Katarina, widow of a Josip Vončina, of Istria: a *V*), *Kunović*, *Ježić*, *Deranja*. **Not read, and so not a nil:** the cut-off row below entry 33 on image 6 left (a stillbirth of 18 September 1888, out of date order, number unclear); the number column of page 377 on image 90, torn away (entries 18–23 inferred by the reader); the origin words of image 29 left, entry 28 («iz Kraj..ske rodom», 15 August 1891), image 47 left, entry 17 (22 February 1893, read like *Šušina*), the mother of image 68 left, entry 55 (25 October 1895, smudged, *Kov-/Kovskovic*), and the surname of image 58 left, entry 22 (21 June 1894, *Kargačin* or *Razgačin*), none of them zoomed; the first letters of *Kargačin* on images 51 and 53, read at crop size; and every cell the readers read at crop magnification only. Images 0–2 are a roll slate, a blank grey frame and a resolution chart, 3 and 4 and 5 a film-start card (roll 86, continued from roll 85), a title slate and a «continued from another roll» card, 102 an end-of-item slate and the title slate again.

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1859–1888: deaths, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Novi Vinodolski deaths of 1859–1888
paras: **8 November 2026.** The first two thirds of the Novi Vinodolski death book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R28-YW1, roll 85 of the Croatian State Archives, item 2; the title slate reads *Matična knjiga umrlih 1859–1899*; the cover of the book carries the label of the Povijesni arhiv Rijeka, *275 (K4), 359*, and the pasted label «*Liber Defunctorum … Novi in Vinodol … ab anno 1859 … usque ad annum 1900*») runs from **entry 1 of 3 August 1859 on image 4** (a Kabalin infant, house 186) to the foot of **image 307**, entry 33 of 10 October 1888 and the first words of one more stillbirth, whose cells go on in the next page, which is not on this roll; the rest, from entry 27 of 9 August 1888 on, is on the next roll (waypoint 9R2C-82J, told above), so the two waypoints overlap on entries 27–33 of 1888 and the whole book from 1859 to the last entry of 1899 has now been looked at. Every image from 0 to 312 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (the deceased, the husband or wife, the parents, the burier, the remarks); images 0–3 are the roll slates (filmed 6 February 1997, roll 85), a resolution chart, the front cover and the inside cover, and images 308–312 two end slates, the «KRAJ» card (roll 85, continued on roll 86), a chart, «END OF ROLL» and a blank frame. **None of the three names stands in it, and no priest called Josephus is a priest of Novi** (the buriers are the chapter, the chaplains and parish priests Joannes / Ivan Potočnjak, Vincentius / Vinko Merzljak as administrator in 1863–64, Vinko Sokolić, Frane Mikulić); two other priests called Josephus are in inserted certificates, not in the parish: a Fr. Josephus *de S. Romulo*, guardian and parish priest at Alexandria in Egypt, who signs a Latin certificate (image 70, entry 45, 18 November 1869, for a Josephus Mažuranić of Novi), and a «Josephus Pot(o)čkaj(?), parochus» of a Hungarian parish on a Predmér slip (image 259, 1883, roughly read).

**What this nil says about the Kalanj of Novi.** The Kalanj of Klenovica who baptise their children at Novi from 1893 (told above: Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, and Marija, born Peričić) are not among the dead of 1859–1888 in this parish, and neither are **Josip and Rosalia Perković** of Klenovica house 22, nor Ana Kalanj, nor Ana's husband, the klesar Josip Defranceschi: the three families do not appear in any role in any cell the readers quoted. That is what a parish nil is worth: the Kalanj of Klenovica belong to the parish of Ledenice, and the Ledenice death books have been read separately. **Leads, not findings:** a mother born *Peričić* occurs in several entries of 1877–78 (entries 128, 130, 131 of 1877 and 4 of 1878) (images 162–167; image 178, entry 70 of 13 September 1878, a child of Josip Kargačin and **Rozalia Peričić**, house 187) and **Perković / Ferković** as a surname of Novi (image 105, entry 32, 1873, a Nicolaus Ferković; image 302, entry 81, 9 November 1887, «Mikula Ferković/Perković», wife Maria Baran; image 307, entry 33 of 10 October 1888, Kate, aged 2, daughter of «Matija Perković, radnik, iz Ledinic[a]»): none of them is Rosalia, and a common surname of the Vinodol is not evidence for or against her family.

**Settled at level 13, and not Kalanj.** *Toljan* (read as a T or Z with a cross-bar, the surname written *Toljan* in full in this same book, e.g. image 52, entry 6, and image 55, entry 34 of 1867): image 63 left, **entry 63 of 12 August 1868**, Clara, 6 days, daughter of «Joannes Toljan ejus uxor Maria Marišević»; image 86 left, **entry 57 of 22 August 1871**, Andreas, 8 months, of «Joannes Toljan ejus uxor Maria»; image 88, entry 78 of 18 October 1871, Maria, 3 years, of the same parents (read like entry 57, not zoomed separately). The scribe's capital K is a double-stroke letter with a loop (the *K* of «Kukalj», image 87, entry 68, 18 September 1871, same hand and month), and the second letter of these cells is an *o*. *Fancić* (image 47 left, **entry 21 of 26 May 1866**, «Paulus Fancis(?) mercator», 36, of Bribir, wife «Margaritha nata Karinl(?) Joannis»; the readers had *Carolus Fancis* and *Franc…*; the page at level 12 and the cell at level 13 show **Paulus** and a *Fanc-* with no *r*, so it is not Franceschi or Francesco; the wife's maiden name is not settled).

**Places, as the readers found them (not counted).** *Draga*: image 19, entry 24, 1861, a Margan «Dragensis» (the only mention of Draga before 1874); image 116 left, entry 30, 18 (or 28) March 1874, **Josip Gojdanić**, 1 day, of «mala Draga», parents Anselmo Gojdanić and Maria Rosić. *Bribir*: image 47, entry 21, 1866 (the Fancić merchant above); image 54, entry 28, 10 November 1867, Maria Velgačić, servant; images 171–172, entry 34, 12 April 1878, Cena Vrinjanin; image 225, entry 112, 5 October 1880, Antonia Kukalj, born at Bribir; and «kapelan bribirski» as burier on image 257, entry 29, 1883 (reading approximate). *Kraljevica*: image 242, entry 73, 8 November 1881, Johana Bacac, «Cernik / Kraljevica»; image 244, entry 6, 26 January 1882, a mother «rodom iz Kraljevice». *Rijeka* («Rieka»): image 135, entry 8, 18 March 1876, Eduard Merzljak, royal court councillor, «umro na Rieci», wife Ludovika born Cabalini; several others, among them a notice of the Rijeka prefect on image 136 (entry 14, 1876), a Rijeka railway hospital on image 145, entry 24, 1877, and image 267, entry 35, 1884. *Ledenice*: image 307 (above). *Crikvenica*: image 25, a Croatian letter of 30 January 1862 inserted before entry 1 of 1862 (the magistrate of Rijeka, the judge Mudrovčić at Crikvenica, a death in the hospital at Trst, Trieste(?), on 15 October 1861 of a Josip Krisković, 68); image 272, entry 68, 20 December 1884, Mate Matejić of Crikvenica, drowned. No Bakar, Trsat, Hreljin or Klenovica in any entry read.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kabalin* in very many entries from the first page to the last (image 4, entry 1, is one), also *Caballini* (image 135, entry 8; image 287, entry 40, 1886, a baroness *Caballini de Slavnigrad*); *Kukalj* from 1871 on (image 87, entry 68; 1872–1887 in many entries, among them images 98, 99, 108, 126, 144, 199, 207, 225, 277, 280, 285, 287, 291–295); *Kargačin* in very many; *Kukuljan* (image 59, 1868, children of Georgius Kukuljan, a financial guard from Karlobag); *Deranja* (images 174–175, 1878, zoomed by a reader: *De-ra-*, not Defranceschi); *Kuhačević* (image 94, entry 17, 1872), *Kalman/Kaliman* the sacristan (image 70, entry 44, 1869, zoomed by a reader); *Rabalin* (image 189, entry 7, 1879), *Sabalja/Kabalja* (image 193, entry 16, 1879). No *Kovačić* was reported by the readers in this book. **Not read, and so not a nil:** the rest of **1862** after entry 12 of 5 May 1862 (images 26 and 27 are one opening photographed twice and the next image, 28, begins on 16 January 1863: the pages between are not on the film); every cell hidden by a pasted slip or a loose sheet (image 26, the whole right page, and image 27, the upper left, by the Croatian *Svjedočanstvo* of 8 February 1878; images 92–93, a pasted Croatian slip over the right half, lifted on 93; images 140–141, entry 45 of 1876 and entries 1–5 of 1877, a German insertion about a *Josef Sokolić, Pfarrer … St. Georgen*; image 143, the right cells of entries 13–19 of 1877; image 144, entries about 13–17 of 1877 under a loose sheet; image 204, the cause and burial cells of entries 55–61 of 1879 under a Grižane certificate; images 253–254, 258–259 and the Serbian death extract on 270–271); the number columns of 1888 on images 300–305, overwritten; image 227, entry 122 of 1880 (no legible number or date); the origin cells of image 210, entry 27, 1880, and image 154, entry 79, 1877 (read roughly); the surnames of **«Se-/Calja Marti-ni»** (image 30, entry 20, 1863), **«Ke-/kalj Pauli»** (image 33, entry 23) and of the Kargačin/Margačin cells on images 32 and 35, the *Kalinić* on image 33, entry 22, **«Zi-gjan»** (image 41, entry 15) and *Mariaševic* (entry 18), none of them zoomed; the wide Latin or Croatian notes on image 49 (entry 45, a Novi man dead at Skradin in Dalmatia on 3 August 1866), image 61 (entry 46, 1868, «prov. Fiume in Austria», signed *Germanus, curatus*), image 72 (entry 11, 1870, signed *fr. Leander*), image 100 (the year-turn note of 1872/73), image 136 (navy notices, entry 21), images 144–145 (notes of entries 18 and 24); the year-turn rows; and every cell the readers read at crop magnification only, which is most of them.

sections.lab: Novi Vinodolski 1823–1859: deaths, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Novi Vinodolski deaths of 1823–1859
paras: **8 November 2026.** The earlier half of the Novi Vinodolski death book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R29-4W1, Croatian State Archives film 219; the slate reads *Matična knjiga umrlih 1815–1859, item 1* and the film begins «nastavak sa filma 218», so the book starts on film 218, which is the second Novi volume, waypoint 9R2M-82L, told above: its deaths of November 1815 to August 1823 are images 534–568 of that volume, and this roll holds the part from 1823) runs from **image 5, the first register opening (pages 58–59, 1823)** to **image 122, the last dated entry of 30 July 1859** and one late out-of-order row (Paulus Piškulić, «8 Martii 1859»); image 123 is an end slate, and images 0–4 are a leader plate, a resolution chart, the film-start slate, the two slates of roll 219 and a «continued» card. The next entry in the book, **3 August 1859, is entry 1 on image 4 of waypoint 9R28-YW1** (told above), so the Novi death book from November 1815 to the last entry of 1899 has now been looked at in four pieces (9R2M-82L images 534–568, this roll, 9R28-YW1 and 9R2C-82J), each with the gaps named in its own row. Every image from 0 to 123 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (the deceased, husband or wife, parents, burier, remarks). It is a printed Latin *Liber defunctorum* table, one opening to an image, house numbers but no entry numbers, in Latin to 29 September 1848 and from 1849 in Croatian, going back to Latin in January 1858. **None of the three names stands in it.** Priests called Josephus do occur, with other surnames, and are not the Josephus of the Defranceschi: Dominus Josephus Umiljenović, *parochus pensionatus* (image 19, 11 August 1830), and Josephus Mažuranić, a capitular priest who supplies in entry 28 of 3 June 1844 (image 62); a burial note of 19 December 1840 («per H…[illegible] Josephi Cooperatorem», image 54 left) may name a cooperator Josephus and is not settled. The buriers are otherwise the chapter and its chaplains; the lay Josephi of the parish and the schoolmaster Dominus Josephus (Wonzhina / Wonthkino, 1825 and 1839) are not priests.

**What this nil says about the Kalanj of Novi.** The Kalanj of Klenovica who baptise their children at Novi from 1893 (Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, and Marija, born Peričić, told above), and **Josip and Rosalia Perković** of Klenovica house 22, and Ana Kalanj and her husband the klesar Josip Defranceschi, are not among the dead of 1823–1859 in this parish, in any role in any cell the readers quoted. A parish nil is worth that and no more: the Kalanj of Klenovica belong to the parish of Ledenice, whose death books have been read separately, and nobody in this run is a Defranceschi or a Kovačina. **Leads that came to nothing:** a mother or widow born *Peričić* in several entries (for example 6 March 1835) and *Perković / Ferković* as surnames of Novi (image 87, 25 August 1849, a Jure son of Josip Ferković «iz Ledenic», aged 8): not Rosalia and not her family on anything the cells say. Place only: Ledenice (images 13, 6 October 1827; 87; 118 right, 28 January 1858, Filippus Cvitković «e Ledenicensi Parochia oriundus»; 115 left, 8 March 1857, Vid Butković «iz Sela povile, plovanie Ledeničkoga»).

**Zoomed by me, and not Kalanj.** *Image 64, right page (p. 173), entry 85, 13 December 1844, house 278* (levels 13 on the whole upper right page, then on the cell): «Maria filia Joannis Piškulić & Maria nata [one struck word] / Kalj», aged 3, *tussis convulsa*. The mother's maiden name is **«Kalj»** after a struck-out word, and I could not settle it further: it is not a catalogued Kalanj form (not Kalanj, Kalain, Kallayn or any of the forms seen on the Kalanj's own records), the scribe has struck a first attempt and written the name over again, and the Novi families of that surname-shape are Kukalj (house 324–326 in the same years: images 62, 63 and 65 here). I have **not** added it to the Atlas and have **not** counted it. *Image 104, right page (p. 251), 4 September 1854*: «Kate kći suprugah Andrija i Mare Su- / Kalj», half a year old, *lijavica* (level 12, the whole page): a name broken across two lines, **Su-kalj / Ku-kalj**, not Kalanj. *Image 109 left, 19 August 1855*, «Mare rođene Ku-/Kalj» (a reader, not zoomed) is the same line-break trap, read as Kukalj.

**Places, as the readers found them (not counted).** *Bakar*: image 59 right, 7 April 1843, Philippus Mudrović died and was buried there «at his canon brother's» («Buccari»); images 36 (1836) and 62 (14 July 1844, «Obiit … Buccari, & ibi sepultus»); image 114 left, 13 August 1856, a child whose parents are «iz Bakarske Drage» (Bakar's Draga). *Kraljevica* («Portus Regius»): image 47 left, 21 August 1838, a soldier of the Ogulin Regiment who died on the way there; image 57 right, 22 June 1842, the Kraljevica cemetery; image 92 right, July 1850, a soldier «hodeći iz Kraljevica». *Bribir*: 1832, 22 July 1836 (image 38 right), image 120 right, 21 December 1858, Joannes Kersul(?) of Bribir found dead on the road between Novi and Bribir. *Klenovica*: image 16, 6 August 1829. *Senj*: 14 August 1836 and 2 August 1838. *Rijeka*: image 107 left, 7 July 1855, a man who died «u gradskoj bolnici u Reci». Also Karlobag (1836, 1849), Grobnik (image 36), Trieste (24 July 1855), Cilli («u Zagorju kod Cilli», 16 October 1848). No Draga proper, Trsat, Fiume as a parish or Crikvenica in a way that bears on a name.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kobalin / Kaballin / Kabalin* in very many entries from 1823 to 1859 (the nearest to the eye, and always K-o/a-b-a-l-l-i-n); *Kukalj* from 1827 to 1858 (images 38 right and 40 left, July 1836, «Lucia uxor Bartholomei Ku-/kalj», house 326; 44, 46, 52, 53, 54, 58, 59, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 72; Bartholomeus Kukalj, 71, 29 September 1846, image 67, zoomed by a reader at the line break); *Kargačin / Karzacin* in very many, among them the canon Agricola Karzacin (image 118 left, 18 January 1858) and the Lieutenant Joannes Kargacin of the 1809 insurrection (image 119 left, 19 June 1858); *Piskulić / Piškulić* (many); *Toljan* (the cooperator Joannes Toljan, died 2 October 1827); *Vončina / Wonzhina*; *Umiljenović* (Dominus Josephus Umiljenović, parochus pensionatus, image 19, 11 August 1830, a priest of that name and not Josephus Defranceschi); *Caballini* (A.R.D. Joannes-Nicolaus Caballini, 1823, image 5); *Hoballini* (image 6, p. 60, 30 September 1823, first letter H/K/Z not settled, K-o-b-a-l-l-i-n in form). *«Franciscus Ču-kulić(?)», parochus pensionatus* (image 21, p. 91, 20 June 1831) is a different name. *Franciscus* occurs as a given name and a patronymic only. **Not read, and so not a nil:** every cell the readers read at crop magnification only, which is every cell except the three above (no reader could zoom); the first letter of the *Hoballini* cell on image 6 and of the cells «Makabunich» (p. 105, 18 January 1833), «Drickia / Vrichia» (16 December 1833) and «Navor / Lavor» (19 August 1835); the Piran ship and the surname «Zhoranich?» (image 57 left, 15 December 1841); **image 54 left, 19 December 1840, a burial note «per H…[illegible] Josephi Cooperatorem»**, which may name a cooperator Josephus and was not zoomed; the order of image 50, an exact duplicate exposure of 49; the pair of images 89 and 90, which carry the same dates and pages (222–223, 6 September to 4 October 1849) and are very probably one opening photographed twice (a weak image hash, not settled); the **gap of about 13 November to 16 December 1847** (images 69–70, no entries, with the book changing hand to Adalbertus Mariassevich at that point) and the **gap of December 1857 and 1–8 January 1858** (image 117 right, folio 139, blank after 29 November; the Latin series begins on 9 January); the year-turn rows and the month marks 8bris/9bris on pp. 136–137.

sections.lab: Hreljin 1800–1844: baptisms, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Hreljin baptisms of 1800–1844
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Hreljin baptism books on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2F-4WT, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 40, 290 images) hold two books. **Item 3** (the roll's slate and the card inside the cover read *Matična knjiga rođenih 1772–1815*) is a hand-ruled Latin register, one entry to a paragraph with the hamlet and house number in the left margin (Poljice, Zlobin, Zastene, Melnice, Vlaka, Ruxich and others); the readers found the first baptism on **image 24, right page (page 1), July 1800**, and the last on **image 91, 14 October 1815**; before it stand a leader and slates (images 0–5, with an inventory of the collegiate church of 1752) and the church's own loan and account ledgers of 1732–1779 in Italian, Croatian and Latin (images 6–23), which are not baptisms. **Item 4** (*Liber baptizatorum in ecclesia S. Georgii M. in Hrelin*, a Latin printed table from the Rijeka press of Karletzky, 1815; the archive card reads *1815–1844*) begins on **image 97 with the tail of 1815 (23 November)** and runs, one opening to an image, to **image 280, entry 112 of 31 December 1844, «Finis.
