The readers noted gaps and repeats in the numbering (entry 68 used twice in 1871, entry 46 of 1873 not seen between images 224 and 225, number 78 twice in 1875) and recorded them as they stand.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Smokvina* (very many, 1860s to 1889), *Margan*, *Kalafat* (the caulker's trade and a Trsat byname, in many cells; **not Kalanj**), *Kalina* (a domicile word on image 331, and a «Grgo Kalina/Kralina» of 25 years, Podvežica 98, 3 April 1876, parents unknown, on image 261), *Kaljner* (image 347, entry 102, Marija Kaljner, parents Frana and Tereza Kaljner, 25 November 1885), «rodj. Calman» (image 257, entry 79), «Kalnica / Zakalj» (a domicile, image 363), *Kovačić* and *Kovačević* in many cells from 1867 to 1889, *Kovač* as a smith's trade and one «Rovac/Kovac» (image 278), *Franciskovic* and its spellings (a wife of 1886 on image 350, a girl's parents of 1886 on image 360, an Ivan of 1888 on image 380, a mother of 1877 «Franušković» on image 269), *Fransar(?)* (images 215 and 226: an initial F or T, not *Franc-*), *Franceskin* (above), *Fiandrini*, *De Pennevet*, *Depeder*, *Deforneli*, *de Fabris*, *de Sardo*, *de Zorzi*, *Castagna*, *Franić*. **Places in cells (not counted):** **Draga** (a village of origin or a domicile in dozens of cells, from 1861 to 1889: Studenac, Večerina, Pajnić, Belten and Bakarčić families), **Bakar** (an origin or a parish note: «župe Bakarske», Krasica, Butković, Arsenić, a struck «Bakar» on image 323), Fiume / Rijeka (origin and the place of a birth or death, throughout), Hreljin, Kraljevica, Kostrena, Volosko, Trst. **A place in a cell is a place and nothing more.** The Bakar magistrate's order on image 195 (3 September 1871, a man hanged) is a note in the margin and no more.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** Every cell at crop magnification except the five I zoomed; the cells of entries 33–36 of 1860 that the tipped-in letter covers on images 49–50; the cell «Kala…» of image 98; the cells the readers called unsettled and I did not open (among them image 194, entry 65, «Rukavina (Kukavina?)»; image 177, entry 31, «Kovačović/Kovačević»; image 256, entry 74, «Materljan Kalafat»; image 366, entry 52, a husband's cell «[K]alova?»; image 370, entry 94, a second line under Sušak); the later hands in the margins; and any entry numbers not compared across image boundaries. **This row is a reader pass over every image and not a walk, and the book's catalogued 1858 – 1889 span is a fact of the slate, not of my count of entries.**

sections.lab: Bribir roll 10: marriages 1858–1900 and deaths 1858–1898, read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: No Defranceschi, no Kovačina and no Kalanj in the Bribir marriage book of 1858–1900 or in the Bribir death book of 1858–1898, and a Kalliman family of Kićeri settled as not Kalanj
paras: **9 November 2026.** Roll 10 of the Croatian State Archives microfilm for the parish of Bribir in the Vinodol (598 images; the FamilySearch browse lists of waypoint 9R28-L23, which the Atlas catalogues as the deaths, and of 9R28-L2Q, catalogued as the marriages, hold the same 598 images, checked arks against arks on 9 November 2026) holds **two books**, and every image of both was looked at once by readers: the **marriage book 1858–1900** (images 6–186) and the **death book 1858–1898** (images 197–587). **Not one cell of either names a Defranceschi-type surname, a Kovačina or a Kalanj in any role that the readers or I could settle** (bride, groom, parents, witness, the priest, the deceased, the spouse or parents of the deceased, the origin and house columns, the Observationes and the margins), and no priest of the parish is a Defranceschi. That is a reader pass and not a walk: the cells named below stayed open and none of them is counted. The earlier Bribir books (the births, marriages and deaths of 1787–1858, the volume that names Defranceschi deaths of 1798, 1801 and 1817) are told above; these two are the later civil-register books of the same parish.

**What the roll holds, from its slates.** Images 0–5: the filming slates and charts; **6–186 the marriage book**, «Župa Bribir / Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1858–1900 / Item 1» (printed Latin «Sponsi et Sponsae» table, entries in Latin to 1877 and in Croatian from 1878; numbering restarts at 1 each year; the last entry, no. 50 of 28 November 1900, is on image 186); 187–190 blank leaves with loose slips; **191 the slate «End of item», CRO 00008, roll 10**; **192 the slate «Župa Bribir / Matična knjiga umrlih 1858–1898 / Item 2»**; 193–194 targets; 195 the book's front cover («Matična knjiga umrlih mjesnog ureda Bribir 1858.–1898.», Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 48); 196 an inside card; **197–587 the death book** (printed Latin «Defuncti» table, Latin entries to 1877 and Croatian from 1878; numbering restarts at 1 each year, 11 to 20 entries to an image; entry 1 of 3 January 1858 on image 197; the last written entry on image 587, no. 56 of 11 August 1898); 588 a ruled leaf struck out with a diagonal and the note «Nastavak vidi u Knjizi VI.» (the continuation is in Book VI, which is not on this roll); 589 blank; **590 the slate «End of item», roll 10, with the slate of Item 2**; 591 the Croatian State Archives card «Kraj … nastavak na mikrofilmskom svitku br. 11»; 592 a resolution chart; 593 «End of roll». Images 594–597 hold a blank frame, a resolution chart and two identical frames of a second «End of roll» slate (they add nothing). **No page of either book prints the name of the parish** in a heading: Bribir is named by the slates, by the cover, by a visitation note «U Bribiru dne» (image 178) and by the origin column of the death book.

**The Kalliman family of Kićeri (my zooms at level 13, three cells, settled).** The readers marked several cells in the 1860s–1880s whose surname begins *Kal-* and ends *-man* or *-nan* and whose house is at **Kićeri** (Kićeri 1, 2 and 5). I zoomed three at level 13. **Image 332, left, entry 83** (2 April 1871): «*Georgius Kalliman filius*», parents «*Georgius & Catharina Kalliman agricola*», Kićeri 2, an infant: the surname is written *Kalliman* in both cells, three minims in the *m*, no *j*. **Image 387, left, entry 103** (6 October 1876): «*Catharina Ka-/liman*», parents «*Nicolaus et Margareta*», Kićeri 5, three years: *Kaliman* across a line break. **Image 418, left, entry 23** (22 March 1880): «*Helena Kaliman*», parents «*Jure i Ursula*», Kićeri 1, ten days. **These are *Kaliman*, a Bribir house of Kićeri, and not *Kalanj*; they are not counted.** The other *Kaliman*/*Kalliman* cells of the books (the marriage book from 1869; the priest *Antonius Kaliman*(?), a cantor-canon, of the marriage book (images 60–83) and of death-book images 375 and 380–382, read at crop level; image 53 entry 23, the 1870 bride Lucia whose father Joseph is *Kal(l)iman*; image 48, right, entry 45, parents «Georg Ugrin & Steph Kallimau»; the death entries of 1881–1897 at Kićeri 1 to 3) read the same way at crop level and I did not open them. **Kalafatić** (Gradac, Stale, Podugljin, many cells from 1858 to 1898) is a trade-name family and **not Kalanj**; **Kovačić** (and *Kovač* as a trade) is **not Kovačina**.

**Cells left open (none counted, none excluded).** In the marriage book: image 272, left, entry 43, groom «Paulus Fancic/Francic» of Bribir 73; image 313, entries 102 and 106 (December 1869) «Fancic/Tancic»; image 356, left, no. 112 (3 September 1873) «Margareta Fra-/nic»; image 353, left, no. 69 (25 May 1873) the origin of «Josephus Andria Mramor», read «Terfacti/Tersacti» (a place or a misreading: the Trsat of the same year is *Tersat*); image 35, right, entry 28 a struck «Joannes ?Kovačić», and left, entry 22 «Kalafat(ić)»; image 22, entry 23, a priest «Toki(?) Fucinensis»; image 23, entry 37, a bride «Kallić/Hallić(?)»; image 94, left, entry 14, a bride «Nov-/Kov-ackovic»; image 96, left, entry 5, «Kukalj»; image 42, no. 35, «Kabalin». In the death book: image 379, left, entry 88, «Nicolaus Kalli-man(?)», and image 380, left, entry 105, «Anna Kallic/Hallic(?)» of Sv. Mikula 35; image 413, left, entry 109, «Maria Kaliman(?)»; image 419, left, entry 30, «Franica Klatic/Kalatic(?)» of Podugljin 14; image 369, right, entry 147, a Portorè to Bribir note read as «Bakar?»; image 429, left, entry 29 (19 January 1881) «Ursula Kaliman(?)», Kićeri 5; image 430, left, entry 50 (15 February 1881) «Hinko Franjić/Stanišić(?)»; image 424, left, no. 99 (30 November 1880) «Vjekoslav K/H-alman?»; image 435, left, entry 116 (1 November 1881) «Mate Kalman» (a Kalman, not a Kalan form, read at crop level); image 455, left, 1885 entry 3 «Franjo Halić/Kalić»; image 453, right, entry 66 (16 October 1884) a burial cell that may name Rijeka. **None of these is a Defranceschi or a Kalanj as read**; each is a cell the readers could not settle at crop level and I did not open.

**Clergy.** **Josip Mrzljak (Josephus)**, canon, cantor and parish priest of Bribir, aged 69, died 30 November 1882 (image 442, entry 73; buried 2 December 1882 by the abbot Vinko Mrzljak) and buries many of the entries of the entries of 1880–1882; in the marriage book the priests Merzljak / Merkljaky and Sandri are named *Josephus*. **A Josephus, and not a Defranceschi.** The Defranceschi who died at Bribir in 1798, 1801 and 1817 are told above and have no successor in these books. Other burying priests: Petar Car (canon, died 15 June 1887, image 467, entry 30), Marko Rakuša, Božo Mihovilić, Mihovil Pekić, Stanislav Gregović, Lovro Vidaš, Ambroz Brozović, Rok Katnić, Karlo Kokot, Josip Zagar (curate), Karlo and Dragutin Šefer, Ivan Petrenjak (provost).

**Places in cells (not counted).** Villages of the Vinodol parish (Bribir, Gradac, Stale, Ugrini, Podgora, Kićeri, Dragaljin / Dragažin / Dragašin, Podugljin, Sv. Vid, Sv. Mikula, Zagrad, Jargovo and others), Novi, Grižane, Ledenice, Lokve, Fužine, Selce and, from the 1880s, **burials and deaths of Bribir people away from home**: Vienna and Millendorf, Puchberg am Schneeberg, Zagreb, Sarajevo, Thessaloniki, Rio de Janeiro, Romania, America, the steamer «Ika» in Rijeka harbour (1897). **Draga**: «Dragaljin / Dragažin» is a hamlet of Bribir and is not read as the Draga of Bakar; the early death-book entries that give *Draga* as a deceased's village (1859–1860) name no Defranceschi-adjacent family. **A place in a cell is a place and nothing more.**

**Near-names, none of them counted.** Kalafatić / Kolafatić / Kalafat (very many); Kaliman / Kalliman / Kalman / Kalinan / Kalivan (Kićeri and Vicini, above); Kovačić, Kovač, Kovačević; Kukalj; Kabalin; Fancić / Francić / Tancić; Franjić / Stanišić; Ugrin; Mrzljak. **Structure notes from the readers:** the death-book numbering jumps from 165 to 173 on images 340–341 of 1871 (an offset, no date gap), number 44 is used twice in 1886 (image 463), 40 twice in 1888 (images 474–475), 57 and 70 are repeated on other images, image 334 repeats an opening, and some years end with unnumbered late entries for deaths abroad. Blank-page slates (images 494, 506, 547) and the 1890 and 1891 openings are leaves left blank on the microfilm's own account.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** Every cell at crop magnification except the three zoomed Kaliman cells; every cell named as open above; the loose slips on 187–190 and the tipped-in notes; the margin hands; the entry numbers not compared across image boundaries; and **the death book after August 1898 (Book VI, not on this roll)**. **This row is a reader pass over every image and not a walk; the catalogued 1858–1900 and 1858–1898 spans are facts of the slates, not of my count of entries.**

sections.lab: Bribir births 1858–1886 (9R2Z-ZNG), read by readers · 9 November 2026
sections.h2: No Defranceschi, no Kovačina and no Kalanj that the readers or I could settle in the Bribir baptism register of 1858–1886; a later note beside the entries of 10 September 1886 left open, and the Kaliman house of Kićeri settled again as not Kalanj
paras: **9 November 2026.** The baptism register of the parish of Bribir in the Vinodol, **1858–1886** (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2Z-ZNG, which the Atlas catalogues as «Births 1858–1886»; Croatian State Archives microfilm, **roll 9**, 412 images; the item's title card, on image 406, reads «rođenih 1856–1886»), was looked at **once, image by image, by readers**: entries from **image 4** (January 1858) to the last written page, **image 405** (page 396, 31 December 1886, entry 170). **Not one cell that the readers or I could settle names a Defranceschi-type surname, a Kovačina or a Kalanj in any role** (child, father, mother's maiden name, godparent, midwife, the baptising priest, the Observationes and the margins), and no priest called Josephus is a Defranceschi. That is a reader pass and not a walk: the cells named below stayed open and none of them is counted. **One of them, a later note on image 398, may carry a «De Francesk-» and is told first.**

**The one note that matters (image 398, beside entries 79 and 80 of 10 September 1886; my zoom at level 13, the full size of the leaf; open, not counted, not excluded).** Image 397 is page 391; **image 398 is a second exposure of the same page.** In the Observationes margin a later hand writes: «*Sklopio drugu ženidbu sa* [**De?**] *Franc-esk-om pd. Pipin…* | *… vjenčani u Bribiru dne 18. rujna 19…*» (he contracted a second marriage with …, born Pipinić …, married at Bribir on 18 September 19..). The note is cut at the right edge by an envelope or slip, and the year is lost. On image 397 a typed slip over the same margin is a court's note («… Okružnog suda u Rijeci, Pov. br. P-67/65. g. od 1. travnja 1965., **brak sa PIPINIĆ FRANCISKOM razriješen je** …», and «Umro dana 1. svibnja 1967. u Rijeci»), which names the woman as *Pipinić*, with *Franciska* as her given name. **So the word is most likely the given name *Franceska / Franciska* with the surname Pipinić; the initial before it is a large flourished capital that I cannot settle (*De*, *D* or a flourish of the hand).** Read as a given name it says nothing about the name Defranceschi; read as «De Francesk-» it would be a woman's married name and a find. It stays **open**: not counted, and the nil below is written with this cell named. If the Bribir marriage book of the 1900s is ever found, the marriage of 18 September 19.. is the thing to look for.

**What the register holds.** A printed Latin table, one page per image; entries in Latin, and from 1878 in Croatian in the same printed table; **numbering restarts at 1 each January.** The year begins on these images, from the readers' reports: 1865 about 101, 1866 on 115, 1867 on 132, 1868 on 143, 1869 on 155, 1870 on 172, 1871 on 192, 1872 on 210, 1873 on 227, 1874 on 243, 1875 on 258, 1876 on 271, 1877 on 289, 1878 on 300, 1879 on 313, 1880 on 325, 1881 on 343, 1882 on 356, 1883 on 363, 1884 on 375, 1885 on 385, 1886 on 394 (1858 to 1864 on images 4 to about 100). **Second exposures of one page:** images 224 and 225 (printed page 221), 279 and 280 (folio 275), 333, 334 and 335 (page 329, entry 117, September 1880, three times), 397 and 398 (page 391), 399 and 400. **The end:** image 405 is page 396 (31 December 1886, entry 170, a note by the canon-archdeacon Petar Car with a jubilee note); 406 is the end-of-roll card of roll 9 and the title card of the next item («rođenih 1856–1886»); 407 «Kraj, svitak 9, nastavak svitak 10»; 408 a resolution target; 409 and 411 «END OF ROLL» cards; 410 a blank grey frame. The card says 1856, and the entries I have summaries for begin in January 1858; I have not resolved that. Roll 10 holds the marriage and death books of 1858–1900 and 1858–1898 (told above).

**The Kaliman house of Kićeri (a cell I zoomed, and the readers' zooms; settled, not counted).** Image 271, right, entry 1 (4 January 1876): the godparents «*Georgius Kalli-* | *man et Catharina*» (Kićeri 3) at level 13 — *Kaliman* across a line break, the baptiser of that entry being the cantor-canon *Antonius Kaliman*. The readers' own zooms of the family (images 54, 80, 92, 239 and 395) read *-lim-* and not *-lan-*. **Kaliman / Kalliman is a Bribir house of Kićeri; it is not Kalanj** (the same settling as in the roll 10 section above). **Kalafatić** (the commonest surname in the book) is a different name and **not Kalanj**; **Kovačić** is **not Kovačina**.

**Cells left open (none counted, none excluded; read by readers at crop level, not opened by me beyond what is said above).** Image 39, right, entry 68: «Nicolaus & Ursula Kalinskahe(?)». Image 6, left, entries 28, 29 and 33. Image 28, entry 101: «Kalafat» with a *f* or *g*. Image 43, right: a pasted slip «Georg. Ban(?) Modrusiensis & … Fran. vid. Dfti Josephi». Image 73, right, entry 2: «Kalu?a». Image 96, left, entry 89: «Kallman». Image 120, right: «Ursula Kalimaj(?)». Image 125, right, entry 107: «Kathović (Kalković?)». Image 129, entry 142: «Kranjcevog(?)». Image 130, foot: «Kalimas / Kaliman». Image 136, left, entry 44: *Hallić / Kallić* (*H* or *K*). Image 138, entry 70: dashes. Image 145, right, entry 23: *Kali- / Keli-man*. Image 185, left, entry 134: *Kalinau / Kaliman*. Image 193, entry 15: under tape. Image 195: a *Kalafatić / Plovanić* mismatch. Image 198, right, entry 60. Image 203, left, entry 117. Image 214, left, entry 47: «?ovačić». Image 340, right, entry 179: a struck word «Kala- / Kalafatić(?)». Image 344, entry 27: *Kalic / Hallic*. Image 347, entry 55: *Ijali / Kali*. Image 355, right, entry 164: *Kalin / Kulin?*. Image 358, left, entries 36–39. Image 359, left, entry 47. Image 364, left, entry 24: «Kalim…». Image 378, right, the margin by entry 61 (10 September 1884): a note «krsni list zamjenjen u Dragi(?) … RIJEKA …». Image 382, left, entry 132. Image 389, left, entry 77: «Kelak / Kolak», read by a reader as not *Kalaj*. Image 391, entry 120: *Kalman*. Image 394, entry 4: a margin «Frank[…]». Image 395, entry 28: *Kaliman*. Torn strips hide foot rows on images 384–389. **None of these is a Defranceschi or a Kalanj as read; each is a cell that was not settled at crop level and that I did not open.**

**Clergy.** The baptisers are the canons and priests of Bribir: **Josip Mrzljak (*Josephus*)**, canon and parish priest, written Merzljak, Mrzljak and Merkljak in the cells (the readers record his death on 30 November 1882); *Josephus Sandri(ć)*, cooperator, 1869–1871; **Antonius Kaliman**, cantor-canon; Martinčić; Georg Csor; Andreas Canjuga; Petar Car, canon-archdeacon (to about 1887); and Mihovil Gerčević, Marko Rakuša, Boro Mihovilić, Mihovil Pekić, Josip Polić, Konrad Modrčin, Luka Malinarić, Ambroz Brozović, Anton Colessi, Juraj Borovčak and Ivan Šimac. **Every *Josephus* is a priest of the parish, and none is a Defranceschi.** Two foot cells where the surname of a *Josephus* did not come clear — «*Josephus Mar… Canon. parochus*» (image 34, right) and «*Josephus Merk-?*» (image 117, right) — begin neither *De-* nor *Fran-*.

**Places in cells (not counted).** **Dragaljin / Dragasin are hamlets of Bribir and are not read as the Draga of Bakar.** Bakar appears as «*Capitanei Navalis Buccarani*» (a godparent's father, image 163, right, entry 90, 27 September 1869), Kostrena on image 125 and Jelenje on image 195. Later hands name Rijeka, Trsat, Bakar and Draga in the Observationes in the twentieth century (Trsat 1910 on image 130, 1937 on image 227 and 1914 on image 395; Bakar 1943 on image 278 and 1947 on image 325; «*krstni list sa vjenčanja u Dragi* 27/? 1908» on image 253, right, entry 148, and the note on image 378 above); these are certificates and marriages of Bribir people elsewhere, not entries of the families. **A place in a cell is a place and nothing more.**

**Near-names, none of them counted.** Kalafatić (very many); Kaliman / Kalliman / Kalman / Kalinan (Kićeri; the cantor Antonius); Kovačić; Kranjčević; Fančić / Tančić; Frankovic (1869); Franić (1880); Hranjčić; Hallić; Kabalin (1872, 1883, 1885); Kelak / Kolak; Frezza «*Fluminensis*». **Structure notes from the readers:** numbering drifts or doubles on images 164, 173, 238, 285, 373 and 382; a struck 1872 slot after entry 198 on image 257; a cancelled Croatian entry of 1887 on image 171; a bishop's visitation note (Georgius Posilović, 12 October 1881) on image 351; entries 92 and 93 written 1882 and 1883 on image 399.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** Every cell at crop magnification except the Kaliman cell and the Pipinić note zoomed above; every cell named as open; the foot rows hidden by torn strips; the pasted slips and tipped-in notes; the margin hands; the entry numbers were not compared across image boundaries. The readers' full per-image reports for images 0–131 did not survive a restart of the machine; what is told for those images is each reader's hand-back summary. **This is a reader pass over every image and not a walk.** Terms typed to the readers: Defranci, Defranca, Defrancesco, Defranceschi, Defrancesci, Defrančeski, De Franceschi, de Franceschi, Defranceski, De Franceski, Defrancheski, Franceski, De Francesco, di Franceschi, Franceschi; Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich; Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Callajn, Kallanij, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalay, Kalan, Kalagn, Kalaj, Calan, Calagn, Callain, Callein, Kallein, Kalagnia, Kalianj, Callayn, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalayn. The Atlas `cover` run exits 0 for Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj.

rows_retired.lab: The join: Anna Kalanj, born 3 January 1864
rows_retired.text: Entry 2 of 1864 in the baptismal register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica: «Anna, legitima — Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» — at «Kljenovica N° 22». Godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. She married Josip Defranceschi, the stonecutter's son who brought this archive's line down from Gračišće to the coast, and she is generation four of the direct line. (doc — the plate is held here.)

rows_retired.lab: ⚠ «Rijenovica» does not exist, and the mistake hid a fact
rows_retired.text: Until today this archive read that place as «Rijenovica house 22» and said so in fifteen files, including the pedigree's own wall note. There is no Rijenovica: the word returns zero hits in this archive's Croatian gazetteer. The register says KLJENOVICA — the older spelling of Klenovica — and the Blažević Archive has read it correctly all along. What the misreading concealed: this site's Crikvenica page already says «House 22 is somewhere in this line of roofs — Anton Rudolf Defranceski was born in it on 20 January 1890.» Anna was born in the SAME HOUSE twenty-six years earlier. The archive held «house 22» at both ends and never joined them. The correction is on /corrections/.

rows_retired.lab: ⚠ And the entry says where they came from: BRINJE
rows_retired.text: «Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» — country people of the parish of Brinje. No file of this archive carried that phrase, and it is the most important thing in the entry: the Kalanj were not coastal people. Brinje is inland, up behind the Velebit gap, and they had come down to Klenovica on the shore. The Blažević Archive calls Brinje «the single largest hole in this family» and records that «not one page of its register has been opened». So both archives now stand at the same closed door, and this page exists partly to say so.

rows_retired.lab: The oldest open question here is a Kalanj question
rows_retired.text: The registers name ANA KALANJ in all four Crikvenica baptismal entries of her children. The family's own genealogy gives Josip a wife ANA GRUBIŠIĆ, 19 September 1863 – 28 May 1936, and that is the name cut on the Crikvenica gravestone. The registers govern and the stone is unexplained — and the stone no longer exists, because the plot was sold and the monument taken apart, so the photograph of it is now the only record. This is why Anna's page carries no death date: the only date on offer belongs to a name this archive cannot yet reconcile with hers.

rows_retired.lab: The stones — eleven of them, and a sibling set taking shape
rows_retired.text: Eleven Kalanj monuments have now been photographed in the cemeteries of Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica and are held here as plates. ⚠ AND FOUR OF THEM CLUSTER AROUND ANNA'S OWN GENERATION. LUKA KALANJ 1859–1944 and KATA 1860–1942 on a ledger slab; and ROZALIJA KALANJ 1865–1943, whose first digit is damaged and was read at 5×. Anna was born in 1864. So there are Kalanj born in 1859, 1860, 1864 and 1865 in one small stretch of the Vinodol — and ROZALIJA IS THE NAME OF ANNA'S OWN MOTHER, Rosalia née Perković, which is exactly what a daughter would be called. A sibling set is the obvious reading: Josip Kalanj and Rosalia's children, with the second daughter named for her mother. ⚠ IT IS STILL A GUESS. No stone here names a father, and this archive has spent the day learning what proximity is worth without a document. The test is cheap and specific: THE LEDENICE BAPTISMS OF 1855–1870, where Anna's own entry (number 2 of 1864) already sits, and where her brothers and sisters would sit within a few pages of her. (open, and the most tractable question on this page.) The other stones: Albert 1895–1945 with five of his household; Petar 1913–1971 and Vera 1917–2011 with the infant Milan 1943–1944; Mate 1928–1992; Franjo 1933–2004; a joint Kalanj–Rebrović stone; Vinko 1901–1961 and Paulina 1904–1984; Josip 1950–1983 with Franjo 1909–1991 and Zora 1923–1999; Tomislav 1935–2006; Judita 1934–2012 with Marijan 1931–2019; and Rozalija's own, with Anton 1897–1977, Marija 1898–1989 and Milan 1927–2006. ⚠ And one more, which carries something none of the others do: OBITELJ KALANJ — MARTIN 1905–1988 and MARTINA 1913–1995, two porcelain ovals, a stone cross standing in the gravel above — and propped against the plot, A PINK STONE PLAQUE CUT WITH THE CROATIAN CHEQUY SHIELD, the šahovnica. It is the only national emblem on any stone in this whole set of photographs, and it is worth recording as such and nothing more: a family put it there, and when or why is not on the stone. Two stones could not be stored because they reached this archive inline rather than as files — that one, and LOVRO 1906–1965 with Ana, Ivan and Marijan. They want re-sending if they are to be kept.

rows_retired.lab: Where this page stops, and why
rows_retired.text: The Kalanj genealogy proper — 215 published people, earliest birth 1734, running through Klenovica and Povile — is kept in The Blažević Archive, and is not rebuilt here. That boundary is right, and it had one cost that this page is the answer to: while each archive read only its own page, the two of them held one baptism and disagreed about the village for months. What belongs HERE is the join, the evidence photographed on this side, and the disagreements between the two. What belongs THERE is the family.
